180.s:
vyāsa uvāca
namaskṛtvā sureśāya viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave
puruṣāya purāṇāya śāśvatāyāvyayāya ca //
180.d:
व्यास उवाच
नमस्कृत्वा सुरेशाय विष्णवे प्रभविष्णवे
पुरुषाय पुराणाय शाश्वतायाव्ययाय च ॥
180.m: Vyāsa said: / Having bowed to the lord of the gods, Viṣṇu the powerful ruler, / the ancient puruṣa, the constant and imperishable,

180.s:
caturvyūhātmane tasmai nirguṇāya guṇāya ca
variṣṭhāya gariṣṭhāya vareṇyāyāmitāya ca //
180.d:
चतुर्व्यूहात्मने तस्मै निर्गुणाय गुणाय च
वरिष्ठाय गरिष्ठाय वरेण्यायामिताय च ॥
180.m: to him who possesses the nature of the four manifestations, devoid of qualities and endowed with qualities, / the highest, the weightiest, the most worthy of choice, and the boundless,

180.s:
yajñāṅgāyākhilāṅgāya devādyair īpsitāya ca
yasmād aṇutaraṃ nāsti yasmān nāsti bṛhattaram //
180.d:
यज्ञाङ्गायाखिलाङ्गाय देवाद्यैर् ईप्सिताय च
यस्माद् अणुतरं नास्ति यस्मान् नास्ति बृहत्तरम् ॥
180.m: the limb of the sacrifice, possessing all limbs, sought by the gods and others, / than whom there is nothing smaller, than whom there is nothing greater,

180.s:
yena viśvam idaṃ vyāptam ajena sacarācaram
āvirbhāvatirobhāvadṛṣṭādṛṣṭavilakṣaṇam //
180.d:
येन विश्वम् इदं व्याप्तम् अजेन सचराचरम्
आविर्भावतिरोभावदृष्टादृष्टविलक्षणम् ॥
180.m: by whom this whole universe, moving and unmoving, is pervaded, the unborn one, / distinct from manifestation and disappearance, from the seen and unseen,

180.s:
vadanti yat sṛṣṭam iti tathaivāpy upasaṃhṛtam
brahmaṇe cādidevāya namaskṛtya samādhinā //
180.d:
वदन्ति यत् सृष्टम् इति तथैवाप्य् उपसंहृतम्
ब्रह्मणे चादिदेवाय नमस्कृत्य समाधिना ॥
180.m: which they declare to be created and likewise withdrawn— / and having bowed in meditation to the primeval god, to Brahman,

180.s:
avikārāya śuddhāya nityāya paramātmane
sadaikarūparūpāya jiṣṇave viṣṇave namaḥ //
180.d:
अविकाराय शुद्धाय नित्याय परमात्मने
सदैकरूपरूपाय जिष्णवे विष्णवे नमः ॥
180.m: to the changeless, pure, eternal supreme self, / whose form is ever of one nature, to the victorious Viṣṇu, salutation!

180.s:
namo hiraṇyagarbhāya haraye śaṃkarāya ca
vāsudevāya tārāya sargasthityantakāriṇe //
180.d:
नमो हिरण्यगर्भाय हरये शंकराय च
वासुदेवाय ताराय सर्गस्थित्यन्तकारिणे ॥
180.m: Salutation to Hiraṇyagarbha, to Hari and to Śaṅkara, / to Vāsudeva the savior, the agent of primary creation, preservation, and dissolution,

180.s:
ekānekasvarūpāya sthūlasūkṣmātmane namaḥ
avyaktavyaktabhūtāya viṣṇave muktihetave //
180.d:
एकानेकस्वरूपाय स्थूलसूक्ष्मात्मने नमः
अव्यक्तव्यक्तभूताय विष्णवे मुक्तिहेतवे ॥
180.m: whose nature is one and manifold, whose self is gross and subtle, / who is unmanifest and manifest, to Viṣṇu, the cause of liberation!

180.s:
sargasthitivināśānāṃ jagato yo jaganmayaḥ
mūlabhūto namas tasmai viṣṇave paramātmane //
180.d:
सर्गस्थितिविनाशानां जगतो यो जगन्मयः
मूलभूतो नमस् तस्मै विष्णवे परमात्मने ॥
180.m: Salutation to that Viṣṇu, the supreme self, who consists of the universe, / the foundational source of the universe’s primary creation, preservation, and destruction!

180.s:
ādhārabhūtaṃ viśvasyāpy aṇīyāṃsam aṇīyasām
praṇamya sarvabhūtastham acyutaṃ puruṣottamam //
180.d:
आधारभूतं विश्वस्याप्य् अणीयांसम् अणीयसाम्
प्रणम्य सर्वभूतस्थम् अच्युतं पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
180.m: Having bowed to the foundation of the universe, the subtlest of the subtle, / abiding in all beings, the infallible Puruṣottama,

180.s:
jñānasvarūpam atyantaṃ nirmalaṃ paramārthataḥ
tam evārthasvarūpeṇa bhrāntidarśanataḥ sthitam //
180.d:
ज्ञानस्वरूपम् अत्यन्तं निर्मलं परमार्थतः
तम् एवार्थस्वरूपेण भ्रान्तिदर्शनतः स्थितम् ॥
180.m: whose nature is knowledge, completely stainless in ultimate reality, / who yet abides in the form of worldly objects through illusory perception,

180.s:
viṣṇuṃ grasiṣṇuṃ viśvasya sthitisarge tathā prabhum
anādiṃ jagatām īśam ajam akṣayam avyayam //
180.d:
विष्णुं ग्रसिष्णुं विश्वस्य स्थितिसर्गे तथा प्रभुम्
अनादिं जगताम् ईशम् अजम् अक्षयम् अव्ययम् ॥
180.m: to Viṣṇu, the consumer of the universe, and likewise the lord of preservation and primary creation, / without beginning, the lord of worlds, unborn, undecaying, imperishable,

180.s:
kathayāmi yathā pūrvaṃ yakṣādyair munisattamaiḥ
pṛṣṭaḥ provāca bhagavān abjayoniḥ pitāmahaḥ //
180.d:
कथयामि यथा पूर्वं यक्षाद्यैर् मुनिसत्तमैः
पृष्टः प्रोवाच भगवान् अब्जयोनिः पितामहः ॥
180.m: I shall relate what the blessed grandfather born from the lotus, / when asked in former times by the yakṣas and best of sages, declared,

180.s:
ṛksāmāny udgiran vaktrair yaḥ punāti jagattrayam
praṇipatya tatheśānam ekārṇavavinirgatam //
180.d:
ऋक्सामान्य् उद्गिरन् वक्त्रैर् यः पुनाति जगत्त्रयम्
प्रणिपत्य तथेशानम् एकार्णवविनिर्गतम् ॥
180.m: he who purifies the three worlds by uttering the Ṛg and Sāma verses through his mouths, / having bowed to the Lord who emerged from the single primeval ocean,

180.s:
yasyāsuragaṇā yajñān vilumpanti na yājinām
pravakṣyāmi mataṃ kṛtsnaṃ brahmaṇo 'vyaktajanmanaḥ //
180.d:
यस्यासुरगणा यज्ञान् विलुम्पन्ति न याजिनाम्
प्रवक्ष्यामि मतं कृत्स्नं ब्रह्मणो ऽव्यक्तजन्मनः ॥
180.m: whose sacrifices of the sacrificers the host of asuras do not plunder: / I shall expound the complete doctrine of Brahmā, whose birth is from the unmanifest,

180.s:
yena sṛṣṭiṃ samuddiśya dharmādyāḥ prakaṭīkṛtāḥ
āpo nārā iti proktā munibhis tattvadarśibhiḥ //
180.d:
येन सृष्टिं समुद्दिश्य धर्माद्याः प्रकटीकृताः
आपो नारा इति प्रोक्ता मुनिभिस् तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
180.m: by whom dharma and the rest were manifested for the purpose of creation. / The waters are called nārāḥ by the sages who see the truth;

180.s:
ayanaṃ tasya tāḥ pūrvaṃ tena nārāyaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ
sa devo bhagavān sarvaṃ vyāpya nārāyaṇo vibhuḥ //
180.d:
अयनं तस्य ताः पूर्वं तेन नारायणः स्मृतः
स देवो भगवान् सर्वं व्याप्य नारायणो विभुः ॥
180.m: they were his abode in the beginning, and therefore he is remembered as Nārāyaṇa. / That divine, blessed Nārāyaṇa, the all-pervading lord,

180.s:
caturdhā saṃsthito brahmā saguṇo nirguṇas tathā
ekā mūrtir anuddeśyā śuklāṃ paśyanti tāṃ budhāḥ //
180.d:
चतुर्धा संस्थितो ब्रह्मा सगुणो निर्गुणस् तथा
एका मूर्तिर् अनुद्देश्या शुक्लां पश्यन्ति तां बुधाः ॥
180.m: abides fourfold, Brahmā, endowed with qualities and likewise devoid of qualities. / One form is undefinable; the wise perceive it as white.

180.s:
jvālāmālāvanaddhāṅgī niṣṭhā sā yogināṃ parā
dūrasthā cāntikasthā ca vijñeyā sā guṇātigā //
180.d:
ज्वालामालावनद्धाङ्गी निष्ठा सा योगिनां परा
दूरस्था चान्तिकस्था च विज्ञेया सा गुणातिगा ॥
180.m: With limbs encircled by garlands of flames, it is the supreme goal of yogins; / distant and near, it is to be known as transcending the qualities.

180.s:
vāsudevābhidhānāsau nirmamatvena dṛśyate
rūpavarṇādayas tasyā na bhāvāḥ kalpanāmayāḥ //
180.d:
वासुदेवाभिधानासौ निर्ममत्वेन दृश्यते
रूपवर्णादयस् तस्या न भावाः कल्पनामयाः ॥
180.m: Bearing the name Vāsudeva, it is seen through egolessness; / its forms, colors, and other attributes are not fabricated by imagination.

180.s:
āste ca sā sadā śuddhā supratiṣṭhaikarūpiṇī
dvitīyā pṛthivīṃ mūrdhnā śeṣākhyā dhārayaty adhaḥ //
180.d:
आस्ते च सा सदा शुद्धा सुप्रतिष्ठैकरूपिणी
द्वितीया पृथिवीं मूर्ध्ना शेषाख्या धारयत्य् अधः ॥
180.m: And it rests ever pure, well-established, of a single form. / The second, named Śeṣa, supports the earth below with its head;

180.s:
tāmasī sā samākhyātā tiryaktvaṃ samupāgatā
tṛtīyā karma kurute prajāpālanatatparā //
180.d:
तामसी सा समाख्याता तिर्यक्त्वं समुपागता
तृतीया कर्म कुरुते प्रजापालनतत्परा ॥
180.m: that form is declared to consist of darkness, having attained animal nature. / The third performs action, devoted to protecting creatures;

180.s:
sattvodriktā tu sā jñeyā dharmasaṃsthānakāriṇī
caturthī jalamadhyasthā śete pannagatalpagā //
180.d:
सत्त्वोद्रिक्ता तु सा ज्ञेया धर्मसंस्थानकारिणी
चतुर्थी जलमध्यस्था शेते पन्नगतल्पगा ॥
180.m: it is to be known as abounding in purity, establishing dharma. / The fourth abides in the midst of the waters, resting on a serpent couch;

180.s:
rajas tasyā guṇaḥ sargaṃ sā karoti sadaiva hi
yā tṛtīyā harer mūrtiḥ prajāpālanatatparā //
180.d:
रजस् तस्या गुणः सर्गं सा करोति सदैव हि
या तृतीया हरेर् मूर्तिः प्रजापालनतत्परा ॥
180.m: its quality is passion; it performs primary creation at all times. / As for that third form of Hari, devoted to protecting creatures—

180.s:
sā tu dharmavyavasthānaṃ karoti niyataṃ bhuvi
proddhatān asurān hanti dharmavyucchittikāriṇaḥ //
180.d:
सा तु धर्मव्यवस्थानं करोति नियतं भुवि
प्रोद्धतान् असुरान् हन्ति धर्मव्युच्छित्तिकारिणः ॥
180.m: That [form], indeed, constantly establishes dharma on earth; / it slays the arrogant asuras who cause the destruction of dharma.

180.s:
pāti devān sagandharvān dharmarakṣāparāyaṇān
yadā yadā ca dharmasya glāniḥ samupajāyate //
180.d:
पाति देवान् सगन्धर्वान् धर्मरक्षापरायणान्
यदा यदा च धर्मस्य ग्लानिः समुपजायते ॥
180.m: It protects the gods along with the gandharvas, who are dedicated to the preservation of dharma. / And whenever there arises a decline of dharma,

180.s:
abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjaty asau
bhūtvā purā varāheṇa tuṇḍenāpo nirasya ca //
180.d:
अभ्युत्थानम् अधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजत्य् असौ
भूत्वा पुरा वराहेण तुण्डेनापो निरस्य च ॥
180.m: and an ascendance of adharma, then it creates itself. / Long ago, having become a boar and cast aside the waters with his snout,

180.s:
ekayā daṃṣṭrayotkhātā nalinīva vasuṃdharā
kṛtvā nṛsiṃharūpaṃ ca hiraṇyakaśipur hataḥ //
180.d:
एकया दंष्ट्रयोत्खाता नलिनीव वसुंधरा
कृत्वा नृसिंहरूपं च हिरण्यकशिपुर् हतः ॥
180.m: the earth was dug up with a single tusk, like a lotus. / And having assumed the form of the Man-Lion, Hiraṇyakaśipu was slain,

180.s:
vipracittimukhāś cānye dānavā vinipātitāḥ
vāmanaṃ rūpam āsthāya baliṃ saṃyamya māyayā //
180.d:
विप्रचित्तिमुखाश् चान्ये दानवा विनिपातिताः
वामनं रूपम् आस्थाय बलिं संयम्य मायया ॥
180.m: and other dānavas, headed by Vipracitti, were struck down. / Assuming the Dwarf form, having restrained Bali by illusory power,

180.s:
trailokyaṃ krāntavān eva vinirjitya diteḥ sutān
bhṛgor vaṃśe samutpanno jāmadagnyaḥ pratāpavān //
180.d:
त्रैलोक्यं क्रान्तवान् एव विनिर्जित्य दितेः सुतान्
भृगोर् वंशे समुत्पन्नो जामदग्न्यः प्रतापवान् ॥
180.m: he indeed traversed the three worlds, having completely conquered the sons of Diti. / Arising in the lineage of Bhṛgu, the mighty son of Jamadagni,

180.s:
jaghāna kṣatriyān rāmaḥ pitur vadham anusmaran
tathātritanayo bhūtvā dattātreyaḥ pratāpavān //
180.d:
जघान क्षत्रियान् रामः पितुर् वधम् अनुस्मरन्
तथात्रितनयो भूत्वा दत्तात्रेयः प्रतापवान् ॥
180.m: Rāma, struck down the kṣatriyas, remembering the murder of his father. / Likewise, having become Dattātreya, the mighty son of Atri,

180.s:
yogam aṣṭāṅgam ācakhyāv alarkāya mahātmane
rāmo dāśarathir bhūtvā sa tu devaḥ pratāpavān //
180.d:
योगम् अष्टाङ्गम् आचख्याव् अलर्काय महात्मने
रामो दाशरथिर् भूत्वा स तु देवः प्रतापवान् ॥
180.m: he explained the eight-limbed yoga to the great-souled Alarka. / Having become Rāma, son of Daśaratha, that mighty god,

180.s:
jaghāna rāvaṇaṃ saṃkhye trailokyasya bhayaṃkaram
yadā caikārṇave supto devadevo jagatpatiḥ //
180.d:
जघान रावणं संख्ये त्रैलोक्यस्य भयंकरम्
यदा चैकार्णवे सुप्तो देवदेवो जगत्पतिः ॥
180.m: slew in battle Rāvaṇa, who caused terror to the three worlds. / And when the lord of the world, the god of gods, was asleep in the single ocean,

180.s:
sahasrayugaparyantaṃ nāgaparyaṅkago vibhuḥ
yoganidrāṃ samāsthāya sve mahimni vyavasthitaḥ //
180.d:
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तं नागपर्यङ्कगो विभुः
योगनिद्रां समास्थाय स्वे महिम्नि व्यवस्थितः ॥
180.m: reclining on the serpent couch for the span of a thousand yugas, the all-pervading lord, / having recourse to yogic sleep, remaining established in his own greatness,

180.s:
trailokyam udare kṛtvā jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam
janalokagataiḥ siddhaiḥ stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ //
180.d:
त्रैलोक्यम् उदरे कृत्वा जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्
जनलोकगतैः सिद्धैः स्तूयमानो महर्षिभिः ॥
180.m: having placed the three worlds—the world of moving and unmoving things—within his belly, / being praised by the great sages and the siddhas who had gone to Janaloka,

180.s:
tasya nābhau samutpannaṃ padmaṃ dikpattramaṇḍitam
marutkiñjalkasaṃyuktaṃ gṛhaṃ paitāmahaṃ varam //
180.d:
तस्य नाभौ समुत्पन्नं पद्मं दिक्पत्त्रमण्डितम्
मरुत्किञ्जल्कसंयुक्तं गृहं पैतामहं वरम् ॥
180.m: there arose from his navel a lotus adorned with the directions as its petals / and possessing the winds as its filaments, the excellent ancestral abode,

180.s:
yatra brahmā samutpanno devadevaś caturmukhaḥ
tadā karṇamalodbhūtau dānavau madhukaiṭabhau //
180.d:
यत्र ब्रह्मा समुत्पन्नो देवदेवश् चतुर्मुखः
तदा कर्णमलोद्भूतौ दानवौ मधुकैटभौ ॥
180.m: where Brahmā, the four-faced god of gods, arose. / Then the two dānavas, Madhu and Kaiṭabha, born from the wax of his ears,

180.s:
mahābalau mahāvīryau brahmāṇaṃ hantum udyatau
jaghāna tau durādharṣau utthāya śayanodadheḥ //
180.d:
महाबलौ महावीर्यौ ब्रह्माणं हन्तुम् उद्यतौ
जघान तौ दुराधर्षौ उत्थाय शयनोदधेः ॥
180.m: of great strength and great prowess, strove to slay Brahmā. / Rising from his ocean bed, he slew those two invincible ones.

180.s:
evamādīṃs tathaivānyān asaṃkhyātum ihotsahe
avatāro hy ajasyeha māthuraḥ sāṃpratas tv ayam //
180.d:
एवमादींस् तथैवान्यान् असंख्यातुम् इहोत्सहे
अवतारो ह्य् अजस्येह माथुरः सांप्रतस् त्व् अयम् ॥
180.m: I am unable to enumerate these and still other [manifestations] in this world. / For this present descent of the unborn one is in Mathurā.

180.s:
iti sā sāttvikī mūrtir avatāraṃ karoti ca
pradyumneti samākhyātā rakṣākarmaṇy avasthitā //
180.d:
इति सा सात्त्विकी मूर्तिर् अवतारं करोति च
प्रद्युम्नेति समाख्याता रक्षाकर्मण्य् अवस्थिता ॥
180.m: Thus that sāttvika form descends, / known as Pradyumna, engaged in the work of protection.

180.s:
devatve 'tha manuṣyatve tiryagyonau ca saṃsthitā
gṛhṇāti tatsvabhāvaś ca vāsudevecchayā sadā //
180.d:
देवत्वे ऽथ मनुष्यत्वे तिर्यग्योनौ च संस्थिता
गृह्णाति तत्स्वभावश् च वासुदेवेच्छया सदा ॥
180.m: Stationed in godhead, humanity, or the womb of an animal, / it always adopts that nature by the will of Vāsudeva.

180.s:
dadāty abhimatān kāmān pūjitā sā dvijottamāḥ
evaṃ mayā samākhyātaḥ kṛtakṛtyo 'pi yaḥ prabhuḥ
mānuṣatvaṃ gato viṣṇuḥ śṛṇudhvaṃ cottaraṃ punaḥ //
180.d:
ददात्य् अभिमतान् कामान् पूजिता सा द्विजोत्तमाः
एवं मया समाख्यातः कृतकृत्यो ऽपि यः प्रभुः
मानुषत्वं गतो विष्णुः शृणुध्वं चोत्तरं पुनः ॥
180.m: When worshipped, it grants desired wishes, O best of the twice-born. / Thus has been recounted by me how Viṣṇu, the lord who has accomplished everything, entered the human state; now hear what follows.

181.s:
vyāsa uvāca
śṛṇudhvaṃ muniśārdūlāḥ pravakṣyāmi samāsataḥ
avatāraṃ hareś cātra bhārāvataraṇecchayā //
181.d:
व्यास उवाच
शृणुध्वं मुनिशार्दूलाः प्रवक्ष्यामि समासतः
अवतारं हरेश् चात्र भारावतरणेच्छया ॥
181.m: Vyāsa said: / Listen, O tigers among sages; I shall explain in brief / the descent of Hari here, through his desire to relieve the burden.

181.s:
yadā yadā tv adharmasya vṛddhir bhavati bho dvijāḥ
dharmaś ca hrāsam abhyeti tadā devo janārdanaḥ //
181.d:
यदा यदा त्व् अधर्मस्य वृद्धिर् भवति भो द्विजाः
धर्मश् च ह्रासम् अभ्येति तदा देवो जनार्दनः ॥
181.m: Whenever an increase of adharma occurs, O twice-born, / and dharma undergoes decline, then the divine Janārdana

181.s:
avatāraṃ karoty atra dvidhā kṛtvātmanas tanum
sādhūnāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya dharmasaṃsthāpanāya ca //
181.d:
अवतारं करोत्य् अत्र द्विधा कृत्वात्मनस् तनुम्
साधूनां रक्षणार्थाय धर्मसंस्थापनाय च ॥
181.m: makes a descent here, dividing his own body into two, / for the protection of the good and the establishment of dharma,

181.s:
duṣṭānāṃ nigrahārthāya anyeṣāṃ ca suradviṣām
prajānāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya jāyate 'sau yuge yuge //
181.d:
दुष्टानां निग्रहार्थाय अन्येषां च सुरद्विषाम्
प्रजानां रक्षणार्थाय जायते ऽसौ युगे युगे ॥
181.m: for the restraint of the wicked and other enemies of the gods, / and for the protection of creatures, he is born age after age.

181.s:
purā kila mahī viprā bhūribhārāvapīḍitā
jagāma dharaṇī merau samāje tridivaukasām //
181.d:
पुरा किल मही विप्रा भूरिभारावपीडिता
जगाम धरणी मेरौ समाजे त्रिदिवौकसाम् ॥
181.m: Long ago, O twice-born, the earth, tormented by a heavy burden, / went to Mount Meru, to an assembly of the heaven-dwellers.

181.s:
sabrahmakān surān sarvān praṇipatyātha medinī
kathayām āsa tat sarvaṃ khedāt karuṇabhāṣiṇī //
181.d:
सब्रह्मकान् सुरान् सर्वान् प्रणिपत्याथ मेदिनी
कथयाम् आस तत् सर्वं खेदात् करुणभाषिणी ॥
181.m: Then the earth, bowing down to all the gods together with Brahmā, / speaking piteously out of sorrow, reported all that:

181.s:
dharaṇy uvāca
agniḥ suvarṇasya gurur gavāṃ sūryo 'paro guruḥ
mamāpy akhilalokānāṃ vandyo nārāyaṇo guruḥ //
181.d:
धरण्य् उवाच
अग्निः सुवर्णस्य गुरुर् गवां सूर्यो ऽपरो गुरुः
ममाप्य् अखिललोकानां वन्द्यो नारायणो गुरुः ॥
181.m: The Earth said: / Fire is the master of gold; the sun is the other master of cattle; / Nārāyaṇa, the master worthy of praise by all worlds, is my master as well.

181.s:
tatsāṃpratam ime daityāḥ kālanemipurogamāḥ
martyalokaṃ samāgamya bādhante 'harniśaṃ prajāḥ //
181.d:
तत्सांप्रतम् इमे दैत्याः कालनेमिपुरोगमाः
मर्त्यलोकं समागम्य बाधन्ते ऽहर्निशं प्रजाः ॥
181.m: Therefore now these daityas, led by Kālanemi, / having come to the mortal realm, harass the creatures day and night.

181.s:
kālanemir hato yo 'sau viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā
ugrasenasutaḥ kaṃsaḥ saṃbhūtaḥ sumahāsuraḥ //
181.d:
कालनेमिर् हतो यो ऽसौ विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना
उग्रसेनसुतः कंसः संभूतः सुमहासुरः ॥
181.m: That Kālanemi, who was slain by Viṣṇu the supreme lord, / has been born as Kaṃsa, the son of Ugrasena, a very great asura.

181.s:
ariṣṭo dhenukaḥ keśī pralambo narakas tathā
sundo 'suras tathātyugro bāṇaś cāpi baleḥ sutaḥ //
181.d:
अरिष्टो धेनुकः केशी प्रलम्बो नरकस् तथा
सुन्दो ऽसुरस् तथात्युग्रो बाणश् चापि बलेः सुतः ॥
181.m: Ariṣṭa, Dhenuka, Keśin, Pralamba, and Naraka, / Sunda, the exceedingly fierce asura, and Bāṇa the son of Bali,

181.s:
tathānye ca mahāvīryā nṛpāṇāṃ bhavaneṣu ye
samutpannā durātmānas tān na saṃkhyātum utsahe //
181.d:
तथान्ये च महावीर्या नृपाणां भवनेषु ये
समुत्पन्ना दुरात्मानस् तान् न संख्यातुम् उत्सहे ॥
181.m: and other evil-minded ones of great prowess who have been born / in the palaces of kings—I am unable to count them.

181.s:
akṣauhiṇyo hi bahulā divyamūrtidhṛtāḥ surāḥ
mahābalānāṃ dṛptānāṃ daityendrāṇāṃ mamopari //
181.d:
अक्षौहिण्यो हि बहुला दिव्यमूर्तिधृताः सुराः
महाबलानां दृप्तानां दैत्येन्द्राणां ममोपरि ॥
181.m: Indeed, numerous akṣauhiṇīs of the exceedingly mighty and arrogant / lords of daityas bearing divine forms are upon me, O gods.

181.s:
tadbhūribhārapīḍārtā na śaknomy amareśvarāḥ
vibhartum ātmānam aham iti vijñāpayāmi vaḥ //
181.d:
तद्भूरिभारपीडार्ता न शक्नोम्य् अमरेश्वराः
विभर्तुम् आत्मानम् अहम् इति विज्ञापयामि वः ॥
181.m: Afflicted by the pain of that heavy burden, I am not able / to bear myself, O lords of immortals; thus I make representation to you.

181.s:
kriyatāṃ tan mahābhāgā mama bhārāvatāraṇam
yathā rasātalaṃ nāhaṃ gaccheyam ativihvalā //
181.d:
क्रियतां तन् महाभागा मम भारावतारणम्
यथा रसातलं नाहं गच्छेयम् अतिविह्वला ॥
181.m: Therefore, O fortunate ones, let the removal of my burden be carried out, / so that, utterly bewildered, I may not sink into Rasātala.

181.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity ākarṇya dharāvākyam aśeṣais tridaśais tataḥ
bhuvo bhārāvatārārthaṃ brahmā prāha ca coditaḥ //
181.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् आकर्ण्य धरावाक्यम् अशेषैस् त्रिदशैस् ततः
भुवो भारावतारार्थं ब्रह्मा प्राह च चोदितः ॥
181.m: Vyāsa said: / Having heard the speech of the Earth, then Brahmā, / urged by all the thirty [gods] to remove the earth's burden, spoke:

181.s:
brahmovāca
yad āha vasudhā sarvaṃ satyam etad divaukasaḥ
ahaṃ bhavo bhavantaś ca sarvaṃ nārāyaṇātmakam //
181.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
यद् आह वसुधा सर्वं सत्यम् एतद् दिवौकसः
अहं भवो भवन्तश् च सर्वं नारायणात्मकम् ॥
181.m: Brahmā said: / All that the earth has said is true, O heaven-dwellers. / I, Bhava, and all of you have the nature of Nārāyaṇa.

181.s:
vibhūtayas tu yās tasya tāsām eva parasparam
ādhikyaṃ nyūnatā bādhyabādhakatvena vartate //
181.d:
विभूतयस् तु यास् तस्य तासाम् एव परस्परम्
आधिक्यं न्यूनता बाध्यबाधकत्वेन वर्तते ॥
181.m: Yet among his manifestations there exists mutual / superiority and inferiority, through the state of being oppressor and oppressed.

181.s:
tad āgacchata gacchāmaḥ kṣīrābdhes taṭam uttamam
tatrārādhya hariṃ tasmai sarvaṃ vijñāpayāma vai //
181.d:
तद् आगच्छत गच्छामः क्षीराब्धेस् तटम् उत्तमम्
तत्राराध्य हरिं तस्मै सर्वं विज्ञापयाम वै ॥
181.m: Therefore come, let us go to the excellent shore of the Ocean of Milk; / having propitiated Hari there, we shall make all this known to him.

181.s:
sarvadaiva jagatyarthe sa sarvātmā jaganmayaḥ
svalpāṃśenāvatīryorvyāṃ dharmasya kurute sthitim //
181.d:
सर्वदैव जगत्यर्थे स सर्वात्मा जगन्मयः
स्वल्पांशेनावतीर्योर्व्यां धर्मस्य कुरुते स्थितिम् ॥
181.m: Always indeed, for the sake of the world, that soul of all, consisting of the universe, / descending to earth with a small portion [of himself], brings about the preservation of dharma.

181.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktvā prayayau tatra saha devaiḥ pitāmahaḥ
samāhitamanā bhūtvā tuṣṭāva garuḍadhvajam //
181.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा प्रययौ तत्र सह देवैः पितामहः
समाहितमना भूत्वा तुष्टाव गरुडध्वजम् ॥
181.m: Vyāsa said: / Having spoken thus, the Grandfather set out there with the gods; / having concentrated his mind, he praised the one whose banner is Garuḍa:

181.s:
brahmovāca
namo namas te 'stu sahasramūrte
sahasrabāho bahuvaktrapāda
namo namas te jagataḥ pravṛtti
vināśasaṃsthānaparāprameya
181.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
नमो नमस् ते ऽस्तु सहस्रमूर्ते
सहस्रबाहो बहुवक्त्रपाद
नमो नमस् ते जगतः प्रवृत्ति
विनाशसंस्थानपराप्रमेय
181.m: Brahmā said: / Homage, homage be to you of a thousand forms, / of a thousand arms, many faces and feet! / Homage, homage be to you, the supreme and immeasurable cause / of the origination, destruction, and preservation of the universe!

181.s:
sūkṣmātisūkṣmaṃ ca bṛhatpramāṇaṃ
garīyasām apy atigauravātman
pradhānabuddhīndriyavākpradhāna
mūlāparātman bhagavan prasīda
181.d:
सूक्ष्मातिसूक्ष्मं च बृहत्प्रमाणं
गरीयसाम् अप्य् अतिगौरवात्मन्
प्रधानबुद्धीन्द्रियवाक्प्रधान
मूलापरात्मन् भगवन् प्रसीद
181.m: Subtlest of the subtle and of vast magnitude, / the soul of supreme weight among the weightiest, / supreme over pradhāna, intellect, sense-faculties, and speech, / the higher soul beyond the primal root, O Blessed One, be gracious!

181.s:
eṣā mahī deva mahīprasūtair
mahāsuraiḥ pīḍitaśailabandhā
parāyaṇaṃ tvāṃ jagatām upaiti
bhārāvatārārtham apārapāram
181.d:
एषा मही देव महीप्रसूतैर्
महासुरैः पीडितशैलबन्धा
परायणं त्वां जगताम् उपैति
भारावतारार्थम् अपारपारम्
181.m: This earth, O God, whose mountain-bindings are afflicted / by great asuras born on earth, / approaches you, the supreme refuge of the worlds, / the shore of the shoreless, for the lifting of her burden.

181.s:
ete vayaṃ vṛtraripus tathāyaṃ
nāsatyadasrau varuṇas tathaiṣaḥ
ime ca rudrā vasavaḥ sasūryāḥ
samīraṇāgnipramukhās tathānye
181.d:
एते वयं वृत्ररिपुस् तथायं
नासत्यदस्रौ वरुणस् तथैषः
इमे च रुद्रा वसवः ससूर्याः
समीरणाग्निप्रमुखास् तथान्ये
181.m: Here are we, and this foe of Vṛtra, / the Nāsatyas, and Varuṇa here, / and these Rudras, the Vasus together with the suns, / and others headed by the Wind and Fire,

181.s:
surāḥ samastāḥ suranātha kāryam
ebhir mayā yac ca tad īśa sarvam
ājñāpayājñāṃ pratipālayantas
tavaiva tiṣṭhāma sadāstadoṣāḥ
181.d:
सुराः समस्ताः सुरनाथ कार्यम्
एभिर् मया यच् च तद् ईश सर्वम्
आज्ञापयाज्ञां प्रतिपालयन्तस्
तवैव तिष्ठाम सदास्तदोषाः
181.m: all the gods, O Lord of gods! Whatever duty is to be done / by them and by me, O Lord, command all that! / Awaiting your command, / we stand as yours alone, ever freed from fault.

181.s:
vyāsa uvāca
evaṃ saṃstūyamānas tu bhagavān parameśvaraḥ
ujjahārātmanaḥ keśau sitakṛṣṇau dvijottamāḥ //
181.d:
व्यास उवाच
एवं संस्तूयमानस् तु भगवान् परमेश्वरः
उज्जहारात्मनः केशौ सितकृष्णौ द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
181.m: Vyāsa said: / While he was thus being praised, the Blessed One, the supreme lord, / plucked two hairs of his, one white and one black, O best of the twice-born,

181.s:
uvāca ca surān etau matkeśau vasudhātale
avatīrya bhuvo bhārakleśahāniṃ kariṣyataḥ //
181.d:
उवाच च सुरान् एतौ मत्केशौ वसुधातले
अवतीर्य भुवो भारक्लेशहानिं करिष्यतः ॥
181.m: and said to the gods: "These two hairs of mine, having descended / to the surface of the earth, will bring about the removal of the affliction of the earth's burden."

181.s:
surāś ca sakalāḥ svāṃśair avatīrya mahītale
kurvantu yuddham unmattaiḥ pūrvotpannair mahāsuraiḥ //
181.d:
सुराश् च सकलाः स्वांशैर् अवतीर्य महीतले
कुर्वन्तु युद्धम् उन्मत्तैः पूर्वोत्पन्नैर् महासुरैः ॥
181.m: And let all the gods descend to the earth with their portions / and wage war with the maddened, great asuras born of old.

181.s:
tataḥ kṣayam aśeṣās te daiteyā dharaṇītale
prayāsyanti na saṃdeho nānāyudhavicūrṇitāḥ //
181.d:
ततः क्षयम् अशेषास् ते दैतेया धरणीतले
प्रयास्यन्ति न संदेहो नानायुधविचूर्णिताः ॥
181.m: Then all those Daityas on the earth will without doubt go to destruction, / crushed to powder by diverse weapons.

181.s:
vasudevasya yā patnī devakī devatopamā
tasyā garbho 'ṣṭamo 'yaṃ tu matkeśo bhavitā surāḥ //
181.d:
वसुदेवस्य या पत्नी देवकी देवतोपमा
तस्या गर्भो ऽष्टमो ऽयं तु मत्केशो भविता सुराः ॥
181.m: This hair of mine, O gods, will become the eighth child / of Vasudeva’s godlike wife, Devakī.

181.s:
avatīrya ca tatrāyaṃ kaṃsaṃ ghātayitā bhuvi
kālanemisamudbhūtam ity uktvāntardadhe hariḥ //
181.d:
अवतीर्य च तत्रायं कंसं घातयिता भुवि
कालनेमिसमुद्भूतम् इत्य् उक्त्वान्तर्दधे हरिः ॥
181.m: And having descended there, this one will slay Kaṃsa on earth, / who is an incarnation of Kālanemi." Having spoken thus, Hari vanished.

181.s:
adṛśyāya tatas te 'pi praṇipatya mahātmane
merupṛṣṭhaṃ surā jagmur avateruś ca bhūtale //
181.d:
अदृश्याय ततस् ते ऽपि प्रणिपत्य महात्मने
मेरुपृष्ठं सुरा जग्मुर् अवतेरुश् च भूतले ॥
181.m: Then those gods also bowed to the invisible, great-souled one, / went to the summit of Mount Meru, and descended to the earth.

181.s:
kaṃsāya cāṣṭamo garbho devakyā dharaṇītale
bhaviṣyatīty ācacakṣe bhagavān nārado muniḥ //
181.d:
कंसाय चाष्टमो गर्भो देवक्या धरणीतले
भविष्यतीत्य् आचचक्षे भगवान् नारदो मुनिः ॥
181.m: And the venerable sage Nārada proclaimed to Kaṃsa: / "The eighth child of Devakī will be born on the earth [to slay you]."

181.s:
kaṃso 'pi tad upaśrutya nāradāt kupitas tataḥ
devakīṃ vasudevaṃ ca gṛhe guptāv adhārayat //
181.d:
कंसो ऽपि तद् उपश्रुत्य नारदात् कुपितस् ततः
देवकीं वसुदेवं च गृहे गुप्ताव् अधारयत् ॥
181.m: Hearing that from Nārada, Kaṃsa was angered then, / and kept Devakī and Vasudeva closely guarded in his house.

181.s:
jātaṃ jātaṃ ca kaṃsāya tenaivoktaṃ yathā purā
tathaiva vasudevo 'pi putram arpitavān dvijāḥ //
181.d:
जातं जातं च कंसाय तेनैवोक्तं यथा पुरा
तथैव वसुदेवो ऽपि पुत्रम् अर्पितवान् द्विजाः ॥
181.m: And as each son was born, Vasudeva, O twice-born ones, / offered him up to Kaṃsa just as he had promised of old.

181.s:
hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putrāḥ ṣaḍgarbhā iti viśrutāḥ
viṣṇuprayuktā tān nidrā kramād garbhe nyayojayat //
181.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोः पुत्राः षड्गर्भा इति विश्रुताः
विष्णुप्रयुक्ता तान् निद्रा क्रमाद् गर्भे न्ययोजयत् ॥
181.m: There were sons of Hiraṇyakaśipu known as the Six Embryos; / directed by Viṣṇu, Sleep placed them in her womb in succession.

181.s:
yoganidrā mahāmāyā vaiṣṇavī mohitaṃ yayā
avidyayā jagat sarvaṃ tām āha bhagavān hariḥ //
181.d:
योगनिद्रा महामाया वैष्णवी मोहितं यया
अविद्यया जगत् सर्वं ताम् आह भगवान् हरिः ॥
181.m: To that Yoganidrā, the great illusory power belonging to Viṣṇu, by whom through ignorance / the entire universe is deluded, the blessed lord Hari said:

181.s:
viṣṇur uvāca
gaccha nidre mamādeśāt pātālatalasaṃśrayān
ekaikaśyena ṣaḍgarbhān devakījaṭhare naya //
181.d:
विष्णुर् उवाच
गच्छ निद्रे ममादेशात् पातालतलसंश्रयान्
एकैकश्येन षड्गर्भान् देवकीजठरे नय ॥
181.m:
Viṣṇu said:
"Go, O Sleep, by my command, / and one by one bring the Six Embryos dwelling in the subterranean realm into Devakī's womb.

181.s:
hateṣu teṣu kaṃsena śeṣākhyo 'ṃśas tato 'naghaḥ
aṃśāṃśenodare tasyāḥ saptamaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati //
181.d:
हतेषु तेषु कंसेन शेषाख्यो ऽंशस् ततो ऽनघः
अंशांशेनोदरे तस्याः सप्तमः संभविष्यति ॥
181.m: When they are slain by Kaṃsa, the faultless portion known as Śeṣa / will then be born as the seventh from a fraction of my portion in her belly.

181.s:
gokule vasudevasya bhāryā vai rohiṇī sthitā
tasyāḥ prasūtisamaye garbho neyas tvayodaram //
181.d:
गोकुले वसुदेवस्य भार्या वै रोहिणी स्थिता
तस्याः प्रसूतिसमये गर्भो नेयस् त्वयोदरम् ॥
181.m: In Gokula resides Rohiṇī, the wife of Vasudeva; / at the time of her delivery, that embryo must be transferred by you into her womb.

181.s:
saptamo bhojarājasya bhayād rodhoparodhataḥ
devakyāḥ patito garbha iti loko vadiṣyati //
181.d:
सप्तमो भोजराजस्य भयाद् रोधोपरोधतः
देवक्याः पतितो गर्भ इति लोको वदिष्यति ॥
181.m: People in the world will say: 'Due to fear of the king of the Bhojas, / and because of her confinement, Devakī’s embryo miscarried.'

181.s:
garbhasaṃkarṣaṇāt so 'tha loke saṃkarṣaṇeti vai
saṃjñām avāpsyate vīraḥ śvetādriśikharopamaḥ //
181.d:
गर्भसंकर्षणात् सो ऽथ लोके संकर्षणेति वै
संज्ञाम् अवाप्स्यते वीरः श्वेताद्रिशिखरोपमः ॥
181.m: Because of that extraction from the womb, that hero resembling the peak of a white mountain / shall then indeed receive the name Saṃkarṣaṇa in the world.

181.s:
tato 'haṃ saṃbhaviṣyāmi devakījaṭhare śubhe
garbhe tvayā yaśodāyā gantavyam avilambitam //
181.d:
ततो ऽहं संभविष्यामि देवकीजठरे शुभे
गर्भे त्वया यशोदाया गन्तव्यम् अविलम्बितम् ॥
181.m: Then I will be born in Devakī's auspicious belly; / you must enter the womb of Yaśodā without delay.

181.s:
prāvṛṭkāle ca nabhasi kṛṣṇāṣṭamyām ahaṃ niśi
utpatsyāmi navamyāṃ ca prasūtiṃ tvam avāpsyasi //
181.d:
प्रावृट्काले च नभसि कृष्णाष्टम्याम् अहं निशि
उत्पत्स्यामि नवम्यां च प्रसूतिं त्वम् अवाप्स्यसि ॥
181.m: And in the rainy season, in the month of Nabhas, on the eighth day of the dark fortnight, at night / I will be born, and on the ninth day you will be born.

181.s:
yaśodāśayane māṃ tu devakyās tvām anindite
macchaktipreritamatir vasudevo nayiṣyati //
181.d:
यशोदाशयने मां तु देवक्यास् त्वाम् अनिन्दिते
मच्छक्तिप्रेरितमतिर् वसुदेवो नयिष्यति ॥
181.m: O blameless one, Vasudeva, his mind impelled by my power, / will carry me to Yaśodā’s bed, and you to Devakī’s.

181.s:
kaṃsaś ca tvām upādāya devi śailaśilātale
prakṣepsyaty antarikṣe ca tvaṃ sthānaṃ samavāpsyasi //
181.d:
कंसश् च त्वाम् उपादाय देवि शैलशिलातले
प्रक्षेप्स्यत्य् अन्तरिक्षे च त्वं स्थानं समवाप्स्यसि ॥
181.m: And Kaṃsa, taking hold of you, O goddess, will dash you / onto the surface of a rock, and you will obtain a place in the sky.

181.s:
tatas tvāṃ śatadhā śakraḥ praṇamya mama gauravāt
praṇipātānataśirā bhaginītve grahīṣyati //
181.d:
ततस् त्वां शतधा शक्रः प्रणम्य मम गौरवात्
प्रणिपातानतशिरा भगिनीत्वे ग्रहीष्यति ॥
181.m: Then Śakra, bowing down a hundred times out of respect for me, / with his head bent low in salutation, will accept you as his sister.

181.s:
tataḥ śumbhaniśumbhādīn hatvā daityān sahasraśaḥ
sthānair anekaiḥ pṛthivīm aśeṣāṃ maṇḍayiṣyasi //
181.d:
ततः शुम्भनिशुम्भादीन् हत्वा दैत्यान् सहस्रशः
स्थानैर् अनेकैः पृथिवीम् अशेषां मण्डयिष्यसि ॥
181.m: Then, having slain thousands of Daityas such as Śumbha and Niśumbha, / you will adorn the entire earth with many sacred places.

181.s:
tvaṃ bhūtiḥ saṃnatiḥ kīrtiḥ kāntir vai pṛthivī dhṛtiḥ
lajjā puṣṭir uṣā yā ca kācid anyā tvam eva sā //
181.d:
त्वं भूतिः संनतिः कीर्तिः कान्तिर् वै पृथिवी धृतिः
लज्जा पुष्टिर् उषा या च काचिद् अन्या त्वम् एव सा ॥
181.m: You are prosperity, modesty, renown, beauty, the earth itself, fortitude, / shame, nourishment, dawn, and whatever else exists—you alone are that.

181.s:
ye tvām āryeti durgeti vedagarbhe 'mbiketi ca
bhadreti bhadrakālīti kṣemyā kṣemaṃkarīti ca //
181.d:
ये त्वाम् आर्येति दुर्गेति वेदगर्भे ऽम्बिकेति च
भद्रेति भद्रकालीति क्षेम्या क्षेमंकरीति च ॥
181.m: Those who praise you with bodies bowed low, / morning and afternoon, [calling you] Āryā, Durgā, Vedagarbhā, Ambikā, / Bhadrā, Bhadrakālī, Kṣemyā, and Kṣemaṃkarī—

181.s:
prātaś caivāparāhṇe ca stoṣyanty ānamramūrtayaḥ
teṣāṃ hi vāñchitaṃ sarvaṃ matprasādād bhaviṣyati //
181.d:
प्रातश् चैवापराह्णे च स्तोष्यन्त्य् आनम्रमूर्तयः
तेषां हि वाञ्छितं सर्वं मत्प्रसादाद् भविष्यति ॥
181.m: all that they desire / will surely come to pass by my grace.

181.s:
surāmāṃsopahārais tu bhakṣyabhojyaiś ca pūjitā
nṛṇām aśeṣakāmāṃs tvaṃ prasannāyāṃ pradāsyasi //
181.d:
सुरामांसोपहारैस् तु भक्ष्यभोज्यैश् च पूजिता
नृणाम् अशेषकामांस् त्वं प्रसन्नायां प्रदास्यसि ॥
181.m: Worshipped with offerings of liquor and meat, and foods to chew and eat, / you, when pleased, will grant men all their desires.

181.s:
te sarve sarvadā bhadrā matprasādād asaṃśayam
asaṃdigdhaṃ bhaviṣyanti gaccha devi yathoditam //
181.d:
ते सर्वे सर्वदा भद्रा मत्प्रसादाद् असंशयम्
असंदिग्धं भविष्यन्ति गच्छ देवि यथोदितम् ॥
181.m: All of them will always have good fortune, without doubt, by my grace; / of this there is no question. Go, O goddess, as spoken."

182.s:
vyāsa uvāca
yathoktaṃ sā jagaddhātrī devadevena vai purā
ṣaḍgarbhagarbhavinyāsaṃ cakre cānyasya karṣaṇam //
182.d:
व्यास उवाच
यथोक्तं सा जगद्धात्री देवदेवेन वै पुरा
षड्गर्भगर्भविन्यासं चक्रे चान्यस्य कर्षणम् ॥
182.m:
Vyāsa said:
As previously instructed by the god of gods, that sustainer of the world / deposited the Six Embryos and extracted the other.

182.s:
saptame rohiṇīṃ prāpte garbhe garbhe tato hariḥ
lokatrayopakārāya devakyāḥ praviveśa vai //
182.d:
सप्तमे रोहिणीं प्राप्ते गर्भे गर्भे ततो हरिः
लोकत्रयोपकाराय देवक्याः प्रविवेश वै ॥
182.m: When the seventh embryo reached Rohiṇī, / Hari then indeed entered Devakī's womb for the welfare of the three worlds.

182.s:
yoganidrā yaśodāyās tasminn eva tato dine
saṃbhūtā jaṭhare tadvad yathoktaṃ parameṣṭhinā //
182.d:
योगनिद्रा यशोदायास् तस्मिन्न् एव ततो दिने
संभूता जठरे तद्वद् यथोक्तं परमेष्ठिना ॥
182.m: Then, on that very day, Yoganidrā was born in the womb / of Yaśodā, just as had been told by the supreme lord.

182.s:
tato grahagaṇaḥ samyak pracacāra divi dvijāḥ
viṣṇor aṃśe mahīṃ yāta ṛtavo 'py abhavañ śubhāḥ //
182.d:
ततो ग्रहगणः सम्यक् प्रचचार दिवि द्विजाः
विष्णोर् अंशे महीं यात ऋतवो ऽप्य् अभवञ् शुभाः ॥
182.m: Then the planetary host moved favorably in the sky, O twice-born ones; / when Viṣṇu's portion came to earth, the seasons also became auspicious.

182.s:
notsehe devakīṃ draṣṭuṃ kaścid apy atitejasā
jājvalyamānāṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā manāṃsi kṣobham āyayuḥ //
182.d:
नोत्सेहे देवकीं द्रष्टुं कश्चिद् अप्य् अतितेजसा
जाज्वल्यमानां तां दृष्ट्वा मनांसि क्षोभम् आययुः ॥
182.m: No one was able to look upon Devakī / blazing with intense splendor; seeing her, [their] minds were agitated.

182.s:
adṛṣṭāṃ puruṣaiḥ strībhir devakīṃ devatāgaṇāḥ
bibhrāṇāṃ vapuṣā viṣṇuṃ tuṣṭuvus tām aharniśam //
182.d:
अदृष्टां पुरुषैः स्त्रीभिर् देवकीं देवतागणाः
बिभ्राणां वपुषा विष्णुं तुष्टुवुस् ताम् अहर्निशम् ॥
182.m: Unseen by mortal men and women, Devakī, / bearing Viṣṇu in her body, was praised day and night by hosts of deities.

182.s:
devā ūcuḥ
tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā vidyā sudhā tvaṃ jyotir eva ca
tvaṃ sarvalokarakṣārtham avatīrṇā mahītale //
182.d:
देवा ऊचुः
त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा विद्या सुधा त्वं ज्योतिर् एव च
त्वं सर्वलोकरक्षार्थम् अवतीर्णा महीतले ॥
182.m:
The gods said:
"You are Svāhā, you are Svadhā, learning, nectar, and light; / you have descended upon the earth for the protection of all the worlds.

182.s:
prasīda devi sarvasya jagatas tvaṃ śubhaṃ kuru
prītyarthaṃ dhārayeśānaṃ dhṛtaṃ yenākhilaṃ jagat //
182.d:
प्रसीद देवि सर्वस्य जगतस् त्वं शुभं कुरु
प्रीत्यर्थं धारयेशानं धृतं येनाखिलं जगत् ॥
182.m: Be gracious, O goddess! Bring welfare to the entire world! / For our joy, bear the Lord by whom the whole universe is sustained."

182.s:
vyāsa uvāca
evaṃ saṃstūyamānā sā devair devam adhārayat
garbheṇa puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ jagatāṃ trāṇakāraṇam //
182.d:
व्यास उवाच
एवं संस्तूयमाना सा देवैर् देवम् अधारयत्
गर्भेण पुण्डरीकाक्षं जगतां त्राणकारणम् ॥
182.m:
Vyāsa said:
Being thus praised by the gods, she bore the god / in her womb—the lotus-eyed one who is the cause of the preservation of the worlds.

182.s:
tato 'khilajagatpadmabodhāyācyutabhānunā
devakyāḥ pūrvasaṃdhyāyām āvirbhūtaṃ mahātmanā //
182.d:
ततो ऽखिलजगत्पद्मबोधायाच्युतभानुना
देवक्याः पूर्वसंध्यायाम् आविर्भूतं महात्मना ॥
182.m: Then, for the awakening of the lotus of the entire universe, / the great-souled sun that is Acyuta arose in the eastern twilight that was Devakī.

182.s:
madhyarātre 'khilādhāre jāyamāne janārdane
mandaṃ jagarjur jaladāḥ puṣpavṛṣṭimucaḥ surāḥ //
182.d:
मध्यरात्रे ऽखिलाधारे जायमाने जनार्दने
मन्दं जगर्जुर् जलदाः पुष्पवृष्टिमुचः सुराः ॥
182.m: At midnight, as Janārdana, the foundation of all, was being born, / the clouds thundered softly, and the gods rained down flowers.

182.s:
phullendīvarapattrābhaṃ caturbāhum udīkṣya tam
śrīvatsavakṣasaṃ jātaṃ tuṣṭāvānakadundubhiḥ //
182.d:
फुल्लेन्दीवरपत्त्राभं चतुर्बाहुम् उदीक्ष्य तम्
श्रीवत्सवक्षसं जातं तुष्टावानकदुन्दुभिः ॥
182.m: Beholding him born with four arms, gleaming like the petals of a blooming blue lotus, / and marked with the Śrīvatsa on his chest, Ānakadundubhi praised him.

182.s:
abhiṣṭūya ca taṃ vāgbhiḥ prasannābhir mahāmatiḥ
vijñāpayām āsa tadā kaṃsād bhīto dvijottamāḥ //
182.d:
अभिष्टूय च तं वाग्भिः प्रसन्नाभिर् महामतिः
विज्ञापयाम् आस तदा कंसाद् भीतो द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
182.m: Having praised him with serene words, that great-minded man, / terrified of Kaṃsa, then addressed him, O best of the twice-born:

182.s:
vasudeva uvāca
jñāto 'si devadeveśa śaṅkhacakragadādhara
divyaṃ rūpam idaṃ deva prasādenopasaṃhara //
182.d:
वसुदेव उवाच
ज्ञातो ऽसि देवदेवेश शङ्खचक्रगदाधर
दिव्यं रूपम् इदं देव प्रसादेनोपसंहर ॥
182.m:
Vasudeva said:
"You are recognized, O Lord of the gods of gods, bearer of the conch, discus, and mace! / O God, graciously withdraw this divine form!

182.s:
adyaiva deva kaṃso 'yaṃ kurute mama yātanām
avatīrṇam iti jñātvā tvām asmin mandire mama //
182.d:
अद्यैव देव कंसो ऽयं कुरुते मम यातनाम्
अवतीर्णम् इति ज्ञात्वा त्वाम् अस्मिन् मन्दिरे मम ॥
182.m: This Kaṃsa will inflict torment upon me this very day, O God, / once he learns that you have descended here in my house."

182.s:
devaky uvāca
yo 'nantarūpo 'khilaviśvarūpo
garbhe 'pi lokān vapuṣā bibharti
prasīdatām eṣa sa devadevaḥ
svamāyayāviṣkṛtabālarūpaḥ
182.d:
देवक्य् उवाच
यो ऽनन्तरूपो ऽखिलविश्वरूपो
गर्भे ऽपि लोकान् वपुषा बिभर्ति
प्रसीदताम् एष स देवदेवः
स्वमाययाविष्कृतबालरूपः
182.m:
Devakī said:
"May this god of gods be pleased, who, having infinite forms and all universal forms, / sustains the worlds with his body even while in the womb, / and has revealed a child's form by his own illusory power!"

182.s:
upasaṃhara sarvātman rūpam etac caturbhujam
jānātu māvatāraṃ te kaṃso 'yaṃ ditijāntaka //
182.d:
उपसंहर सर्वात्मन् रूपम् एतच् चतुर्भुजम्
जानातु मावतारं ते कंसो ऽयं दितिजान्तक ॥
182.m: Withdraw this four-armed form, O self of all; / let not this Kaṃsa know of your descent, O slayer of Diti’s sons!

182.s:
śrībhagavān uvāca
stuto 'haṃ yat tvayā pūrvaṃ putrārthinyā tad adya te
saphalaṃ devi saṃjātaṃ jāto 'haṃ yat tavodarāt //
182.d:
श्रीभगवान् उवाच
स्तुतो ऽहं यत् त्वया पूर्वं पुत्रार्थिन्या तद् अद्य ते
सफलं देवि संजातं जातो ऽहं यत् तवोदरात् ॥
182.m: The Blessed Lord said: / 'That for which I was formerly praised by you who desired a son has today, O queen, / borne fruit, since I have been born from your womb.'

182.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktvā bhagavāṃs tūṣṇīṃ babhūva munisattamāḥ
vasudevo 'pi taṃ rātrāv ādāya prayayau bahiḥ //
182.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा भगवांस् तूष्णीं बभूव मुनिसत्तमाः
वसुदेवो ऽपि तं रात्राव् आदाय प्रययौ बहिः ॥
182.m: Vyāsa said: / Having spoken thus, the Blessed Lord fell silent, O best of sages. / Vasudeva took him by night and went outside.

182.s:
mohitāś cābhavaṃs tatra rakṣiṇo yoganidrayā
mathurādvārapālāś ca vrajaty ānakadundubhau //
182.d:
मोहिताश् चाभवंस् तत्र रक्षिणो योगनिद्रया
मथुराद्वारपालाश् च व्रजत्य् आनकदुन्दुभौ ॥
182.m: And the guards there were bewildered by Yoganidrā, / as were the Mathurā gatekeepers, while Ānakadundubhi departed.

182.s:
varṣatāṃ jaladānāṃ ca tat toyam ulbaṇaṃ niśi
saṃchādya taṃ yayau śeṣaḥ phaṇair ānakadundubhim //
182.d:
वर्षतां जलदानां च तत् तोयम् उल्बणं निशि
संछाद्य तं ययौ शेषः फणैर् आनकदुन्दुभिम् ॥
182.m: And as the clouds rained down that violent water in the night, / Śeṣa followed, covering Ānakadundubhi with his hoods.

182.s:
yamunāṃ cātigambhīrāṃ nānāvartaśatākulām
vasudevo vahan viṣṇuṃ jānumātravahāṃ yayau //
182.d:
यमुनां चातिगम्भीरां नानावर्तशताकुलाम्
वसुदेवो वहन् विष्णुं जानुमात्रवहां ययौ ॥
182.m: And carrying Viṣṇu, Vasudeva went across the Yamunā, / which was exceedingly deep and turbulent with hundreds of whirlpools, flowing only knee-deep [for him].

182.s:
kaṃsasya karam ādāya tatraivābhyāgatāṃs taṭe
nandādīn gopavṛddhāṃś ca yamunāyāṃ dadarśa saḥ //
182.d:
कंसस्य करम् आदाय तत्रैवाभ्यागतांस् तटे
नन्दादीन् गोपवृद्धांश् च यमुनायां ददर्श सः ॥
182.m: He saw Nanda and the other cowherd elders on the bank of the Yamunā, / who had arrived right there having brought Kaṃsa's tribute.

182.s:
tasmin kāle yaśodāpi mohitā yoganidrayā
tām eva kanyāṃ munayaḥ prāsūta mohite jane //
182.d:
तस्मिन् काले यशोदापि मोहिता योगनिद्रया
ताम् एव कन्यां मुनयः प्रासूत मोहिते जने ॥
182.m: At that time Yaśodā too, bewildered by Yoganidrā, / gave birth to that very girl, O sages, while the people were bewitched.

182.s:
vasudevo 'pi vinyasya bālam ādāya dārikām
yaśodāśayane tūrṇam ājagāmāmitadyutiḥ //
182.d:
वसुदेवो ऽपि विन्यस्य बालम् आदाय दारिकाम्
यशोदाशयने तूर्णम् आजगामामितद्युतिः ॥
182.m: Placing the boy down and taking the girl / into Yaśodā's bed, Vasudeva of immeasurable splendor returned swiftly.

182.s:
dadarśa ca vibuddhvā sā yaśodā jātam ātmajam
nīlotpaladalaśyāmaṃ tato 'tyarthaṃ mudaṃ yayau //
182.d:
ददर्श च विबुद्ध्वा सा यशोदा जातम् आत्मजम्
नीलोत्पलदलश्यामं ततो ऽत्यर्थं मुदं ययौ ॥
182.m: And waking up, Yaśodā saw a son born to her, / dark as a blue lotus petal; then she felt exceeding joy.

182.s:
ādāya vasudevo 'pi dārikāṃ nijamandiram
devakīśayane nyasya yathāpūrvam atiṣṭhata //
182.d:
आदाय वसुदेवो ऽपि दारिकां निजमन्दिरम्
देवकीशयने न्यस्य यथापूर्वम् अतिष्ठत ॥
182.m: Taking the girl to his own dwelling / and placing her on Devakī's bed, Vasudeva stayed as before.

182.s:
tato bāladhvaniṃ śrutvā rakṣiṇaḥ sahasotthitāḥ
kaṃsam āvedayām āsur devakīprasavaṃ dvijāḥ //
182.d:
ततो बालध्वनिं श्रुत्वा रक्षिणः सहसोत्थिताः
कंसम् आवेदयाम् आसुर् देवकीप्रसवं द्विजाः ॥
182.m: Then, hearing the sound of the child, the guards arose at once / and reported Devakī's delivery to Kaṃsa, O twice-born ones.

182.s:
kaṃsas tūrṇam upetyaināṃ tato jagrāha bālikām
muñca muñceti devakyāsannakaṇṭhaṃ nivāritaḥ //
182.d:
कंसस् तूर्णम् उपेत्यैनां ततो जग्राह बालिकाम्
मुञ्च मुञ्चेति देवक्यासन्नकण्ठं निवारितः ॥
182.m: Approaching quickly, Kaṃsa seized the girl, / [though] restrained by Devakī with a choked throat, saying, 'Spare her! Spare her!'

182.s:
cikṣepa ca śilāpṛṣṭhe sā kṣiptā viyati sthitim
avāpa rūpaṃ ca mahat sāyudhāṣṭamahābhujam
prajahāsa tathaivoccaiḥ kaṃsaṃ ca ruṣitābravīt //
182.d:
चिक्षेप च शिलापृष्ठे सा क्षिप्ता वियति स्थितिम्
अवाप रूपं च महत् सायुधाष्टमहाभुजम्
प्रजहास तथैवोच्चैः कंसं च रुषिताब्रवीत् ॥
182.m: And he dashed her against the surface of a rock. Cast down, she took her stand in the sky, / assuming a vast form with eight mighty arms bearing weapons. / She laughed aloud and, infuriated, spoke to Kaṃsa:

182.s:
yogamāyovāca
kiṃ mayākṣiptayā kaṃsa jāto yas tvāṃ haniṣyati
sarvasvabhūto devānām āsīn mṛtyuḥ purā sa te
tad etat saṃpradhāryāśu kriyatāṃ hitam ātmanaḥ //
182.d:
योगमायोवाच
किं मयाक्षिप्तया कंस जातो यस् त्वां हनिष्यति
सर्वस्वभूतो देवानाम् आसीन् मृत्युः पुरा स ते
तद् एतत् संप्रधार्याशु क्रियतां हितम् आत्मनः ॥
182.m: Yogamāyā said: / 'What is gained, Kaṃsa, by casting me down? The one who will kill you has been born! / He who is the very essence of the gods was previously your death; / therefore, consider this quickly and do what is beneficial for yourself!'

182.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktvā prayayau devī divyasraggandhabhūṣaṇā
paśyato bhojarājasya stutā siddhair vihāyasā //
182.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा प्रययौ देवी दिव्यस्रग्गन्धभूषणा
पश्यतो भोजराजस्य स्तुता सिद्धैर् विहायसा ॥
182.m: Vyāsa said: / Having spoken thus, the goddess, adorned with celestial garlands and unguents, / departed through the sky while the king of the Bhojas looked on, praised by the Siddhas.

183.s:
vyāsa uvāca
kaṃsas tv athodvignamanāḥ prāha sarvān mahāsurān
pralambakeśipramukhān āhūyāsurapuṃgavān //
183.d:
व्यास उवाच
कंसस् त्व् अथोद्विग्नमनाः प्राह सर्वान् महासुरान्
प्रलम्बकेशिप्रमुखान् आहूयासुरपुंगवान् ॥
183.m: Vyāsa said: / Then Kaṃsa, his mind agitated, summoned the foremost Asuras, / led by Pralamba and Keśin, and spoke to all the great Asuras:

183.s:
kaṃsa uvāca
he pralamba mahābāho keśin dhenuka pūtane
ariṣṭādyais tathā cānyaiḥ śrūyatāṃ vacanaṃ mama //
183.d:
कंस उवाच
हे प्रलम्ब महाबाहो केशिन् धेनुक पूतने
अरिष्टाद्यैस् तथा चान्यैः श्रूयतां वचनं मम ॥
183.m: Kaṃsa said: / 'O Pralamba of mighty arms! O Keśin, Dhenuka, Pūtanā, / and Ariṣṭa and the others: let my words be heard!

183.s:
māṃ hantum amarair yatnaḥ kṛtaḥ kila durātmabhiḥ
madvīryatāpitān vīrān na tv etān gaṇayāmy aham //
183.d:
मां हन्तुम् अमरैर् यत्नः कृतः किल दुरात्मभिः
मद्वीर्यतापितान् वीरान् न त्व् एतान् गणयाम्य् अहम् ॥
183.m: An attempt has indeed been made to kill me by the vile-minded gods; / yet I do not consider them heroes, scorched as they are by my valor.

183.s:
āścaryaṃ kanyayā coktaṃ jāyate daityapuṃgavāḥ
hāsyaṃ me jāyate vīrās teṣu yatnapareṣv api //
183.d:
आश्चर्यं कन्यया चोक्तं जायते दैत्यपुंगवाः
हास्यं मे जायते वीरास् तेषु यत्नपरेष्व् अपि ॥
183.m: What the girl has spoken is surprising, O foremost Daityas; / it brings laughter to me, O heroes, even as they persist in their efforts.

183.s:
tathāpi khalu duṣṭānāṃ teṣām apy adhikaṃ mayā
apakārāya daityendrā yatanīyaṃ durātmanām //
183.d:
तथापि खलु दुष्टानां तेषाम् अप्य् अधिकं मया
अपकाराय दैत्येन्द्रा यतनीयं दुरात्मनाम् ॥
183.m: Nevertheless, O lords of Daityas, even greater effort must be made by me / to harm those wicked, evil-minded beings.

183.s:
utpannaś cāpi mṛtyur me bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ
ity etad bālikā prāha devakīgarbhasaṃbhavā //
183.d:
उत्पन्नश् चापि मृत्युर् मे भूतभव्यभवत्प्रभुः
इत्य् एतद् बालिका प्राह देवकीगर्भसंभवा ॥
183.m: And my death, the lord of past, future, and present, has arisen: / thus spoke the girl born from the womb of Devakī.

183.s:
tasmād bāleṣu paramo yatnaḥ kāryo mahītale
yatrodriktaṃ balaṃ bāle sa hantavyaḥ prayatnataḥ //
183.d:
तस्माद् बालेषु परमो यत्नः कार्यो महीतले
यत्रोद्रिक्तं बलं बाले स हन्तव्यः प्रयत्नतः ॥
183.m: Therefore, utmost effort must be made regarding children on the earth; / wherever excess strength is found in a child, he must be slain with effort.'

183.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity ājñāpyāsurān kaṃsaḥ praviśyātmagṛhaṃ tataḥ
uvāca vasudevaṃ ca devakīm avirodhataḥ //
183.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् आज्ञाप्यासुरान् कंसः प्रविश्यात्मगृहं ततः
उवाच वसुदेवं च देवकीम् अविरोधतः ॥
183.m: Vyāsa said: / Having commanded the Asuras thus, Kaṃsa entered his own house, / and then spoke to Vasudeva and Devakī without hostility:

183.s:
kaṃsa uvāca
yuvayor ghātitā garbhā vṛthaivaite mayādhunā
ko 'py anya eva nāśāya bālo mama samudgataḥ //
183.d:
कंस उवाच
युवयोर् घातिता गर्भा वृथैवैते मयाधुना
को ऽप्य् अन्य एव नाशाय बालो मम समुद्गतः ॥
183.m: Kaṃsa said: / 'In vain were those embryos of yours destroyed by me just now; / some other boy has arisen entirely for my destruction.

183.s:
tad alaṃ paritāpena nūnaṃ yad bhāvino hi te
arbhakā yuvayoḥ ko vā āyuṣo 'nte na hanyate //
183.d:
तद् अलं परितापेन नूनं यद् भाविनो हि ते
अर्भका युवयोः को वा आयुषो ऽन्ते न हन्यते ॥
183.m: Therefore, enough of sorrow! For surely those children / of yours were destined to pass away. Who is not slain at the end of his lifespan?'

183.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity āśvāsya vimucyaiva kaṃsas tau paritoṣya ca
antargṛhaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ praviveśa punaḥ svakam //
183.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् आश्वास्य विमुच्यैव कंसस् तौ परितोष्य च
अन्तर्गृहं द्विजश्रेष्ठाः प्रविवेश पुनः स्वकम् ॥
183.m: Vyāsa said: / Having consoled them thus, released them, and pacified them, O best of the twice-born, / Kaṃsa entered his own inner apartment once again.

184.s:
vyāsa uvāca
vimukto vasudevo 'pi nandasya śakaṭaṃ gataḥ
prahṛṣṭaṃ dṛṣṭavān nandaṃ putro jāto mameti vai //
184.d:
व्यास उवाच
विमुक्तो वसुदेवो ऽपि नन्दस्य शकटं गतः
प्रहृष्टं दृष्टवान् नन्दं पुत्रो जातो ममेति वै ॥
184.m: Vyāsa said: / Being released, Vasudeva went to Nanda's cart; / he saw Nanda rejoicing, thinking, 'A son has been born to me!'

184.s:
vasudevo 'pi taṃ prāha diṣṭyā diṣṭyeti sādaram
vārdhake 'pi samutpannas tanayo 'yaṃ tavādhunā //
184.d:
वसुदेवो ऽपि तं प्राह दिष्ट्या दिष्ट्येति सादरम्
वार्धके ऽपि समुत्पन्नस् तनयो ऽयं तवाधुना ॥
184.m: Vasudeva respectfully said to him: 'By good fortune! By good fortune! / In your old age, this son has now been born to you!

184.s:
datto hi vārṣikaḥ sarvo bhavadbhir nṛpateḥ karaḥ
yadartham āgatas tasmān nātra stheyaṃ mahātmanā //
184.d:
दत्तो हि वार्षिकः सर्वो भवद्भिर् नृपतेः करः
यदर्थम् आगतस् तस्मान् नात्र स्थेयं महात्मना ॥
184.m: The entire annual tax to the king has been paid by you, / for the sake of which you had come; therefore you, great-souled one, should not remain here.

184.s:
yadartham āgataḥ kāryaṃ tan niṣpannaṃ kim āsyate
bhavadbhir gamyatāṃ nanda tac chīghraṃ nijagokulam //
184.d:
यदर्थम् आगतः कार्यं तन् निष्पन्नं किम् आस्यते
भवद्भिर् गम्यतां नन्द तच् छीघ्रं निजगोकुलम् ॥
184.m: The business for which you came has been accomplished; why do you linger? / Go quickly, Nanda, to your own Gokula!

184.s:
mamāpi bālakas tatra rohiṇīprasavo hi yaḥ
sa rakṣaṇīyo bhavatā yathāyaṃ tanayo nijaḥ //
184.d:
ममापि बालकस् तत्र रोहिणीप्रसवो हि यः
स रक्षणीयो भवता यथायं तनयो निजः ॥
184.m: There is also my boy there, the child born of Rohiṇī; / he should be protected by you just like this own son of yours.'

184.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktāḥ prayayur gopā nandagopapurogamāḥ
śakaṭāropitair bhāṇḍaiḥ karaṃ dattvā mahābalāḥ //
184.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्ताः प्रययुर् गोपा नन्दगोपपुरोगमाः
शकटारोपितैर् भाण्डैः करं दत्त्वा महाबलाः ॥
184.m: Vyāsa said: / Being spoken to thus, the cowherds, headed by Nandagopa, / departed with goods loaded on carts, having paid the tax, full of great strength.

184.s:
vasatāṃ gokule teṣāṃ pūtanā bālaghātinī
suptaṃ kṛṣṇam upādāya rātrau ca pradadau stanam //
184.d:
वसतां गोकुले तेषां पूतना बालघातिनी
सुप्तं कृष्णम् उपादाय रात्रौ च प्रददौ स्तनम् ॥
184.m: While they were living in Gokula, Pūtanā, the child-slayer, / took up the sleeping Kṛṣṇa at night and gave him her breast.

184.s:
yasmai yasmai stanaṃ rātrau pūtanā saṃprayacchati
tasya tasya kṣaṇenāṅgaṃ bālakasyopahanyate //
184.d:
यस्मै यस्मै स्तनं रात्रौ पूतना संप्रयच्छति
तस्य तस्य क्षणेनाङ्गं बालकस्योपहन्यते ॥
184.m: To whomever Pūtanā gives her breast at night, / in an instant that child's body is destroyed.

184.s:
kṛṣṇas tasyāḥ stanaṃ gāḍhaṃ karābhyām atipīḍitam
gṛhītvā prāṇasahitaṃ papau krodhasamanvitaḥ //
184.d:
कृष्णस् तस्याः स्तनं गाढं कराभ्याम् अतिपीडितम्
गृहीत्वा प्राणसहितं पपौ क्रोधसमन्वितः ॥
184.m: Grasping her breast tightly, pressing it hard with both hands, / Kṛṣṇa, filled with wrath, sucked it together with her vital breath.

184.s:
sā vimuktamahārāvā vicchinnasnāyubandhanā
papāta pūtanā bhūmau mriyamāṇātibhīṣaṇā //
184.d:
सा विमुक्तमहारावा विच्छिन्नस्नायुबन्धना
पपात पूतना भूमौ म्रियमाणातिभीषणा ॥
184.m: Uttering a terrible roar, her sinews torn apart, / Pūtanā fell to the ground, dying, exceedingly terrifying.

184.s:
tannādaśrutisaṃtrāsād vibuddhās te vrajaukasaḥ
dadṛśuḥ pūtanotsaṅge kṛṣṇaṃ tāṃ ca nipātitām //
184.d:
तन्नादश्रुतिसंत्रासाद् विबुद्धास् ते व्रजौकसः
ददृशुः पूतनोत्सङ्गे कृष्णं तां च निपातिताम् ॥
184.m: Awoken in terror from hearing that roar, the residents of Vraja / saw Kṛṣṇa on the lap of Pūtanā and saw her struck down.

184.s:
ādāya kṛṣṇaṃ saṃtrastā yaśodā ca tato dvijāḥ
gopucchabhrāmaṇādyaiś ca bāladoṣam apākarot //
184.d:
आदाय कृष्णं संत्रस्ता यशोदा च ततो द्विजाः
गोपुच्छभ्रामणाद्यैश् च बालदोषम् अपाकरोत् ॥
184.m: Terrified, Yaśodā took Kṛṣṇa, O twice-born ones, / and removed the evil influences from the boy by waving a cow's tail and other rites.

184.s:
gopurīṣam upādāya nandagopo 'pi mastake
kṛṣṇasya pradadau rakṣāṃ kurvann idam udairayat //
184.d:
गोपुरीषम् उपादाय नन्दगोपो ऽपि मस्तके
कृष्णस्य प्रददौ रक्षां कुर्वन्न् इदम् उदैरयत् ॥
184.m: Taking cow dung, Nandagopa also placed it on the head / of Kṛṣṇa, performing protection while reciting this:

184.s:
nandagopa uvāca
rakṣatu tvām aśeṣāṇāṃ bhūtānāṃ prabhavo hariḥ
yasya nābhisamudbhūtāt paṅkajād abhavaj jagat //
184.d:
नन्दगोप उवाच
रक्षतु त्वाम् अशेषाणां भूतानां प्रभवो हरिः
यस्य नाभिसमुद्भूतात् पङ्कजाद् अभवज् जगत् ॥
184.m: Nandagopa said: / 'May Hari, the source of all beings, protect you, / from whose navel-born lotus arose the world!

184.s:
yena daṃṣṭrāgravidhṛtā dhārayaty avanī jagat
varāharūpadhṛg devaḥ sa tvāṃ rakṣatu keśavaḥ //
184.d:
येन दंष्ट्राग्रविधृता धारयत्य् अवनी जगत्
वराहरूपधृग् देवः स त्वां रक्षतु केशवः ॥
184.m: May that god Keśava protect you, who assumes the form of a boar, / held on the tip of whose tusk the earth supports the universe!

184.s:
guhyaṃ sa jaṭharaṃ viṣṇur jaṅghāpādau janārdanaḥ
vāmano rakṣatu sadā bhavantaṃ yaḥ kṣaṇād abhūt //
184.d:
गुह्यं स जठरं विष्णुर् जङ्घापादौ जनार्दनः
वामनो रक्षतु सदा भवन्तं यः क्षणाद् अभूत् ॥
184.m: May Viṣṇu protect the privities and the belly, Janārdana the shanks and feet; / may Vāmana, who arose in an instant, protect you always!

184.s:
trivikramakramākrāntatrailokyasphuradāyudhaḥ
śiras te pātu govindaḥ kaṇṭhaṃ rakṣatu keśavaḥ //
184.d:
त्रिविक्रमक्रमाक्रान्तत्रैलोक्यस्फुरदायुधः
शिरस् ते पातु गोविन्दः कण्ठं रक्षतु केशवः ॥
184.m: May Govinda, whose weapons gleam and who traversed the three worlds with the strides of Trivikrama, / guard your head; may Keśava protect your throat!

184.s:
mukhabāhū prabāhū ca manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca
rakṣatv avyāhataiśvaryas tava nārāyaṇo 'vyayaḥ //
184.d:
मुखबाहू प्रबाहू च मनः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि च
रक्षत्व् अव्याहतैश्वर्यस् तव नारायणो ऽव्ययः ॥
184.m: May the imperishable Nārāyaṇa of unimpeded sovereignty protect your face, / arms, forearms, mind, and all your senses!'

184.s:
tvāṃ dikṣu pātu vaikuṇṭho vidikṣu madhusūdanaḥ
hṛṣīkeśo 'mbare bhūmau rakṣatu tvāṃ mahīdharaḥ //
184.d:
त्वां दिक्षु पातु वैकुण्ठो विदिक्षु मधुसूदनः
हृषीकेशो ऽम्बरे भूमौ रक्षतु त्वां महीधरः ॥
184.m: May Vaikuṇṭha protect you in the cardinal directions, and Madhusūdana in the intermediate directions; / may Hṛṣīkeśa protect you in the sky, and Mahīdhara on earth.

184.s:
vyāsa uvāca
evaṃ kṛtasvastyayano nandagopena bālakaḥ
śāyitaḥ śakaṭasyādho bālaparyaṅkikātale //
184.d:
व्यास उवाच
एवं कृतस्वस्त्ययनो नन्दगोपेन बालकः
शायितः शकटस्याधो बालपर्यङ्किकातले ॥
184.m: Vyāsa said: / When the blessing of auspiciousness had thus been performed by the cowherd Nanda, the child / was laid down beneath a cart, under a small cot for babies.

184.s:
te ca gopā mahad dṛṣṭvā pūtanāyāḥ kalevaram
mṛtāyāḥ paramaṃ trāsaṃ vismayaṃ ca tadā yayuḥ //
184.d:
ते च गोपा महद् दृष्ट्वा पूतनायाः कलेवरम्
मृतायाः परमं त्रासं विस्मयं च तदा ययुः ॥
184.m: And those cowherds, seeing the huge body of the dead Pūtanā, / were struck with immense terror and astonishment at that time.

184.s:
kadācic chakaṭasyādhaḥ śayāno madhusūdanaḥ
cikṣepa caraṇāv ūrdhvaṃ stanārthī praruroda ca //
184.d:
कदाचिच् छकटस्याधः शयानो मधुसूदनः
चिक्षेप चरणाव् ऊर्ध्वं स्तनार्थी प्ररुरोद च ॥
184.m: Once, lying beneath the cart, Madhusūdana / tossed his feet upward, desirous of the breast, and wept loudly.

184.s:
tasya pādaprahāreṇa śakaṭaṃ parivartitam
vidhvastabhāṇḍakumbhaṃ tad viparītaṃ papāta vai //
184.d:
तस्य पादप्रहारेण शकटं परिवर्तितम्
विध्वस्तभाण्डकुम्भं तद् विपरीतं पपात वै ॥
184.m: By the blow of his foot, the cart was overturned; / with its pots and pitchers smashed, it truly fell upside down.

184.s:
tato hāhākṛtaḥ sarvo gopagopījano dvijāḥ
ājagāma tadā jñātvā bālam uttānaśāyinam //
184.d:
ततो हाहाकृतः सर्वो गोपगोपीजनो द्विजाः
आजगाम तदा ज्ञात्वा बालम् उत्तानशायिनम् ॥
184.m: Then, crying out in alarm, all the cowherd men and women came running, O twice-born ones, / realizing [what had happened], and found the boy lying on his back.

184.s:
gopāḥ keneti jagaduḥ śakaṭaṃ parivartitam
tatraiva bālakāḥ procur bālenānena pātitam //
184.d:
गोपाः केनेति जगदुः शकटं परिवर्तितम्
तत्रैव बालकाः प्रोचुर् बालेनानेन पातितम् ॥
184.m: The cowherds asked: "By whom was the cart overturned?" / The children right there said: "It was knocked over by this baby.

184.s:
rudatā dṛṣṭam asmābhiḥ pādavikṣepatāḍitam
śakaṭaṃ parivṛttaṃ vai naitad anyasya ceṣṭitam //
184.d:
रुदता दृष्टम् अस्माभिः पादविक्षेपताडितम्
शकटं परिवृत्तं वै नैतद् अन्यस्य चेष्टितम् ॥
184.m: While he was crying, we saw it struck by the kicking of his feet, / and the cart truly overturned; this was not the deed of anyone else."

184.s:
tataḥ punar atīvāsan gopā vismitacetasaḥ
nandagopo 'pi jagrāha bālam atyantavismitaḥ //
184.d:
ततः पुनर् अतीवासन् गोपा विस्मितचेतसः
नन्दगोपो ऽपि जग्राह बालम् अत्यन्तविस्मितः ॥
184.m: Then the cowherds were again exceedingly amazed in their minds; / and the cowherd Nanda too picked up the boy, deeply astonished.

184.s:
yaśodā vismayārūḍhā bhagnabhāṇḍakapālakam
śakaṭaṃ cārcayām āsa dadhipuṣpaphalākṣataiḥ //
184.d:
यशोदा विस्मयारूढा भग्नभाण्डकपालकम्
शकटं चार्चयाम् आस दधिपुष्पफलाक्षतैः ॥
184.m: Filled with wonder, Yaśodā worshipped the broken pottery fragments / and the cart with curds, flowers, fruits, and unhusked barley grains.

184.s:
gargaś ca gokule tatra vasudevapracoditaḥ
pracchanna eva gopānāṃ saṃskāram akarot tayoḥ //
184.d:
गर्गश् च गोकुले तत्र वसुदेवप्रचोदितः
प्रच्छन्न एव गोपानां संस्कारम् अकरोत् तयोः ॥
184.m: And Garga, urged by Vasudeva, / performed their sacramental rites right there in Gokula, secretly from the cowherds.

184.s:
jyeṣṭhaṃ ca rāmam ity āha kṛṣṇaṃ caiva tathāparam
gargo matimatāṃ śreṣṭho nāma kurvan mahāmatiḥ //
184.d:
ज्येष्ठं च रामम् इत्य् आह कृष्णं चैव तथापरम्
गर्गो मतिमतां श्रेष्ठो नाम कुर्वन् महामतिः ॥
184.m: Bestowing names, the wise Garga, foremost among the intelligent, / named the elder Rāma, and the other Kṛṣṇa.

184.s:
alpenaiva hi kālena vijñātau tau mahābalau
ghṛṣṭajānukarau viprā babhūvatur ubhāv api //
184.d:
अल्पेनैव हि कालेन विज्ञातौ तौ महाबलौ
घृष्टजानुकरौ विप्रा बभूवतुर् उभाव् अपि ॥
184.m: Indeed, in a short time those two mighty ones came to be recognized, / O twice-born ones, as both crawled on hands and knees.

184.s:
karīṣabhasmadigdhāṅgau bhramamāṇāv itas tataḥ
na nivārayituṃ śaktā yaśodā tau na rohiṇī //
184.d:
करीषभस्मदिग्धाङ्गौ भ्रममाणाव् इतस् ततः
न निवारयितुं शक्ता यशोदा तौ न रोहिणी ॥
184.m: With their limbs smeared with cow dung and ash, wandering here and there, / neither Yaśodā nor Rohiṇī was able to restrain them.

184.s:
govāṭamadhye krīḍantau vatsavāṭagatau punaḥ
tadaharjātagovatsapucchākarṣaṇatatparau //
184.d:
गोवाटमध्ये क्रीडन्तौ वत्सवाटगतौ पुनः
तदहर्जातगोवत्सपुच्छाकर्षणतत्परौ ॥
184.m: Playing inside the cow-pen and then entering the calf-pen, / they were intent on pulling the tails of calves born that very day.

184.s:
yadā yaśodā tau bālāv ekasthānacarāv ubhau
śaśāka no vārayituṃ krīḍantāv aticañcalau //
184.d:
यदा यशोदा तौ बालाव् एकस्थानचराव् उभौ
शशाक नो वारयितुं क्रीडन्ताव् अतिचञ्चलौ ॥
184.m: When Yaśodā was unable to restrain those two boys / roaming in one place, playing, and exceedingly restless,

184.s:
dāmnā baddhvā tadā madhye nibabandha ulūkhale
kṛṣṇam akliṣṭakarmāṇam āha cedam amarṣitā //
184.d:
दाम्ना बद्ध्वा तदा मध्ये निबबन्ध उलूखले
कृष्णम् अक्लिष्टकर्माणम् आह चेदम् अमर्षिता ॥
184.m: tying [him] around the waist with a rope, she then bound Kṛṣṇa of effortless deeds / to a mortar, and spoke these words in anger:

184.s:
yaśodovāca
yadi śakto 'si gaccha tvam aticañcalaceṣṭita //
184.d:
यशोदोवाच
यदि शक्तो ऽसि गच्छ त्वम् अतिचञ्चलचेष्टित ॥
184.m: Yaśodā said: / "If you are able, you may go, you of exceedingly restless conduct!"

184.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktvā ca nijaṃ karma sā cakāra kuṭumbinī
vyagrāyām atha tasyāṃ sa karṣamāṇa ulūkhalam //
184.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा च निजं कर्म सा चकार कुटुम्बिनी
व्यग्रायाम् अथ तस्यां स कर्षमाण उलूखलम् ॥
184.m: Vyāsa said: / Having spoken thus, the housewife attended to her own work. / While she was occupied, he, dragging the mortar,

184.s:
yamalārjunayor madhye jagāma kamalekṣaṇaḥ
karṣatā vṛkṣayor madhye tiryag evam ulūkhalam //
184.d:
यमलार्जुनयोर् मध्ये जगाम कमलेक्षणः
कर्षता वृक्षयोर् मध्ये तिर्यग् एवम् उलूखलम् ॥
184.m: the lotus-eyed one, went between two arjuna trees; / as he dragged the mortar sideways between the two trees,

184.s:
bhagnāv uttuṅgaśākhāgrau tena tau yamalārjunau
tataḥ kaṭakaṭāśabdasamākarṇanakātaraḥ //
184.d:
भग्नाव् उत्तुङ्गशाखाग्रौ तेन तौ यमलार्जुनौ
ततः कटकटाशब्दसमाकर्णनकातरः ॥
184.m: the two arjuna trees had their lofty branch-tops broken by it. / Then, alarmed by hearing the cracking sound,

184.s:
ājagāma vrajajano dadṛśe ca mahādrumau
bhagnaskandhau nipātitau bhagnaśākhau mahītale //
184.d:
आजगाम व्रजजनो ददृशे च महाद्रुमौ
भग्नस्कन्धौ निपातितौ भग्नशाखौ महीतले ॥
184.m: the people of Vraja arrived and saw the two great trees / with broken trunks, fallen to the ground with shattered branches.

184.s:
dadarśa cālpadantāsyaṃ smitahāsaṃ ca bālakam
tayor madhyagataṃ baddhaṃ dāmnā gāḍhaṃ tathodare //
184.d:
ददर्श चाल्पदन्तास्यं स्मितहासं च बालकम्
तयोर् मध्यगतं बद्धं दाम्ना गाढं तथोदरे ॥
184.m: And they saw the child, with tiny teeth showing in his mouth and a smiling laugh, / standing between the two, firmly bound around his belly by the rope.

184.s:
tataś ca dāmodaratāṃ sa yayau dāmabandhanāt
gopavṛddhās tataḥ sarve nandagopapurogamāḥ //
184.d:
ततश् च दामोदरतां स ययौ दामबन्धनात्
गोपवृद्धास् ततः सर्वे नन्दगोपपुरोगमाः ॥
184.m: And thence he came to be known as Dāmodara, on account of being bound with a rope. / Then all the elder cowherds, headed by the cowherd Nanda,

184.s:
mantrayām āsur udvignā mahotpātātibhīravaḥ
sthāneneha na naḥ kāryaṃ vrajāmo 'nyan mahāvanam //
184.d:
मन्त्रयाम् आसुर् उद्विग्ना महोत्पातातिभीरवः
स्थानेनेह न नः कार्यं व्रजामो ऽन्यन् महावनम् ॥
184.m: held counsel, distressed and terrified by the great portents: / "We have no business staying in this place; let us go to another great forest.

184.s:
utpātā bahavo hy atra dṛśyante nāśahetavaḥ
pūtanāyā vināśaś ca śakaṭasya viparyayaḥ //
184.d:
उत्पाता बहवो ह्य् अत्र दृश्यन्ते नाशहेतवः
पूतनाया विनाशश् च शकटस्य विपर्ययः ॥
184.m: For many portents that cause destruction are seen here: / the destruction of Pūtanā, and the overturning of the cart,

184.s:
vinā vātādidoṣeṇa drumayoḥ patanaṃ tathā
vṛndāvanam itaḥ sthānāt tasmād gacchāma mā ciram //
184.d:
विना वातादिदोषेण द्रुमयोः पतनं तथा
वृन्दावनम् इतः स्थानात् तस्माद् गच्छाम मा चिरम् ॥
184.m: and likewise the falling of the two trees without any fault of wind and the like. / Therefore let us go without delay from this place to Vṛndāvana,

184.s:
yāvad bhaumamahotpātadoṣo nābhibhaved vrajam
iti kṛtvā matiṃ sarve gamane te vrajaukasaḥ //
184.d:
यावद् भौममहोत्पातदोषो नाभिभवेद् व्रजम्
इति कृत्वा मतिं सर्वे गमने ते व्रजौकसः ॥
184.m: before the calamity of great earthly portents overwhelms Vraja." / Having thus resolved upon departure, all those dwellers of Vraja

184.s:
ūcuḥ svaṃ svaṃ kulaṃ śīghraṃ gamyatāṃ mā vilambyatām
tataḥ kṣaṇena prayayuḥ śakaṭair godhanais tathā //
184.d:
ऊचुः स्वं स्वं कुलं शीघ्रं गम्यतां मा विलम्ब्यताम्
ततः क्षणेन प्रययुः शकटैर् गोधनैस् तथा ॥
184.m: said to their respective families: "Go quickly, do not delay!" / Then in an instant they set out with their carts and their herds of cattle,

184.s:
yūthaśo vatsapālīś ca kālayanto vrajaukasaḥ
sarvāvayavanirdhūtaṃ kṣaṇamātreṇa tat tadā //
184.d:
यूथशो वत्सपालीश् च कालयन्तो व्रजौकसः
सर्वावयवनिर्धूतं क्षणमात्रेण तत् तदा ॥
184.m: the dwellers of Vraja driving herds of calves in groups. / In a mere instant, stripped of all its parts,

184.s:
kākakākīsamākīrṇaṃ vrajasthānam abhūd dvijāḥ
vṛndāvanaṃ bhagavatā kṛṣṇenākliṣṭakarmaṇā //
184.d:
काककाकीसमाकीर्णं व्रजस्थानम् अभूद् द्विजाः
वृन्दावनं भगवता कृष्णेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ॥
184.m: the site of Vraja became crowded with crows and female crows, O twice-born ones. / Vṛndāvana had been contemplated with an auspicious mind / by the blessed Kṛṣṇa of effortless deeds, desiring the prosperity of the cows.

184.s:
śubhena manasā dhyātaṃ gavāṃ vṛddhim abhīpsatā
tatas tatrātirukṣe 'pi dharmakāle dvijottamāḥ //
184.d:
शुभेन मनसा ध्यातं गवां वृद्धिम् अभीप्सता
ततस् तत्रातिरुक्षे ऽपि धर्मकाले द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
184.m: Therefore, even in the extremely dry summer season there, O best of the twice-born,

184.s:
prāvṛṭkāla ivābhūc ca navaśaṣpaṃ samantataḥ
sa samāvāsitaḥ sarvo vrajo vṛndāvane tataḥ //
184.d:
प्रावृट्काल इवाभूच् च नवशष्पं समन्ततः
स समावासितः सर्वो व्रजो वृन्दावने ततः ॥
184.m: it was like the rainy season, with fresh green grass all around. / Then that entire Vraja settled in Vṛndāvana,

184.s:
śakaṭīvāṭaparyantacandrārdhākārasaṃsthitiḥ
vatsabālau ca saṃvṛttau rāmadāmodarau tataḥ //
184.d:
शकटीवाटपर्यन्तचन्द्रार्धाकारसंस्थितिः
वत्सबालौ च संवृत्तौ रामदामोदरौ ततः ॥
184.m: arranged in the shape of a crescent moon bordered by an enclosure of carts. / And then Rāma and Dāmodara became young boys tending the calves.

184.s:
tatra sthitau tau ca goṣṭhe ceratur bālalīlayā
barhipattrakṛtāpīḍau vanyapuṣpāvataṃsakau //
184.d:
तत्र स्थितौ तौ च गोष्ठे चेरतुर् बाललीलया
बर्हिपत्त्रकृतापीडौ वन्यपुष्पावतंसकौ ॥
184.m: Dwelling there in the cow-station, they wandered about in childish play, / wearing crests made of peacock feathers and garlands of wild flowers,

184.s:
gopaveṇukṛtātodyapattravādyakṛtasvanau
kākapakṣadharau bālau kumārāv iva pāvakau //
184.d:
गोपवेणुकृतातोद्यपत्त्रवाद्यकृतस्वनौ
काकपक्षधरौ बालौ कुमाराव् इव पावकौ ॥
184.m: producing musical notes from flutes of cowherds and sounds from leaf-whistles, / the two boys wearing side-locks like the two Kumāras, sons of fire.

184.s:
hasantau ca ramantau ca ceratus tan mahad vanam
kvacid dhasantāv anyonyaṃ krīḍamānau tathā paraiḥ //
184.d:
हसन्तौ च रमन्तौ च चेरतुस् तन् महद् वनम्
क्वचिद् धसन्ताव् अन्योन्यं क्रीडमानौ तथा परैः ॥
184.m: Laughing and playing, they roamed that great forest, / at times laughing with each other and playing likewise with others.

184.s:
gopaputraiḥ samaṃ vatsāṃś cārayantau viceratuḥ
kālena gacchatā tau tu saptavarṣau babhūvatuḥ //
184.d:
गोपपुत्रैः समं वत्सांश् चारयन्तौ विचेरतुः
कालेन गच्छता तौ तु सप्तवर्षौ बभूवतुः ॥
184.m: Together with the sons of the cowherds, they roamed grazing the calves. / As time passed, they became seven years old,

184.s:
sarvasya jagataḥ pālau vatsapālau mahāvraje
prāvṛṭkālas tato 'tīva meghaughasthagitāmbaraḥ //
184.d:
सर्वस्य जगतः पालौ वत्सपालौ महाव्रजे
प्रावृट्कालस् ततो ऽतीव मेघौघस्थगिताम्बरः ॥
184.m: the two protectors of the entire universe acting as calf-herds in the great Vraja. / Then came the rainy season, with the sky completely covered by masses of clouds,

184.s:
babhūva vāridhārābhir aikyaṃ kurvan diśām iva
prarūḍhanavapuṣpāḍhyā śakragopavṛtā mahī //
184.d:
बभूव वारिधाराभिर् ऐक्यं कुर्वन् दिशाम् इव
प्ररूढनवपुष्पाढ्या शक्रगोपवृता मही ॥
184.m: as if uniting the directions by streams of rain. / Abundant with newly sprouted flowers and filled with cochineal insects, the earth

184.s:
yathā mārakate vāsīt padmarāgavibhūṣitā
ūhur unmārgagāmīni nimnagāmbhāṃsi sarvataḥ //
184.d:
यथा मारकते वासीत् पद्मरागविभूषिता
ऊहुर् उन्मार्गगामीनि निम्नगाम्भांसि सर्वतः ॥
184.m: was like an emerald garment decorated with rubies. / Flowing off their courses on every side, the waters of the rivers rushed,

184.s:
manāṃsi durvinītānāṃ prāpya lakṣmīṃ navām iva
vikāle ca yathākāmaṃ vrajam etya mahābalau
gopaiḥ samānaiḥ sahitau cikrīḍāte 'marāv iva //
184.d:
मनांसि दुर्विनीतानां प्राप्य लक्ष्मीं नवाम् इव
विकाले च यथाकामं व्रजम् एत्य महाबलौ
गोपैः समानैः सहितौ चिक्रीडाते ऽमराव् इव ॥
184.m: like the minds of the undisciplined when they attain new fortune. / And in the evening, returning to Vraja at will, those two mighty ones / played with the cowherds of their own age, like two immortals.

185.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ekadā tu vinā rāmaṃ kṛṣṇo vṛndāvanaṃ yayau
vicacāra vṛto gopair vanyapuṣpasragujjvalaḥ //
185.d:
व्यास उवाच
एकदा तु विना रामं कृष्णो वृन्दावनं ययौ
विचचार वृतो गोपैर् वन्यपुष्पस्रगुज्ज्वलः ॥
185.m: Vyāsa said: / Once, without Rāma, Kṛṣṇa went to Vṛndāvana. / Surrounded by the cowherds, he wandered about, radiant with a garland of wild flowers.

185.s:
sa jagāmātha kālindīṃ lolakallolaśālinīm
tīrasaṃlagnaphenaughair hasantīm iva sarvataḥ //
185.d:
स जगामाथ कालिन्दीं लोलकल्लोलशालिनीम्
तीरसंलग्नफेनौघैर् हसन्तीम् इव सर्वतः ॥
185.m: He then went to the Kālindī, possessing rolling waves, / laughing, as it were, on all sides with masses of foam clinging to its banks.

185.s:
tasyāṃ cātimahābhīmaṃ viṣāgnikaṇadūṣitam
hradaṃ kālīyanāgasya dadarśātivibhīṣaṇam //
185.d:
तस्यां चातिमहाभीमं विषाग्निकणदूषितम्
ह्रदं कालीयनागस्य ददर्शातिविभीषणम् ॥
185.m: And in it he saw the most dreadful, exceedingly terrifying pool / of the serpent Kālīya, polluted by sparks of poisonous fire,

185.s:
viṣāgninā visaratā dagdhatīramahātarum
vātāhatāmbuvikṣepasparśadagdhavihaṃgamam //
185.d:
विषाग्निना विसरता दग्धतीरमहातरुम्
वाताहताम्बुविक्षेपस्पर्शदग्धविहंगमम् ॥
185.m: whose spreading fiery poison had burnt the great trees on its banks, / and the birds were scorched by contact with the spray of water whipped up by the wind.

185.s:
tam atīva mahāraudraṃ mṛtyuvaktram ivāparam
vilokya cintayām āsa bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ //
185.d:
तम् अतीव महारौद्रं मृत्युवक्त्रम् इवापरम्
विलोक्य चिन्तयाम् आस भगवान् मधुसूदनः ॥
185.m: Seeing that [pool], exceedingly fierce like another mouth of Death, / the blessed Madhusūdana reflected:

185.s:
asmin vasati duṣṭātmā kālīyo 'sau viṣāyudhaḥ
yo mayā nirjitas tyaktvā duṣṭo naṣṭaḥ payonidhau //
185.d:
अस्मिन् वसति दुष्टात्मा कालीयो ऽसौ विषायुधः
यो मया निर्जितस् त्यक्त्वा दुष्टो नष्टः पयोनिधौ ॥
185.m: "In this [pool] dwells that evil-minded Kālīya whose weapon is poison, / who, vanquished by me, fled and perished [from here], abandoning the ocean.

185.s:
teneyaṃ dūṣitā sarvā yamunā sāgaraṃgamā
na narair godhanair vāpi tṛṣārtair upabhujyate //
185.d:
तेनेयं दूषिता सर्वा यमुना सागरंगमा
न नरैर् गोधनैर् वापि तृषार्तैर् उपभुज्यते ॥
185.m: By him this entire Yamunā flowing to the ocean has been fouled; / it cannot be enjoyed by men or by herds of cattle tormented by thirst."

185.s:
tad asya nāgarājasya kartavyo nigraho mayā
nityatrastāḥ sukhaṃ yena careyur vrajavāsinaḥ //
185.d:
तद् अस्य नागराजस्य कर्तव्यो निग्रहो मया
नित्यत्रस्ताः सुखं येन चरेयुर् व्रजवासिनः ॥
185.m: "Therefore, this king of snakes must be subdued by me, / so that the inhabitants of Vraja, who are constantly terrified, may move about in comfort.

185.s:
etadarthaṃ nṛloke 'sminn avatāro mayā kṛtaḥ
yad eṣām utpathasthānāṃ kāryā śāstir durātmanām //
185.d:
एतदर्थं नृलोके ऽस्मिन्न् अवतारो मया कृतः
यद् एषाम् उत्पथस्थानां कार्या शास्तिर् दुरात्मनाम् ॥
185.m: It is for this purpose that my descent into this mortal world was made: / that punishment be meted out to these wicked ones walking the path of evil.

185.s:
tad etan nātidūrasthaṃ kadambam uruśākhinam
adhiruhyotpatiṣyāmi hrade 'smiñ jīvanāśinaḥ //
185.d:
तद् एतन् नातिदूरस्थं कदम्बम् उरुशाखिनम्
अधिरुह्योत्पतिष्यामि ह्रदे ऽस्मिञ् जीवनाशिनः ॥
185.m: Therefore, climbing up this kadamba tree with large branches not far away, / I will jump into this lake of the destroyer of life."

185.s:
vyāsa uvāca
itthaṃ vicintya baddhvā ca gāḍhaṃ parikaraṃ tataḥ
nipapāta hrade tatra sarparājasya vegataḥ //
185.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्थं विचिन्त्य बद्ध्वा च गाढं परिकरं ततः
निपपात ह्रदे तत्र सर्पराजस्य वेगतः ॥
185.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having thought thus and tightly girding his loins, / he then leaped with great force into that lake of the serpent king.

185.s:
tenāpi patatā tatra kṣobhitaḥ sa mahāhradaḥ
atyarthadūrajātāṃś ca tāṃś cāsiñcan mahīruhān //
185.d:
तेनापि पतता तत्र क्षोभितः स महाह्रदः
अत्यर्थदूरजातांश् च तांश् चासिञ्चन् महीरुहान् ॥
185.m: And by him plunging in there, that great pool was agitated, / and [its water] splashed even upon those trees that grew very far away.

185.s:
te 'hiduṣṭaviṣajvālātaptāmbutapanokṣitāḥ
jajvaluḥ pādapāḥ sadyo jvālāvyāptadigantarāḥ //
185.d:
ते ऽहिदुष्टविषज्वालातप्ताम्बुतपनोक्षिताः
जज्वलुः पादपाः सद्यो ज्वालाव्याप्तदिगन्तराः ॥
185.m: Splashed by the water heated by the fire of the serpent's noxious venom, / those trees immediately burst into flames, their fire filling every quarter.

185.s:
āsphoṭayām āsa tadā kṛṣṇo nāgahradaṃ bhujaiḥ
tacchabdaśravaṇāc cātha nāgarājo 'bhyupāgamat //
185.d:
आस्फोटयाम् आस तदा कृष्णो नागह्रदं भुजैः
तच्छब्दश्रवणाच् चाथ नागराजो ऽभ्युपागमत् ॥
185.m: Then Kṛṣṇa struck the serpent's pool with his arms; / and upon hearing that sound, the serpent king approached.

185.s:
ātāmranayanaḥ kopād viṣajvālākulaiḥ phaṇaiḥ
vṛto mahāviṣaiś cānyair aruṇair anilāśanaiḥ //
185.d:
आताम्रनयनः कोपाद् विषज्वालाकुलैः फणैः
वृतो महाविषैश् चान्यैर् अरुणैर् अनिलाशनैः ॥
185.m: His eyes were copper-red with rage, his hoods agitated with flames of poison; / he was surrounded by other highly venomous, red wind-eaters.

185.s:
nāgapatnyaś ca śataśo hārihāropaśobhitāḥ
prakampitatanūtkṣepacalatkuṇḍalakāntayaḥ //
185.d:
नागपत्न्यश् च शतशो हारिहारोपशोभिताः
प्रकम्पिततनूत्क्षेपचलत्कुण्डलकान्तयः ॥
185.m: There were also hundreds of serpent wives, adorned with charming necklaces, / the beauty of their earrings swaying with the shaking and rearing of their bodies.

185.s:
tataḥ praveṣṭitaḥ sarpaiḥ sa kṛṣṇo bhogabandhanaiḥ
dadaṃśuś cāpi te kṛṣṇaṃ viṣajvālāvilair mukhaiḥ //
185.d:
ततः प्रवेष्टितः सर्पैः स कृष्णो भोगबन्धनैः
ददंशुश् चापि ते कृष्णं विषज्वालाविलैर् मुखैः ॥
185.m: Then, encircled by the serpents with the coils of their bodies, / they bit Kṛṣṇa with mouths turbid with flames of poison.

185.s:
taṃ tatra patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā nāgabhoganipīḍitam
gopā vrajam upāgatya cukruśuḥ śokalālasāḥ //
185.d:
तं तत्र पतितं दृष्ट्वा नागभोगनिपीडितम्
गोपा व्रजम् उपागत्य चुक्रुशुः शोकलालसाः ॥
185.m: Seeing him fallen there and oppressed by the coils of the serpents, / the cowherds went to Vraja and cried out, overcome with grief:

185.s:
gopā ūcuḥ
eṣa kṛṣṇo gato mohamagno vai kāliye hrade
bhakṣyate sarparājena tad āgacchata mā ciram //
185.d:
गोपा ऊचुः
एष कृष्णो गतो मोहमग्नो वै कालिये ह्रदे
भक्ष्यते सर्पराजेन तद् आगच्छत मा चिरम् ॥
185.m: The cowherds said: / 'This Kṛṣṇa has sunk into unconsciousness in the pool of Kāliya; / he is being devoured by the king of serpents! Come without delay!'

185.s:
vyāsa uvāca
etac chrutvā tato gopā vajrapātopamaṃ vacaḥ
gopyaś ca tvaritā jagmur yaśodāpramukhā hradam //
185.d:
व्यास उवाच
एतच् छ्रुत्वा ततो गोपा वज्रपातोपमं वचः
गोप्यश् च त्वरिता जग्मुर् यशोदाप्रमुखा ह्रदम् ॥
185.m: Vyāsa said: / Hearing this word resembling the strike of a thunderbolt, the cowherds / and the cowherd women, led by Yaśodā, went in haste to the pool.

185.s:
hā hā kvāsāv iti jano gopīnām ativihvalaḥ
yaśodayā samaṃ bhrānto drutaḥ praskhalito yayau //
185.d:
हा हा क्वासाव् इति जनो गोपीनाम् अतिविह्वलः
यशोदया समं भ्रान्तो द्रुतः प्रस्खलितो ययौ ॥
185.m: 'Alas, alas! Where is he?' cried the company of cowherd women, intensely distraught; / confounded, running and stumbling, they went along with Yaśodā.

185.s:
nandagopaś ca gopāś ca rāmaś cādbhutavikramaḥ
tvaritaṃ yamunāṃ jagmuḥ kṛṣṇadarśanalālasāḥ //
185.d:
नन्दगोपश् च गोपाश् च रामश् चाद्भुतविक्रमः
त्वरितं यमुनां जग्मुः कृष्णदर्शनलालसाः ॥
185.m: Nandagopa, the cowherds, and Rāma of wondrous valor / quickly went to the Yamunā, longing for the sight of Kṛṣṇa.

185.s:
dadṛśuś cāpi te tatra sarparājavaśaṃgatam
niṣprayatnaṃ kṛtaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sarpabhogena veṣṭitam //
185.d:
ददृशुश् चापि ते तत्र सर्पराजवशंगतम्
निष्प्रयत्नं कृतं कृष्णं सर्पभोगेन वेष्टितम् ॥
185.m: They saw Kṛṣṇa there, fallen under the power of the serpent king, / rendered motionless, wrapped around by the coils of the serpent.

185.s:
nandagopaś ca niśceṣṭaḥ paśyan putramukhaṃ bhṛśam
yaśodā ca mahābhāgā babhūva munisattamāḥ //
185.d:
नन्दगोपश् च निश्चेष्टः पश्यन् पुत्रमुखं भृशम्
यशोदा च महाभागा बभूव मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
185.m: Nandagopa stood paralyzed, gazing intently upon the face of his son, / as did the fortunate Yaśodā, O best of sages.

185.s:
gopyas tv anyā rudatyaś ca dadṛśuḥ śokakātarāḥ
procuś ca keśavaṃ prītyā bhayakātaragadgadam //
185.d:
गोप्यस् त्व् अन्या रुदत्यश् च ददृशुः शोककातराः
प्रोचुश् च केशवं प्रीत्या भयकातरगद्गदम् ॥
185.m: The other cowherd women, weeping and distressed by grief, looked on; / full of affection, they spoke to Keśava in voices faltering and choked with fear:

185.s:
sarvā yaśodayā sārdhaṃ viśāmo 'tra mahāhrade
nāgarājasya no gantum asmākaṃ yujyate vraje //
185.d:
सर्वा यशोदया सार्धं विशामो ऽत्र महाह्रदे
नागराजस्य नो गन्तुम् अस्माकं युज्यते व्रजे ॥
185.m: 'Together with Yaśodā, we all enter into this great pool of the serpent king; / it is not fitting for us to go back to Vraja.

185.s:
divasaḥ ko vinā sūryaṃ vinā candreṇa kā niśā
vinā dugdhena kā gāvo vinā kṛṣṇena ko vrajaḥ
vinākṛtā na yāsyāmaḥ kṛṣṇenānena gokulam //
185.d:
दिवसः को विना सूर्यं विना चन्द्रेण का निशा
विना दुग्धेन का गावो विना कृष्णेन को व्रजः
विनाकृता न यास्यामः कृष्णेनानेन गोकुलम् ॥
185.m: What is day without the sun? What is night without the moon? / What are cows without milk? What is Vraja without Kṛṣṇa? / Bereft of this Kṛṣṇa, we will not return to Gokula.'

185.s:
vyāsa uvāca
iti gopīvacaḥ śrutvā rauhiṇeyo mahābalaḥ
uvāca gopān vidhurān vilokya stimitekṣaṇaḥ //
185.d:
व्यास उवाच
इति गोपीवचः श्रुत्वा रौहिणेयो महाबलः
उवाच गोपान् विधुरान् विलोक्य स्तिमितेक्षणः ॥
185.m: Vyāsa said: / Hearing these words of the cowherd women, Rohiṇī's son [Balarāma] of great strength, / with steady eyes, spoke as he beheld the afflicted cowherds,

185.s:
nandaṃ ca dīnam atyarthaṃ nyastadṛṣṭiṃ sutānane
mūrchākulāṃ yaśodāṃ ca kṛṣṇamāhātmyasaṃjñayā //
185.d:
नन्दं च दीनम् अत्यर्थं न्यस्तदृष्टिं सुतानने
मूर्छाकुलां यशोदां च कृष्णमाहात्म्यसंज्ञया ॥
185.m: and Nanda, deeply dejected with his gaze fixed upon his son's face, / and Yaśodā, fainting in confusion—alluding to the greatness of Kṛṣṇa.

185.s:
balarāma uvāca
kim ayaṃ devadeveśa bhāvo 'yaṃ mānuṣas tvayā
vyajyate svaṃ tam ātmānaṃ kim anyaṃ tvaṃ na vetsi yat //
185.d:
बलराम उवाच
किम् अयं देवदेवेश भावो ऽयं मानुषस् त्वया
व्यज्यते स्वं तम् आत्मानं किम् अन्यं त्वं न वेत्सि यत् ॥
185.m: Balarāma said: / 'Why, O lord of the gods, is this human condition / displayed by you? Do you not know your own true self, or [do you think] you are someone else?

185.s:
tvam asya jagato nābhiḥ surāṇām eva cāśrayaḥ
kartāpahartā pātā ca trailokyaṃ tvaṃ trayīmayaḥ //
185.d:
त्वम् अस्य जगतो नाभिः सुराणाम् एव चाश्रयः
कर्तापहर्ता पाता च त्रैलोक्यं त्वं त्रयीमयः ॥
185.m: You are the navel of this universe, and the refuge of the gods; / you are the creator, destroyer, and protector; you are the three worlds; you embody the threefold Veda.

185.s:
atrāvatīrṇayoḥ kṛṣṇa gopā eva hi bāndhavāḥ
gopyaś ca sīdataḥ kasmāt tvaṃ bandhūn samupekṣase //
185.d:
अत्रावतीर्णयोः कृष्ण गोपा एव हि बान्धवाः
गोप्यश् च सीदतः कस्मात् त्वं बन्धून् समुपेक्षसे ॥
185.m: For both of us descended here, Kṛṣṇa, these cowherds are our kinsmen, / and these cowherd women are perishing: why do you overlook your kin?

185.s:
darśito mānuṣo bhāvo darśitaṃ bālaceṣṭitam
tad ayaṃ damyatāṃ kṛṣṇa durātmā daśanāyudhaḥ //
185.d:
दर्शितो मानुषो भावो दर्शितं बालचेष्टितम्
तद् अयं दम्यतां कृष्ण दुरात्मा दशनायुधः ॥
185.m: The human condition has been displayed; childhood play has been shown. / Therefore, Kṛṣṇa, let this wicked-souled one, whose weapon is his fangs, be subdued!'

185.s:
vyāsa uvāca
iti saṃsmāritaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ smitabhinnauṣṭhasaṃpuṭaḥ
āsphālya mocayām āsa svaṃ dehaṃ bhogabandhanāt //
185.d:
व्यास उवाच
इति संस्मारितः कृष्णः स्मितभिन्नौष्ठसंपुटः
आस्फाल्य मोचयाम् आस स्वं देहं भोगबन्धनात् ॥
185.m: Vyāsa said: / Thus reminded, Kṛṣṇa parted his lips with a smile; / shaking [himself], he freed his body from the bond of coils.

185.s:
ānāmya cāpi hastābhyām ubhābhyāṃ madhyamaṃ phaṇam
āruhya bhugnaśirasaḥ prananartoruvikramaḥ //
185.d:
आनाम्य चापि हस्ताभ्याम् उभाभ्यां मध्यमं फणम्
आरुह्य भुग्नशिरसः प्रननर्तोरुविक्रमः ॥
185.m: Bending down the middle hood with both hands, / he mounted the serpent whose head was bent low and began to dance, he of vast prowess.

185.s:
vraṇāḥ phaṇe 'bhavaṃs tasya kṛṣṇasyāṅghrivikuṭṭanaiḥ
yatronnatiṃ ca kurute nanāmāsya tataḥ śiraḥ //
185.d:
व्रणाः फणे ऽभवंस् तस्य कृष्णस्याङ्घ्रिविकुट्टनैः
