विनाशाय यथा व्याधिर् आप्तभूतैर् उपेक्षितः ॥
190.m: Kṛṣṇa’s arm expanded inside Keśin’s body, O twice-born ones, / just as a disease neglected by trusted kin grows to destruction.

190.s:
vipāṭitauṣṭho bahulaṃ saphenaṃ rudhiraṃ vaman
sṛkkaṇī vivṛte cakre viśliṣṭe muktabandhane //
190.d:
विपाटितौष्ठो बहुलं सफेनं रुधिरं वमन्
सृक्कणी विवृते चक्रे विश्लिष्टे मुक्तबन्धने ॥
190.m: With his lips torn apart, vomiting abundant frothy blood, / the horse opened his mouth wide as the corners tore away and the joints severed.

190.s:
jagāma dharaṇīṃ pādaiḥ śakṛnmūtraṃ samutsṛjan
svedārdragātraḥ śrāntaś ca niryatnaḥ so 'bhavat tataḥ //
190.d:
जगाम धरणीं पादैः शकृन्मूत्रं समुत्सृजन्
स्वेदार्द्रगात्रः श्रान्तश् च निर्यत्नः सो ऽभवत् ततः ॥
190.m: He fell to the ground with his legs, discharging dung and urine; / with his limbs wet with sweat and exhausted, he then became lifeless.

190.s:
vyāditāsyo mahāraudraḥ so 'suraḥ kṛṣṇabāhunā
nipapāta dvidhābhūto vaidyutena yathā drumaḥ //
190.d:
व्यादितास्यो महारौद्रः सो ऽसुरः कृष्णबाहुना
निपपात द्विधाभूतो वैद्युतेन यथा द्रुमः ॥
190.m: With his mouth gaping wide, that terrible Asura, struck by Kṛṣṇa’s arm, / fell split into two, like a tree struck by lightning.

190.s:
dvipādapṛṣṭhapucchārdhaśravaṇaikākṣanāsike
keśinas te dvidhā bhūte śakale ca virejatuḥ //
190.d:
द्विपादपृष्ठपुच्छार्धश्रवणैकाक्षनासिके
केशिनस् ते द्विधा भूते शकले च विरेजतुः ॥
190.m: Those two halves of Keśin shone, / each possessing two legs, half a back, half a tail, one ear, one eye, and one nostril.

190.s:
hatvā tu keśinaṃ kṛṣṇo muditair gopakair vṛtaḥ
anāyastatanuḥ svastho hasaṃs tatraiva saṃsthitaḥ //
190.d:
हत्वा तु केशिनं कृष्णो मुदितैर् गोपकैर् वृतः
अनायस्ततनुः स्वस्थो हसंस् तत्रैव संस्थितः ॥
190.m: Having slain Keśin, Kṛṣṇa, surrounded by rejoicing cowherd boys, / stood right there, his body unwearied, at ease and smiling.

190.s:
tato gopāś ca gopyaś ca hate keśini vismitāḥ
tuṣṭuvuḥ puṇḍarīkākṣam anurāgamanoramam //
190.d:
ततो गोपाश् च गोप्यश् च हते केशिनि विस्मिताः
तुष्टुवुः पुण्डरीकाक्षम् अनुरागमनोरमम् ॥
190.m: Then, Keśin having been slain, the amazed cowherds and cowherdesses / praised the lotus-eyed one, captivating with affection.

190.s:
āyayau tvarito vipro nārado jaladasthitaḥ
keśinaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā harṣanirbharamānasaḥ //
190.d:
आययौ त्वरितो विप्रो नारदो जलदस्थितः
केशिनं निहतं दृष्ट्वा हर्षनिर्भरमानसः ॥
190.m: The brāhmaṇa Nārada, standing in a cloud, quickly arrived; / seeing Keśin slain, his mind was filled with joy.

190.s:
nārada uvāca
sādhu sādhu jagannātha līlayaiva yad acyuta
nihato 'yaṃ tvayā keśī kleśadas tridivaukasām //
190.d:
नारद उवाच
साधु साधु जगन्नाथ लीलयैव यद् अच्युत
निहतो ऽयं त्वया केशी क्लेशदस् त्रिदिवौकसाम् ॥
190.m: Nārada said: / 'Well done, well done, O Lord of the world, that in mere sport, O Acyuta, / this Keśin, who caused distress to the dwellers of heaven, has been slain by you!

190.s:
sukarmāṇy avatāre tu kṛtāni madhusūdana
yāni vai vismitaṃ cetas toṣam etena me gatam //
190.d:
सुकर्माण्य् अवतारे तु कृतानि मधुसूदन
यानि वै विस्मितं चेतस् तोषम् एतेन मे गतम् ॥
190.m: The good deeds done in this incarnation, O slayer of Madhu, / have astonished my mind and brought satisfaction to it.

190.s:
turagasyāsya śakro 'pi kṛṣṇa devāś ca bibhyati
dhutakesarajālasya hreṣato 'bhrāvalokinaḥ //
190.d:
तुरगस्यास्य शक्रो ऽपि कृष्ण देवाश् च बिभ्यति
धुतकेसरजालस्य ह्रेषतो ऽभ्रावलोकिनः ॥
190.m: Even Śakra and the gods, O Kṛṣṇa, were afraid of this horse / who shook his mane, neighed, and looked up into the clouds.

190.s:
yasmāt tvayaiṣa duṣṭātmā hataḥ keśī janārdana
tasmāt keśavanāmnā tvaṃ loke geyo bhaviṣyasi //
190.d:
यस्मात् त्वयैष दुष्टात्मा हतः केशी जनार्दन
तस्मात् केशवनाम्ना त्वं लोके गेयो भविष्यसि ॥
190.m: Because this wicked Keśin has been slain by you, O Janārdana, / therefore you will be celebrated in the world by the name Keśava.

190.s:
svasty astu te gamiṣyāmi kaṃsayuddhe 'dhunā punaḥ
paraśvo 'haṃ sameṣyāmi tvayā keśiniṣūdana //
190.d:
स्वस्त्य् अस्तु ते गमिष्यामि कंसयुद्धे ऽधुना पुनः
परश्वो ऽहं समेष्यामि त्वया केशिनिषूदन ॥
190.m: May it be well with you; I will go now, and in the fight with Kaṃsa, / the day after tomorrow, I will meet you again, O slayer of Keśin.

190.s:
ugrasenasute kaṃse sānuge vinipātite
bhārāvatārakartā tvaṃ pṛthivyā dharaṇīdhara //
190.d:
उग्रसेनसुते कंसे सानुगे विनिपातिते
भारावतारकर्ता त्वं पृथिव्या धरणीधर ॥
190.m: When Kaṃsa, the son of Ugrasena, has been struck down along with his followers, / you, O upholder of the earth, will remove the burden of the earth.

190.s:
tatrānekaprakāreṇa yuddhāni pṛthivīkṣitām
draṣṭavyāni mayā yuṣmatpraṇītāni janārdana //
190.d:
तत्रानेकप्रकारेण युद्धानि पृथिवीक्षिताम्
द्रष्टव्यानि मया युष्मत्प्रणीतानि जनार्दन ॥
190.m: There I must witness the battles of the earthly rulers in various ways, / brought about by you, O Janārdana.

190.s:
so 'haṃ yāsyāmi govinda devakāryaṃ mahat kṛtam
tvayā sabhājitaś cāhaṃ svasti te 'stu vrajāmy aham //
190.d:
सो ऽहं यास्यामि गोविन्द देवकार्यं महत् कृतम्
त्वया सभाजितश् चाहं स्वस्ति ते ऽस्तु व्रजाम्य् अहम् ॥
190.m: So I will go, O Govinda; a great work for the gods has been accomplished, / and I have been honoured by you; may it be well with you, I depart.'

190.s:
vyāsa uvāca
nārade tu gate kṛṣṇaḥ saha gopair avismitaḥ
viveśa gokulaṃ gopīnetrapānaikabhājanam //
190.d:
व्यास उवाच
नारदे तु गते कृष्णः सह गोपैर् अविस्मितः
विवेश गोकुलं गोपीनेत्रपानैकभाजनम् ॥
190.m: Vyāsa said: / When Nārada had departed, Kṛṣṇa, unastonished, together with the cowherds, / entered the cow-settlement, the sole vessel for drinking in by the eyes of the cowherdesses.

191.s:
vyāsa uvāca
akrūro 'pi viniṣkramya syandanenāśugāminā
kṛṣṇasaṃdarśanāsaktaḥ prayayau nandagokule //
191.d:
व्यास उवाच
अक्रूरो ऽपि विनिष्क्रम्य स्यन्दनेनाशुगामिना
कृष्णसंदर्शनासक्तः प्रययौ नन्दगोकुले ॥
191.m: Vyāsa said: / Akrūra too, having set out on a swift chariot / and intent on seeing Kṛṣṇa, arrived at Nanda’s cow-settlement.

191.s:
cintayām āsa cākrūro nāsti dhanyataro mayā
yo 'ham aṃśāvatīrṇasya mukhaṃ drakṣyāmi cakriṇaḥ //
191.d:
चिन्तयाम् आस चाक्रूरो नास्ति धन्यतरो मया
यो ऽहम् अंशावतीर्णस्य मुखं द्रक्ष्यामि चक्रिणः ॥
191.m: And Akrūra reflected: 'There is none more fortunate than I, / since I will behold the face of the discus-bearer descended as a partial incarnation.

191.s:
adya me saphalaṃ janma suprabhātā ca me niśā
yad unnidrābjapattrākṣaṃ viṣṇor drakṣyāmy aham mukham //
191.d:
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म सुप्रभाता च मे निशा
यद् उन्निद्राब्जपत्त्राक्षं विष्णोर् द्रक्ष्याम्य् अहम् मुखम् ॥
191.m: Today my birth is fruitful, and beautiful is the dawning of my night, / since I will behold the face of Viṣṇu, whose eyes are like fully opened lotus petals.

191.s:
pāpaṃ harati yat puṃsāṃ smṛtaṃ saṃkalpanāmayam
tat puṇḍarīkanayanaṃ viṣṇor drakṣyāmy ahaṃ mukham //
191.d:
पापं हरति यत् पुंसां स्मृतं संकल्पनामयम्
तत् पुण्डरीकनयनं विष्णोर् द्रक्ष्याम्य् अहं मुखम् ॥
191.m: I will behold the lotus-eyed face of Viṣṇu, / which, when remembered, removes the sin born of wrongful thoughts in men.

191.s:
nirjagmuś ca yato vedā vedāṅgāny akhilāni ca
drakṣyāmi yat paraṃ dhāma devānāṃ bhagavanmukham //
191.d:
निर्जग्मुश् च यतो वेदा वेदाङ्गान्य् अखिलानि च
द्रक्ष्यामि यत् परं धाम देवानां भगवन्मुखम् ॥
191.m: I will behold that supreme abode of the gods, the face of the Lord, / from which the Vedas and all the auxiliary limbs of the Veda went forth.

191.s:
yajñeṣu yajñapuruṣaḥ puruṣaiḥ puruṣottamaḥ
ijyate yo 'khilādhāras taṃ drakṣyāmi jagatpatim //
191.d:
यज्ञेषु यज्ञपुरुषः पुरुषैः पुरुषोत्तमः
इज्यते यो ऽखिलाधारस् तं द्रक्ष्यामि जगत्पतिम् ॥
191.m: I will behold that Lord of the world, the support of all, / who is worshipped in sacrifices by men as the sacrifice-person, as Puruṣottama.

191.s:
iṣṭvā yam indro yajñānāṃ śatenāmararājatām
avāpa tam anantādim ahaṃ drakṣyāmi keśavam //
191.d:
इष्ट्वा यम् इन्द्रो यज्ञानां शतेनामरराजताम्
अवाप तम् अनन्तादिम् अहं द्रक्ष्यामि केशवम् ॥
191.m: I will behold Keśava, the beginning of the infinite, worshipping whom / Indra obtained sovereignty over the immortals by a hundred sacrifices.

191.s:
na brahmā nendrarudrāśvivasvādityamarudgaṇāḥ
yasya svarūpaṃ jānanti spṛśaty adya sa me hariḥ //
191.d:
न ब्रह्मा नेन्द्ररुद्राश्विवस्वादित्यमरुद्गणाः
यस्य स्वरूपं जानन्ति स्पृशत्य् अद्य स मे हरिः ॥
191.m: Hari, whose essential nature neither Brahmā, nor Indra, Rudra, the Aśvins, the Vasus, Ādityas, or hosts of Maruts / know, will touch me today.

191.s:
sarvātmā sarvagaḥ sarvaḥ sarvabhūteṣu saṃsthitaḥ
yo bhavaty avyayo vyāpī sa vīkṣyate mayādya ha //
191.d:
सर्वात्मा सर्वगः सर्वः सर्वभूतेषु संस्थितः
यो भवत्य् अव्ययो व्यापी स वीक्ष्यते मयाद्य ह ॥
191.m: He who is the self of all, omnipresent, all-things, residing in all beings, / who is imperishable and all-pervading, will indeed be seen by me today.

191.s:
matsyakūrmavarāhādyaiḥ siṃharūpādibhiḥ sthitam
cakāra yogato yogaṃ sa mām ālāpayiṣyati //
191.d:
मत्स्यकूर्मवराहाद्यैः सिंहरूपादिभिः स्थितम्
चकार योगतो योगं स माम् आलापयिष्यति ॥
191.m: He who, assuming forms such as the fish, tortoise, boar, and lion, / established order through his yoga, will converse with me.'

191.s:
sāṃprataṃ ca jagatsvāmī kāryajāte vraje sthitim
kartuṃ manuṣyatāṃ prāptaḥ svecchādehadhṛg avyayaḥ //
191.d:
सांप्रतं च जगत्स्वामी कार्यजाते व्रजे स्थितिम्
कर्तुं मनुष्यतां प्राप्तः स्वेच्छादेहधृग् अव्ययः ॥
191.m:
And now the Lord of the world, to fulfill his purpose, has attained human form
to dwell in Vraja, assuming a body by his own will, imperishable.

191.s:
yo 'nantaḥ pṛthivīṃ dhatte śikharasthitisaṃsthitām
so 'vatīrṇo jagatyarthe mām akrūreti vakṣyati //
191.d:
यो ऽनन्तः पृथिवीं धत्ते शिखरस्थितिसंस्थिताम्
सो ऽवतीर्णो जगत्यर्थे माम् अक्रूरेति वक्ष्यति ॥
191.m:
He who, as Ananta, bears the earth resting on his hoods,
he has descended for the sake of the world, and will say to me, “Akrūra!”

191.s:
pitṛbandhusuhṛdbhrātṛmātṛbandhumayīm imām
yanmāyāṃ nālam uddhartuṃ jagat tasmai namo namaḥ //
191.d:
पितृबन्धुसुहृद्भ्रातृमातृबन्धुमयीम् इमाम्
यन्मायां नालम् उद्धर्तुं जगत् तस्मै नमो नमः ॥
191.m:
Salutations, salutations to him whose illusory power,
consisting of fathers, kinsmen, friends, brothers, and mothers, the world cannot overcome!

191.s:
taranty avidyāṃ vitatāṃ hṛdi yasmin niveśite
yogamāyām imāṃ martyās tasmai vidyātmane namaḥ //
191.d:
तरन्त्य् अविद्यां विततां हृदि यस्मिन् निवेशिते
योगमायाम् इमां मर्त्यास् तस्मै विद्यात्मने नमः ॥
191.m:
Salutations to him whose self is knowledge, placed in whose heart
mortals cross over this widespread ignorance, this yogamāyā!

191.s:
yajvabhir yajñapuruṣo vāsudevaś ca śāśvataiḥ
vedāntavedibhir viṣṇuḥ procyate yo nato 'smi tam //
191.d:
यज्वभिर् यज्ञपुरुषो वासुदेवश् च शाश्वतैः
वेदान्तवेदिभिर् विष्णुः प्रोच्यते यो नतो ऽस्मि तम् ॥
191.m:
I bow down to him who is proclaimed as the Sacrifice-Puruṣa by sacrificers,
as eternal Vāsudeva, and as Viṣṇu by knowers of the Vedānta.

191.s:
tathā yatra jagad dhāmni dhāryate ca pratiṣṭhitam
sadasattvaṃ sa sattvena mayy asau yātu saumyatām //
191.d:
तथा यत्र जगद् धाम्नि धार्यते च प्रतिष्ठितम्
सदसत्त्वं स सत्त्वेन मय्य् असौ यातु सौम्यताम् ॥
191.m:
Likewise, in which abode the world is held and established,
he who is being and non-being, may he, through his sattva, show benevolence toward me.

191.s:
smṛte sakalakalyāṇabhājanaṃ yatra jāyate
puruṣapravaraṃ nityaṃ vrajāmi śaraṇaṃ harim //
191.d:
स्मृते सकलकल्याणभाजनं यत्र जायते
पुरुषप्रवरं नित्यं व्रजामि शरणं हरिम् ॥
191.m:
When he is remembered, one becomes a vessel of all auspiciousness;
I perpetually take refuge in Hari, the foremost puruṣa.

191.s:
vyāsa uvāca
itthaṃ sa cintayan viṣṇuṃ bhaktinamrātmamānasaḥ
akrūro gokulaṃ prāptaḥ kiṃcit sūrye virājati //
191.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्थं स चिन्तयन् विष्णुं भक्तिनम्रात्ममानसः
अक्रूरो गोकुलं प्राप्तः किंचित् सूर्ये विराजति ॥
191.m:
Vyāsa said:
Thus meditating upon Viṣṇu, his mind humbled in devotion,
Akrūra reached Gokula as the sun was still shining a little.

191.s:
sa dadarśa tadā tatra kṛṣṇam ādohane gavām
vatsamadhyagataṃ phullanīlotpaladalacchavim //
191.d:
स ददर्श तदा तत्र कृष्णम् आदोहने गवाम्
वत्समध्यगतं फुल्लनीलोत्पलदलच्छविम् ॥
191.m:
He then saw Kṛṣṇa there at the milking-place of the cows,
standing among the calves, having the luster of a blooming blue lotus petal,

191.s:
praphullapadmapattrākṣaṃ śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam
pralambabāhum āyāmatuṅgorasthalam unnasam //
191.d:
प्रफुल्लपद्मपत्त्राक्षं श्रीवत्साङ्कितवक्षसम्
प्रलम्बबाहुम् आयामतुङ्गोरस्थलम् उन्नसम् ॥
191.m:
with eyes like fully blossomed lotus petals, a chest marked with the Śrīvatsa,
long arms, an expansive and prominent chest, and a raised nose,

191.s:
savilāsasmitādhāraṃ bibhrāṇaṃ mukhapaṅkajam
tuṅgaraktanakhaṃ padbhyāṃ dharaṇyāṃ supratiṣṭhitam //
191.d:
सविलासस्मिताधारं बिभ्राणं मुखपङ्कजम्
तुङ्गरक्तनखं पद्भ्यां धरण्यां सुप्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
191.m:
bearing a lotus-face that was the receptacle of playful smiles,
with elevated red nails, firmly planted on the earth with both feet,

191.s:
bibhrāṇaṃ vāsasī pīte vanyapuṣpavibhūṣitam
sāndranīlalatāhastaṃ sitāmbhojāvataṃsakam //
191.d:
बिभ्राणं वाससी पीते वन्यपुष्पविभूषितम्
सान्द्रनीललताहस्तं सिताम्भोजावतंसकम् ॥
191.m:
wearing two yellow garments, adorned with wild flowers,
holding a dense blue vine in his hand, and wearing a white lotus as an ear-ornament.

191.s:
haṃsendukundadhavalaṃ nīlāmbaradharaṃ dvijāḥ
tasyānu balabhadraṃ ca dadarśa yadunandanam //
191.d:
हंसेन्दुकुन्दधवलं नीलाम्बरधरं द्विजाः
तस्यानु बलभद्रं च ददर्श यदुनन्दनम् ॥
191.m:
And behind him, O twice-born, he saw Balabhadra, the delight of the Yadus,
white as a swan, the moon, and jasmine, and wearing a blue garment,

191.s:
prāṃśum uttuṅgabāhuṃ ca vikāśimukhapaṅkajam
meghamālāparivṛtaṃ kailāsādrim ivāparam //
191.d:
प्रांशुम् उत्तुङ्गबाहुं च विकाशिमुखपङ्कजम्
मेघमालापरिवृतं कैलासाद्रिम् इवापरम् ॥
191.m:
tall, with long arms, an open lotus-face,
resembling another Mount Kailāsa enveloped by a garland of clouds.

191.s:
tau dṛṣṭvā vikasadvaktrasarojaḥ sa mahāmatiḥ
pulakāñcitasarvāṅgas tadākrūro 'bhavad dvijāḥ //
191.d:
तौ दृष्ट्वा विकसद्वक्त्रसरोजः स महामतिः
पुलकाञ्चितसर्वाङ्गस् तदाक्रूरो ऽभवद् द्विजाः ॥
191.m:
Seeing the two of them, O twice-born, the high-minded Akrūra’s lotus-face bloomed,
and all his limbs bristled with thrills.

191.s:
ya etat paramaṃ dhāma etat tat paramaṃ padam
abhavad vāsudevo 'sau dvidhā yo 'yaṃ vyavasthitaḥ //
191.d:
य एतत् परमं धाम एतत् तत् परमं पदम्
अभवद् वासुदेवो ऽसौ द्विधा यो ऽयं व्यवस्थितः ॥
191.m:
[He thought:] “He who is this supreme abode, this supreme state,
this Vāsudeva, is present here divided into two forms.

191.s:
sāphalyam akṣṇor yugapan mamāstu
dṛṣṭe jagaddhātari hāsam uccaiḥ
apy aṅgam etad bhagavatprasādād
dattāṅgasaṅge phalavartma tat syāt
191.d:
साफल्यम् अक्ष्णोर् युगपन् ममास्तु
दृष्टे जगद्धातरि हासम् उच्चैः
अप्य् अङ्गम् एतद् भगवत्प्रसादाद्
दत्ताङ्गसङ्गे फलवर्त्म तत् स्यात्
191.m:
May both my eyes attain fulfillment at once
upon seeing the Creator of the world, whose smile is radiant!
And may this body of mine, through the grace of the Blessed One,
find the path of fulfillment when granted contact with his limbs!

191.s:
adyaiva spṛṣṭvā mama hastapadmaṃ
kariṣyati śrīmadanantamūrtiḥ
yasyāṅgulisparśahatākhilāghair
avāpyate siddhir anuttamā naraiḥ
191.d:
अद्यैव स्पृष्ट्वा मम हस्तपद्मं
करिष्यति श्रीमदनन्तमूर्तिः
यस्याङ्गुलिस्पर्शहताखिलाघैर्
अवाप्यते सिद्धिर् अनुत्तमा नरैः
191.m:
This very day the glorious one of infinite forms
will touch my lotus-hand,
by the touch of whose fingers men, having all sins destroyed,
attain unexcelled perfection.

191.s:
tathāśvirudrendravasupraṇītā
devāḥ prayacchanti varaṃ prahṛṣṭāḥ
cakraṃ ghnatā daityapater hṛtāni
daityāṅganānāṃ nayanāntarāṇi
191.d:
तथाश्विरुद्रेन्द्रवसुप्रणीता
देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति वरं प्रहृष्टाः
चक्रं घ्नता दैत्यपतेर् हृतानि
दैत्याङ्गनानां नयनान्तराणि
191.m:
Likewise, the gods led by the Aśvins, Rudras, Indras, and Vasus
rejoicingly grant boons [to him],
whose disc, slaying the lord of the Daityas,
snatched away the pupils from the eyes of Daitya women.

191.s:
yatrāmbu vinyasya balir manobhyām
avāpa bhogān vasudhātalasthaḥ
tathāmareśas tridaśādhipatyaṃ
manvantaraṃ pūrṇam avāpa śakraḥ
191.d:
यत्राम्बु विन्यस्य बलिर् मनोभ्याम्
अवाप भोगान् वसुधातलस्थः
तथामरेशस् त्रिदशाधिपत्यं
मन्वन्तरं पूर्णम् अवाप शक्रः
191.m:
Placing water upon [whose feet] with his mind, Bali,
though dwelling on the earthly realm, obtained pleasures;
and Śakra, the lord of the immortals, obtained sovereign rule over the thirty [gods]
for a complete manvantara.

191.s:
atheśa māṃ kaṃsaparigraheṇa
doṣāspadībhūtam adoṣayuktam
kartā na mānopahitaṃ dhig astu
yasmān manaḥ sādhubahiṣkṛto yaḥ
191.d:
अथेश मां कंसपरिग्रहेण
दोषास्पदीभूतम् अदोषयुक्तम्
कर्ता न मानोपहितं धिग् अस्तु
यस्मान् मनः साधुबहिष्कृतो यः
191.m:
Now, O Lord, although I am guiltless, because of my acceptance by Kaṃsa
I have become an object of blame; will he not make me honored?
Fie [on me], whose mind is cast out by the virtuous!

191.s:
jñānātmakasyākhilasattvarāśer
vyāvṛttadoṣasya sadāsphuṭasya
kiṃ vā jagaty atra samastapuṃsām
ajñātam asyāsti hṛdi sthitasya
191.d:
ज्ञानात्मकस्याखिलसत्त्वराशेर्
व्यावृत्तदोषस्य सदास्फुटस्य
किं वा जगत्य् अत्र समस्तपुंसाम्
अज्ञातम् अस्यास्ति हृदि स्थितस्य
191.m:
For him who consists of knowledge, who is the aggregate of all beings,
free from fault, ever manifest,
who dwells in the hearts of all men,
what indeed is unknown in this world?

191.s:
tasmād ahaṃ bhaktivinamragātro
vrajāmi viśveśvaram īśvarāṇām
aṃśāvatāraṃ puruṣottamasya
anādimadhyāntam ajasya viṣṇoḥ
191.d:
तस्माद् अहं भक्तिविनम्रगात्रो
व्रजामि विश्वेश्वरम् ईश्वराणाम्
अंशावतारं पुरुषोत्तमस्य
अनादिमध्यान्तम् अजस्य विष्णोः
191.m:
Therefore, with my limbs bent in devotion,
I go to the Lord of the universe, the Ruler of rulers,
the partial incarnation of Puruṣottama,
the unborn Viṣṇu, who has no beginning, middle, or end.”

192.s:
vyāsa uvāca
cintayann iti govindam upagamya sa yādavaḥ
akrūro 'smīti caraṇau nanāma śirasā hareḥ //
192.d:
व्यास उवाच
चिन्तयन्न् इति गोविन्दम् उपगम्य स यादवः
अक्रूरो ऽस्मीति चरणौ ननाम शिरसा हरेः ॥
192.m:
Vyāsa said:
Meditating thus upon Govinda, the Yādava approached,
and saying, “I am Akrūra,” he bowed down with his head to Hari’s feet.

192.s:
so 'py enaṃ dhvajavajrābjakṛtacihnena pāṇinā
saṃspṛśyākṛṣya ca prītyā sugāḍhaṃ pariṣasvaje //
192.d:
सो ऽप्य् एनं ध्वजवज्राब्जकृतचिह्नेन पाणिना
संस्पृश्याकृष्य च प्रीत्या सुगाढं परिषस्वजे ॥
192.m:
And he too, touching him with his hand marked with the banner, thunderbolt, and lotus,
drew him close, and embraced him tightly with affection.

192.s:
kṛtasaṃvadanau tena yathāvad balakeśavau
tataḥ praviṣṭau sahasā tam ādāyātmamandiram //
192.d:
कृतसंवदनौ तेन यथावद् बलकेशवौ
ततः प्रविष्टौ सहसा तम् आदायात्ममन्दिरम् ॥
192.m:
Having duly exchanged greetings with him,
Bala and Keśava then swiftly took him into their home.

192.s:
saha tābhyāṃ tadākrūraḥ kṛtasaṃvandanādikaḥ
bhuktabhojyo yathānyāyam ācacakṣe tatas tayoḥ //
192.d:
सह ताभ्यां तदाक्रूरः कृतसंवन्दनादिकः
भुक्तभोज्यो यथान्यायम् आचचक्षे ततस् तयोः ॥
192.m:
Together with the two of them, having performed salutations and other rites,
Akrūra, having eaten food as was proper, then told both of them

192.s:
yathā nirbhartsitas tena kaṃsenānakadundubhiḥ
yathā ca devakī devī dānavena durātmanā //
192.d:
यथा निर्भर्त्सितस् तेन कंसेनानकदुन्दुभिः
यथा च देवकी देवी दानवेन दुरात्मना ॥
192.m:
how Ānakadundubhi had been reviled by Kaṃsa,
and how Devakī had been abused by that evil-minded Dānava,

192.s:
ugrasene yathā kaṃsaḥ sa durātmā ca vartate
yaṃ caivārthaṃ samuddiśya kaṃsena sa visarjitaḥ //
192.d:
उग्रसेने यथा कंसः स दुरात्मा च वर्तते
यं चैवार्थं समुद्दिश्य कंसेन स विसर्जितः ॥
192.m:
how that evil-souled Kaṃsa treated Ugrasena,
and for what purpose he himself had been dispatched by Kaṃsa.

192.s:
tat sarvaṃ vistarāc chrutvā bhagavān keśisūdanaḥ
uvācākhilam etat tu jñātaṃ dānapate mayā //
192.d:
तत् सर्वं विस्तराच् छ्रुत्वा भगवान् केशिसूदनः
उवाचाखिलम् एतत् तु ज्ञातं दानपते मया ॥
192.m:
Having heard all that in detail, the Blessed One, the slayer of Keśin,
said: “All this is indeed known to me, O lord of gifts.

192.s:
kariṣye ca mahābhāga yad atraupāyikaṃ matam
vicintyaṃ nānyathaitat te viddhi kaṃsaṃ hataṃ mayā //
192.d:
करिष्ये च महाभाग यद् अत्रौपायिकं मतम्
विचिन्त्यं नान्यथैतत् ते विद्धि कंसं हतं मया ॥
192.m:
And, O fortunate one, I will do what is deemed expedient in this matter.
You need not think otherwise about this; know Kaṃsa to be already slain by me.

192.s:
ahaṃ rāmaś ca mathurāṃ śvo yāsyāvaḥ samaṃ tvayā
gopavṛddhāś ca yāsyanti ādāyopāyanaṃ bahu //
192.d:
अहं रामश् च मथुरां श्वो यास्यावः समं त्वया
गोपवृद्धाश् च यास्यन्ति आदायोपायनं बहु ॥
192.m:
Rāma and I shall go to Mathurā tomorrow along with you;
and the elders among the cowherds will go, taking many offerings.

192.s:
niśeyaṃ nīyatāṃ vīra na cintāṃ kartum arhasi
trirātrābhyantare kaṃsaṃ haniṣyāmi sahānugam //
192.d:
निशेयं नीयतां वीर न चिन्तां कर्तुम् अर्हसि
त्रिरात्राभ्यन्तरे कंसं हनिष्यामि सहानुगम् ॥
192.m:
Spend this night [here], O hero; you ought not to worry.
Within three nights I will kill Kaṃsa along with his followers.”

192.s:
vyāsa uvāca
samādiśya tato gopān akrūro 'pi sakeśavaḥ
suṣvāpa balabhadraś ca nandagopagṛhe gataḥ //
192.d:
व्यास उवाच
समादिश्य ततो गोपान् अक्रूरो ऽपि सकेशवः
सुष्वाप बलभद्रश् च नन्दगोपगृहे गतः ॥
192.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having then instructed the cowherds, Akrūra, accompanied by Keśava
and Balabhadra, went to Nandagopa’s house and slept.

192.s:
tataḥ prabhāte vimale rāmakṛṣṇau mahābalau
akrūreṇa samaṃ gantum udyatau mathurāṃ purīm //
192.d:
ततः प्रभाते विमले रामकृष्णौ महाबलौ
अक्रूरेण समं गन्तुम् उद्यतौ मथुरां पुरीम् ॥
192.m:
Then, at clear dawn, Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, of mighty strength,
prepared to depart with Akrūra for the city of Mathurā.

192.s:
dṛṣṭvā gopījanaḥ sāsraḥ ślathadvalayabāhukaḥ
niśvasaṃś cātiduḥkhārtaḥ prāha cedaṃ parasparam //
192.d:
दृष्ट्वा गोपीजनः सास्रः श्लथद्वलयबाहुकः
निश्वसंश् चातिदुःखार्तः प्राह चेदं परस्परम् ॥
192.m:
Seeing them, the gopīs, weeping, with bangles slipping from their arms,
sighing and exceedingly stricken with grief, said this to one another:

192.s:
mathurāṃ prāpya govindaḥ kathaṃ gokulam eṣyati
nāgarastrīkalālāpamadhu śrotreṇa pāsyati //
192.d:
मथुरां प्राप्य गोविन्दः कथं गोकुलम् एष्यति
नागरस्त्रीकलालापमधु श्रोत्रेण पास्यति ॥
192.m:
“Having reached Mathurā, how will Govinda ever return to Gokula?
He will drink with his ear the honey of the sweet speech of city women.

192.s:
vilāsivākyajāteṣu nāgarīṇāṃ kṛtāspadam
cittam asya kathaṃ grāmyagopagopīṣu yāsyati //
192.d:
विलासिवाक्यजातेषु नागरीणां कृतास्पदम्
चित्तम् अस्य कथं ग्राम्यगोपगोपीषु यास्यति ॥
192.m:
His mind, having found a place among the playful words of the city women,
how will it ever turn to rustic cowherd boys and gopīs?

192.s:
sāraṃ samastagoṣṭhasya vidhinā haratā harim
prahṛtaṃ gopayoṣitsu nighṛṇena durātmanā //
192.d:
सारं समस्तगोष्ठस्य विधिना हरता हरिम्
प्रहृतं गोपयोषित्सु निघृणेन दुरात्मना ॥
192.m:
By taking Hari away, the essence of the entire cowherd settlement,
a blow has been struck at the cowherd women by merciless, wicked Fate!

192.s:
bhāvagarbhasmitaṃ vākyaṃ vilāsalalitā gatiḥ
nāgarīṇām atīvaitat kaṭākṣekṣitam eva tu //
192.d:
भावगर्भस्मितं वाक्यं विलासललिता गतिः
नागरीणाम् अतीवैतत् कटाक्षेक्षितम् एव तु ॥
192.m:
The speech laden with romantic sentiment and smiles, the graceful, playful gait
of the city women, and especially their sidelong glances—

192.s:
grāmyo harir ayaṃ tāsāṃ vilāsanigaḍair yataḥ
bhavatīnāṃ punaḥ pārśvaṃ kayā yuktyā sameṣyati //
192.d:
ग्राम्यो हरिर् अयं तासां विलासनिगडैर् यतः
भवतीनां पुनः पार्श्वं कया युक्त्या समेष्यति ॥
192.m:
since this rustic Hari is bound by their playful fetters,
by what means will he ever return to you again?

192.s:
eṣo hi ratham āruhya mathurāṃ yāti keśavaḥ
akrūrakrūrakeṇāpi hatāśena pratāritaḥ //
192.d:
एषो हि रथम् आरुह्य मथुरां याति केशवः
अक्रूरक्रूरकेणापि हताशेन प्रतारितः ॥
192.m:
For Keśava is mounting the chariot and going to Mathurā,
lured away even by that wretched, cruel Akrūra!

192.s:
kiṃ na vetti nṛśaṃso 'yam anurāgaparaṃ janam
yenemam akṣarāhlādaṃ nayaty anyatra no harim //
192.d:
किं न वेत्ति नृशंसो ऽयम् अनुरागपरं जनम्
येनेमम् अक्षराह्लादं नयत्य् अन्यत्र नो हरिम् ॥
192.m:
Does this cruel man not know people who are devoted with passionate love,
since he is carrying our Hari, this imperishable delight, somewhere else?

192.s:
eṣa rāmeṇa sahitaḥ prayāty atyantanirghṛṇaḥ
ratham āruhya govindas tvaryatām asya vāraṇe //
192.d:
एष रामेण सहितः प्रयात्य् अत्यन्तनिर्घृणः
रथम् आरुह्य गोविन्दस् त्वर्यताम् अस्य वारणे ॥
192.m:
Extremely heartless, he is departing along with Rāma,
having mounted the chariot; Govinda must be stopped at once!

192.s:
gurūṇām agrato vaktuṃ kiṃ bravīṣi na naḥ kṣamam
guravaḥ kiṃ kariṣyanti dagdhānāṃ virahāgninā //
192.d:
गुरूणाम् अग्रतो वक्तुं किं ब्रवीषि न नः क्षमम्
गुरवः किं करिष्यन्ति दग्धानां विरहाग्निना ॥
192.m:
Why do you say, ‘It is not proper for us to speak before our elders’?
What will elders do to those who are already burned by the fire of separation?

192.s:
nandagopamukhā gopā gantum ete samudyatāḥ
nodyamaṃ kurute kaścid govindavinivartane //
192.d:
नन्दगोपमुखा गोपा गन्तुम् एते समुद्यताः
नोद्यमं कुरुते कश्चिद् गोविन्दविनिवर्तने ॥
192.m:
These cowherds headed by Nandagopa are prepared to go;
not one of them makes an effort to turn Govinda back!”

192.s:
suprabhātādya rajanī mathurāvāsiyoṣitām
yāsām acyutavaktrābje yāti netrālibhogyatām //
192.d:
सुप्रभाताद्य रजनी मथुरावासियोषिताम्
यासाम् अच्युतवक्त्राब्जे याति नेत्रालिभोग्यताम् ॥
192.m: “Today a fair dawn has broken over the night of the women residing in Mathurā, / whose bee-like eyes come to feast upon the lotus-face of Acyuta.

192.s:
dhanyās te pathi ye kṛṣṇam ito yāntam avāritāḥ
udvahiṣyanti paśyantaḥ svadehaṃ pulakāñcitam //
192.d:
धन्यास् ते पथि ये कृष्णम् इतो यान्तम् अवारिताः
उद्वहिष्यन्ति पश्यन्तः स्वदेहं पुलकाञ्चितम् ॥
192.m: Blessed are those along the road who, unobstructed, as they behold Kṛṣṇa going hence, / will bear their bodies bristling with horripilation!

192.s:
mathurānagarīpauranayanānāṃ mahotsavaḥ
govindavadanālokād atīvādya bhaviṣyati //
192.d:
मथुरानगरीपौरनयनानां महोत्सवः
गोविन्दवदनालोकाद् अतीवाद्य भविष्यति ॥
192.m: A great festival for the eyes of the citizens of Mathurā city / will take place today from the sight of Govinda's face!

192.s:
ko nu svapnaḥ sabhāgyābhir dṛṣṭas tābhir adhokṣajam
vistārikāntanayanā yā drakṣyanty anivāritam //
192.d:
को नु स्वप्नः सभाग्याभिर् दृष्टस् ताभिर् अधोक्षजम्
विस्तारिकान्तनयना या द्रक्ष्यन्त्य् अनिवारितम् ॥
192.m: What fortunate dream was seen by those women who, / with wide, beautiful eyes, will behold Adhokṣaja unhindered?

192.s:
aho gopījanasyāsya darśayitvā mahānidhim
uddhṛtāny adya netrāṇi vidhātrākaruṇātmanā //
192.d:
अहो गोपीजनस्यास्य दर्शयित्वा महानिधिम्
उद्धृतान्य् अद्य नेत्राणि विधात्राकरुणात्मना ॥
192.m: Alas! Having shown a great treasure to these gopīs, / the eyes of today have been plucked out by the pitiless Creator!

192.s:
anurāgeṇa śaithilyam asmāsu vrajato hareḥ
śaithilyam upayānty āśu kareṣu valayāny api //
192.d:
अनुरागेण शैथिल्यम् अस्मासु व्रजतो हरेः
शैथिल्यम् उपयान्त्य् आशु करेषु वलयान्य् अपि ॥
192.m: As Hari departs, our affection undergoes slackening; / even the bracelets upon our wrists swiftly slip and grow loose!”

192.s:
akrūraḥ krūrahṛdayaḥ śīghraṃ prerayate hayān
evam ārtāsu yoṣitsu ghṛṇā kasya na jāyate //
192.d:
अक्रूरः क्रूरहृदयः शीघ्रं प्रेरयते हयान्
एवम् आर्तासु योषित्सु घृणा कस्य न जायते ॥
192.m: Akrūra, cruel-hearted, swiftly urges on the horses. / When women are thus distressed, in whom does pity not arise?

192.s:
he he kṛṣṇa rathasyoccaiś cakrareṇur nirīkṣyatām
dūrīkṛto harir yena so 'pi reṇur na lakṣyate //
192.d:
हे हे कृष्ण रथस्योच्चैश् चक्ररेणुर् निरीक्ष्यताम्
दूरीकृतो हरिर् येन सो ऽपि रेणुर् न लक्ष्यते ॥
192.m: “O Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa! Look at the chariot's wheel-dust rising high! / Even that dust by which Hari is hidden from view can no longer be seen!”

192.s:
ity evam atihārdena gopījananirīkṣitaḥ
tatyāja vrajabhūbhāgaṃ saha rāmeṇa keśavaḥ //
192.d:
इत्य् एवम् अतिहार्देन गोपीजननिरीक्षितः
तत्याज व्रजभूभागं सह रामेण केशवः ॥
192.m: Thus gazed upon with intense affection by the gopīs, / Keśava, together with Rāma, departed from the region of Vraja.

192.s:
gacchanto javanāśvena rathena yamunātaṭam
prāptā madhyāhnasamaye rāmākrūrajanārdanāḥ //
192.d:
गच्छन्तो जवनाश्वेन रथेन यमुनातटम्
प्राप्ता मध्याह्नसमये रामाक्रूरजनार्दनाः ॥
192.m: Proceeding in the chariot drawn by swift horses to the bank of the Yamunā, / Rāma, Akrūra, and Janārdana arrived at midday.

192.s:
athāha kṛṣṇam akrūro bhavadbhyāṃ tāvad āsyatām
yāvat karomi kālindyām āhnikārhaṇam ambhasi //
192.d:
अथाह कृष्णम् अक्रूरो भवद्भ्यां तावद् आस्यताम्
यावत् करोमि कालिन्द्याम् आह्निकार्हणम् अम्भसि ॥
192.m: Then Akrūra said to Kṛṣṇa: “May you both remain here / while I perform my daily worship in the waters of the Kālindī.”

192.s:
tathety ukte tataḥ snātaḥ svācāntaḥ sa mahāmatiḥ
dadhyau brahma paraṃ viprāḥ praviśya yamunājale //
192.d:
तथेत्य् उक्ते ततः स्नातः स्वाचान्तः स महामतिः
दध्यौ ब्रह्म परं विप्राः प्रविश्य यमुनाजले ॥
192.m: When [Kṛṣṇa] said, “So be it,” that wise man bathed, rinsed his mouth, / entered the waters of the Yamunā, O twice-born ones, and meditated on the supreme Brahman.

192.s:
phaṇāsahasramālāḍhyaṃ balabhadraṃ dadarśa saḥ
kundāmalāṅgam unnidrapadmapattrāyatekṣaṇam //
192.d:
फणासहस्रमालाढ्यं बलभद्रं ददर्श सः
कुन्दामलाङ्गम् उन्निद्रपद्मपत्त्रायतेक्षणम् ॥
192.m: He beheld Balabhadra endowed with a garland of a thousand hoods, / his limbs pure white like the kunda flower, his long eyes like the petals of a blooming lotus,

192.s:
vṛtaṃ vāsukiḍimbhaughair mahadbhiḥ pavanāśibhiḥ
saṃstūyamānam udgandhivanamālāvibhūṣitam //
192.d:
वृतं वासुकिडिम्भौघैर् महद्भिः पवनाशिभिः
संस्तूयमानम् उद्गन्धिवनमालाविभूषितम् ॥
192.m: surrounded by the great offspring of Vāsuki that feed on wind, / being praised with hymns, adorned with a fragrant garland of wild flowers,

192.s:
dadhānam asite vastre cārurūpāvataṃsakam
cārukuṇḍalinaṃ mattam antarjalatale sthitam //
192.d:
दधानम् असिते वस्त्रे चारुरूपावतंसकम्
चारुकुण्डलिनं मत्तम् अन्तर्जलतले स्थितम् ॥
192.m: wearing dark garments, with a graceful crest-ornament, / possessing lovely earrings, intoxicated, situated beneath the surface of the water.

192.s:
tasyotsaṅge ghanaśyāmam ātāmrāyatalocanam
caturbāhum udārāṅgaṃ cakrādyāyudhabhūṣaṇam //
192.d:
तस्योत्सङ्गे घनश्यामम् आताम्रायतलोचनम्
चतुर्बाहुम् उदाराङ्गं चक्राद्यायुधभूषणम् ॥
192.m: On his lap [he beheld Hari], dark as a raincloud, with long, reddish eyes, / four-armed, noble of limb, adorned with weapons such as the discus,

192.s:
pīte vasānaṃ vasane citramālyavibhūṣitam
śakracāpataḍinmālāvicitram iva toyadam //
192.d:
पीते वसानं वसने चित्रमाल्यविभूषितम्
शक्रचापतडिन्मालाविचित्रम् इव तोयदम् ॥
192.m: clothed in yellow garments, adorned with diverse garlands, / like a cloud variegated by a rainbow and flashes of lightning,

192.s:
śrīvatsavakṣasaṃ cārukeyūramukuṭojjvalam
dadarśa kṛṣṇam akliṣṭaṃ puṇḍarīkāvataṃsakam //
192.d:
श्रीवत्सवक्षसं चारुकेयूरमुकुटोज्ज्वलम्
ददर्श कृष्णम् अक्लिष्टं पुण्डरीकावतंसकम् ॥
192.m: his chest marked with the Śrīvatsa, radiant with beautiful armlets and a diadem; / he saw Kṛṣṇa, untiring in action, wearing a lotus as an ear-ornament,

192.s:
sanandanādyair munibhiḥ siddhayogair akalmaṣaiḥ
saṃcintyamānaṃ manasā nāsāgranyastalocanaiḥ //
192.d:
सनन्दनाद्यैर् मुनिभिः सिद्धयोगैर् अकल्मषैः
संचिन्त्यमानं मनसा नासाग्रन्यस्तलोचनैः ॥
192.m: being contemplated in mind by sages such as Sanandana, / who were accomplished in yoga and free from taint, their eyes fixed on the tips of their noses.

192.s:
balakṛṣṇau tadākrūraḥ pratyabhijñāya vismitaḥ
acintayad atho śīghraṃ katham atrāgatāv iti //
192.d:
बलकृष्णौ तदाक्रूरः प्रत्यभिज्ञाय विस्मितः
अचिन्तयद् अथो शीघ्रं कथम् अत्रागताव् इति ॥
192.m: Recognizing Bala and Kṛṣṇa, Akrūra was astonished / and then swiftly thought: “How have they come here?”

192.s:
vivakṣoḥ stambhayām āsa vācaṃ tasya janārdanaḥ
tato niṣkramya salilād ratham abhyāgataḥ punaḥ //
192.d:
विवक्षोः स्तम्भयाम् आस वाचं तस्य जनार्दनः
ततो निष्क्रम्य सलिलाद् रथम् अभ्यागतः पुनः ॥
192.m: As he wished to speak, Janārdana paralyzed his voice; / then, emerging from the water, he approached the chariot once more.

192.s:
dadarśa tatra caivobhau rathasyopari saṃsthitau
rāmakṛṣṇau yathā pūrvaṃ manuṣyavapuṣānvitau //
192.d:
ददर्श तत्र चैवोभौ रथस्योपरि संस्थितौ
रामकृष्णौ यथा पूर्वं मनुष्यवपुषान्वितौ ॥
192.m: And there he beheld them both sitting upon the chariot, / Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, endowed with human forms just as before.

192.s:
nimagnaś ca punas toye dadṛśe sa tathaiva tau
saṃstūyamānau gandharvair munisiddhamahoragaiḥ //
192.d:
निमग्नश् च पुनस् तोये ददृशे स तथैव तौ
संस्तूयमानौ गन्धर्वैर् मुनिसिद्धमहोरगैः ॥
192.m: Plunging once more into the water, he saw the two just as before, / being praised with hymns by gandharvas, sages, siddhas, and great serpents.

192.s:
tato vijñātasadbhāvaḥ sa tu dānapatis tadā
tuṣṭāva sarvavijñānamayam acyutam īśvaram //
192.d:
ततो विज्ञातसद्भावः स तु दानपतिस् तदा
तुष्टाव सर्वविज्ञानमयम् अच्युतम् ईश्वरम् ॥
192.m: Then, having realized the true reality, that lord of charity / praised Acyuta, the Lord who consists of all wisdom:

192.s:
akrūra uvāca
tanmātrarūpiṇe 'cintyamahimne paramātmane
vyāpine naikarūpaikasvarūpāya namo namaḥ //
192.d:
अक्रूर उवाच
तन्मात्ररूपिणे ऽचिन्त्यमहिम्ने परमात्मने
व्यापिने नैकरूपैकस्वरूपाय नमो नमः ॥
192.m: Akrūra said: / “Salutations, salutations to you whose form is the subtle elements, of inconceivable majesty, the supreme self, / all-pervading, whose single essential nature possesses manifold forms!

192.s:
śabdarūpāya te 'cintyahavirbhūtāya te namaḥ
namo vijñānarūpāya parāya prakṛteḥ prabho //
192.d:
शब्दरूपाय ते ऽचिन्त्यहविर्भूताय ते नमः
नमो विज्ञानरूपाय पराय प्रकृतेः प्रभो ॥
192.m: Salutations to you whose form is sound, to you who have become the inconceivable oblation; / salutations to you whose form is wisdom, who are beyond prakṛti, O Lord!

192.s:
bhūtātmā cendriyātmā ca pradhānātmā tathā bhavān
ātmā ca paramātmā ca tvam ekaḥ pañcadhā sthitaḥ //
192.d:
भूतात्मा चेन्द्रियात्मा च प्रधानात्मा तथा भवान्
आत्मा च परमात्मा च त्वम् एकः पञ्चधा स्थितः ॥
192.m: You are the self of the elements, the self of the senses, and likewise the self of pradhāna; / you are the self and the supreme self: you, the one, abide in fivefold division.

192.s:
prasīda sarvadharmātman kṣarākṣara maheśvara
brahmaviṣṇuśivādyābhiḥ kalpanābhir udīritaḥ //
192.d:
प्रसीद सर्वधर्मात्मन् क्षराक्षर महेश्वर
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवाद्याभिः कल्पनाभिर् उदीरितः ॥
192.m: Be gracious, O self of all dharma, the perishable and the imperishable, O great lord, / designated by the conceptions of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the rest!

192.s:
anākhyeyasvarūpātmann anākhyeyaprayojana
anākhyeyābhidhāna tvāṃ nato 'smi parameśvaram //
192.d:
अनाख्येयस्वरूपात्मन्न् अनाख्येयप्रयोजन
अनाख्येयाभिधान त्वां नतो ऽस्मि परमेश्वरम् ॥
192.m: O you whose essential nature is ineffable, whose purpose is ineffable, / whose name is ineffable, I bow to you, the supreme lord!

192.s:
na yatra nātha vidyante nāmajātyādikalpanāḥ
tad brahma paramaṃ nityam avikāri bhavān ajaḥ //
192.d:
न यत्र नाथ विद्यन्ते नामजात्यादिकल्पनाः
तद् ब्रह्म परमं नित्यम् अविकारि भवान् अजः ॥
192.m: Where no conceptual constructions of name, genus, and so forth exist, O Lord, / that is the supreme, eternal, immutable Brahman; you are the unborn one.

192.s:
na kalpanām ṛte 'rthasya sarvasyādhigamo yataḥ
tataḥ kṛṣṇācyutānanta viṣṇusaṃjñābhir īḍyase //
192.d:
न कल्पनाम् ऋते ऽर्थस्य सर्वस्याधिगमो यतः
ततः कृष्णाच्युतानन्त विष्णुसंज्ञाभिर् ईड्यसे ॥
192.m: Because without conceptual construction no meaning whatsoever can be apprehended, / therefore you are praised under the appellations of Kṛṣṇa, Acyuta, Ananta, and Viṣṇu.

192.s:
sarvātmaṃs tvam aja vikalpanābhir etair
devās tvaṃ jagad akhilaṃ tvam eva viśvam
viśvātmaṃs tvam ativikārabhedahīnaḥ
sarvasmin nahi bhavato 'sti kiṃcid anyat
192.d:
सर्वात्मंस् त्वम् अज विकल्पनाभिर् एतैर्
देवास् त्वं जगद् अखिलं त्वम् एव विश्वम्
विश्वात्मंस् त्वम् अतिविकारभेदहीनः
सर्वस्मिन् नहि भवतो ऽस्ति किंचिद् अन्यत्
192.m: O self of all, unborn, through these conceptual constructions / you are the gods, you are the entire world, you alone are the universe; / O self of the universe, free from all modifications and distinctions, / in all this there is nothing whatsoever other than you!

192.s:
tvaṃ brahmā paśupatir aryamā vidhātā
tvaṃ dhātā tridaśapatiḥ samīraṇo 'gniḥ
toyeśo dhanapatir antakas tvam eko
bhinnātmā jagad api pāsi śaktibhedaiḥ
192.d:
त्वं ब्रह्मा पशुपतिर् अर्यमा विधाता
त्वं धाता त्रिदशपतिः समीरणो ऽग्निः
तोयेशो धनपतिर् अन्तकस् त्वम् एको
भिन्नात्मा जगद् अपि पासि शक्तिभेदैः
192.m: You are Brahmā, Paśupati, Aryaman, the ordainer; / you are Dhātṛ, the lord of the gods, the wind, fire, / the lord of waters, the lord of wealth, the ender; being one, / differentiated in self, you protect the world through your various powers.

192.s:
viśvaṃ bhavān sṛjati hanti gabhastirūpo
viśvaṃ ca te guṇamayo 'yam aja prapañcaḥ
rūpaṃ paraṃ saditivācakam akṣaraṃ yaj
jñānātmane sadasate praṇato 'smi tasmai
192.d:
विश्वं भवान् सृजति हन्ति गभस्तिरूपो
विश्वं च ते गुणमयो ऽयम् अज प्रपञ्चः
रूपं परं सदितिवाचकम् अक्षरं यज्
ज्ञानात्मने सदसते प्रणतो ऽस्मि तस्मै
192.m: You create the universe, and in the form of rays of light you destroy it; / this phenomenal expanse composed of the guṇas is your universe, O unborn one; / to that supreme, imperishable form expressed by the word 'being', / consisting of knowledge, both being and non-being, I bow!

192.s:
oṃ namo vāsudevāya namaḥ saṃkarṣaṇāya ca
pradyumnāya namas tubhyam aniruddhāya te namaḥ //
192.d:
ओं नमो वासुदेवाय नमः संकर्षणाय च
प्रद्युम्नाय नमस् तुभ्यम् अनिरुद्धाय ते नमः ॥
192.m: Oṃ, salutations to Vāsudeva, and salutations to Saṃkarṣaṇa; / salutations to Pradyumna; salutations to you, Aniruddha!”

192.s:
vyāsa uvāca
evam antar jale kṛṣṇam abhiṣṭūya sa yādavaḥ
arghayām āsa sarveśaṃ dhūpapuṣpair manomayaiḥ //
192.d:
व्यास उवाच
एवम् अन्तर् जले कृष्णम् अभिष्टूय स यादवः
अर्घयाम् आस सर्वेशं धूपपुष्पैर् मनोमयैः ॥
192.m: Vyāsa said: / Having thus praised Kṛṣṇa within the water, that Yādava / offered worship to the Lord of all with mental incense and flowers.

192.s:
parityajyānyaviṣayaṃ manas tatra niveśya saḥ
brahmabhūte ciraṃ sthitvā virarāma samādhitaḥ //
192.d:
परित्यज्यान्यविषयं मनस् तत्र निवेश्य सः
ब्रह्मभूते चिरं स्थित्वा विरराम समाधितः ॥
192.m: Forsaking any other object, fixing his mind upon him, / having remained for a long time as one who has become Brahman, he withdrew from samādhi.

192.s:
kṛtakṛtyam ivātmānaṃ manyamāno dvijottamāḥ
ājagāma rathaṃ bhūyo nirgamya yamunāmbhasaḥ //
192.d:
कृतकृत्यम् इवात्मानं मन्यमानो द्विजोत्तमाः
आजगाम रथं भूयो निर्गम्य यमुनाम्भसः ॥
192.m: Deeming himself to have accomplished his purpose, O best of the twice-born, / he came out of the waters of the Yamunā and went back to the chariot.

192.s:
rāmakṛṣṇau dadarśātha yathāpūrvam avasthitau
vismitākṣaṃ tadākrūraṃ taṃ ca kṛṣṇo 'bhyabhāṣata //
192.d:
रामकृष्णौ ददर्शाथ यथापूर्वम् अवस्थितौ
विस्मिताक्षं तदाक्रूरं तं च कृष्णो ऽभ्यभाषत ॥
192.m: Then he beheld Rāma and Kṛṣṇa remaining just as before; / and Kṛṣṇa addressed that Akrūra whose eyes were filled with wonder:

192.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca
kiṃ tvayā dṛṣṭam āścaryam akrūra yamunājale
vismayotphullanayano bhavān saṃlakṣyate yataḥ //
192.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच
किं त्वया दृष्टम् आश्चर्यम् अक्रूर यमुनाजले
विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयनो भवान् संलक्ष्यते यतः ॥
192.m: The blessed Kṛṣṇa said: / “What wondrous thing did you see in the waters of the Yamunā, Akrūra, / since your eyes appear wide open with astonishment?”

192.s:
akrūra uvāca
antar jale yad āścaryaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tatra mayācyuta
tad atraiva hi paśyāmi mūrtimat purataḥ sthitam //
192.d:
अक्रूर उवाच
अन्तर् जले यद् आश्चर्यं दृष्टं तत्र मयाच्युत
तद् अत्रैव हि पश्यामि मूर्तिमत् पुरतः स्थितम् ॥
192.m: Akrūra said: / “The wonder that I saw within the water there, O Acyuta, / that very same wonder I see right here, standing embodied before me!”

192.s:
jagad etan mahāścaryarūpaṃ yasya mahātmanaḥ
tenāścaryapareṇāhaṃ bhavatā kṛṣṇa saṃgataḥ //
192.d:
जगद् एतन् महाश्चर्यरूपं यस्य महात्मनः
तेनाश्चर्यपरेणाहं भवता कृष्ण संगतः ॥
192.m:
To that great soul whose form is this entire great wondrous world,
to you, Kṛṣṇa, who surpass all wonders, I have come.

192.s:
tat kim etena mathurāṃ prayāmo madhusūdana
bibhemi kaṃsād dhig janma parapiṇḍopajīvinaḥ //
192.d:
तत् किम् एतेन मथुरां प्रयामो मधुसूदन
बिभेमि कंसाद् धिग् जन्म परपिण्डोपजीविनः ॥
192.m:
So why speak of this? Let us proceed to Mathurā, O Madhusūdana!
I fear Kaṃsa. Fie on a life lived depending on another’s bread!

192.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktvā codayām āsa tān hayān vātaraṃhasaḥ
saṃprāptaś cāpi sāyāhne so 'krūro mathurāṃ purīm
vilokya mathurāṃ kṛṣṇaṃ rāmaṃ cāha sa yādavaḥ //
192.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा चोदयाम् आस तान् हयान् वातरंहसः
संप्राप्तश् चापि सायाह्ने सो ऽक्रूरो मथुरां पुरीम्
विलोक्य मथुरां कृष्णं रामं चाह स यादवः ॥
192.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having spoken thus, he urged on those horses swift as the wind,
and Akrūra reached the city of Mathurā in the evening.
Seeing Mathurā, that Yādava said to Kṛṣṇa and Rāma:

192.s:
akrūra uvāca
padbhyāṃ yātaṃ mahāvīryau rathenaiko viśāmy aham
gantavyaṃ vasudevasya no bhavadbhyāṃ tathā gṛhe
yuvayor hi kṛte vṛddhaḥ kaṃsena sa nirasyate //
192.d:
अक्रूर उवाच
पद्भ्यां यातं महावीर्यौ रथेनैको विशाम्य् अहम्
गन्तव्यं वसुदेवस्य नो भवद्भ्यां तथा गृहे
युवयोर् हि कृते वृद्धः कंसेन स निरस्यते ॥
192.m:
Akrūra said:
Go on foot, O two of great valor! I will enter alone in the chariot.
You must not go likewise to Vasudeva’s house,
for on your account that old man is harassed by Kaṃsa.

192.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktvā praviveśāsāv akrūro mathurāṃ purīm
praviṣṭau rāmakṛṣṇau ca rājamārgam upāgatau //
192.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा प्रविवेशासाव् अक्रूरो मथुरां पुरीम्
प्रविष्टौ रामकृष्णौ च राजमार्गम् उपागतौ ॥
192.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having spoken thus, Akrūra entered the city of Mathurā,
and Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, having entered, arrived on the royal highway.

192.s:
strībhir naraiś ca sānandalocanair abhivikṣitau
jagmatur līlayā vīrau prāptau bālagajāv iva //
192.d:
स्त्रीभिर् नरैश् च सानन्दलोचनैर् अभिविक्षितौ
जग्मतुर् लीलया वीरौ प्राप्तौ बालगजाव् इव ॥
192.m:
Gazed upon by women and men with delighted eyes,
the two heroes proceeded playfully, like two arrived young elephants.

192.s:
bhramamāṇau tu tau dṛṣṭvā rajakaṃ raṅgakārakam
ayācetāṃ svarūpāṇi vāsāṃsi rucirāṇi tau //
192.d:
भ्रममाणौ तु तौ दृष्ट्वा रजकं रङ्गकारकम्
अयाचेतां स्वरूपाणि वासांसि रुचिराणि तौ ॥
192.m:
As they wandered, seeing a washerman who was a dyer,
they asked him for beautiful garments of suitable form.

192.s:
kaṃsasya rajakaḥ so 'tha prasādārūḍhavismayaḥ
bahūny ākṣepavākyāni prāhoccai rāmakeśavau //
192.d:
कंसस्य रजकः सो ऽथ प्रसादारूढविस्मयः
बहून्य् आक्षेपवाक्यानि प्राहोच्चै रामकेशवौ ॥
192.m:
Then that washerman of Kaṃsa, filled with haughty insolence born of royal favor,
spoke many harsh insults loudly to Rāma and Keśava.

192.s:
tatas talaprahāreṇa kṛṣṇas tasya durātmanaḥ
pātayām āsa kopena rajakasya śiro bhuvi //
192.d:
ततस् तलप्रहारेण कृष्णस् तस्य दुरात्मनः
पातयाम् आस कोपेन रजकस्य शिरो भुवि ॥
192.m:
Then, with a blow of his palm, Kṛṣṇa in anger struck off
that evil-minded washerman’s head to the ground.

192.s:
hatvādāya ca vastrāṇi pītanīlāmbarau tataḥ
kṛṣṇarāmau mudāyuktau mālākāragṛhaṃ gatau //
192.d:
हत्वादाय च वस्त्राणि पीतनीलाम्बरौ ततः
कृष्णरामौ मुदायुक्तौ मालाकारगृहं गतौ ॥
192.m:
Having killed him and taken the clothes, the two, dressed in yellow and dark blue garments,
Kṛṣṇa and Rāma, filled with joy, went to the house of a garland-maker.

192.s:
vikāsinetrayugalo mālākāro 'tivismitaḥ
etau kasya kuto yātau manasācintayat tataḥ //
192.d:
विकासिनेत्रयुगलो मालाकारो ऽतिविस्मितः
एतौ कस्य कुतो यातौ मनसाचिन्तयत् ततः ॥
192.m:
With a pair of wide-open eyes, the garland-maker, greatly amazed,
then thought in his mind: “Whose sons are these two, and whence have they come?”

192.s:
pītanīlāmbaradharau dṛṣṭvātisumanoharau
sa tarkayām āsa tadā bhuvaṃ devāv upāgatau //
192.d:
पीतनीलाम्बरधरौ दृष्ट्वातिसुमनोहरौ
स तर्कयाम् आस तदा भुवं देवाव् उपागतौ ॥
192.m:
Seeing them wearing yellow and dark blue garments, exceedingly charming,
he then surmised: “Two gods have arrived on earth.”

192.s:
vikāśimukhapadmābhyāṃ tābhyāṃ puṣpāṇi yācitaḥ
bhuvaṃ viṣṭabhya hastābhyāṃ pasparśa śirasā mahīm //
192.d:
विकाशिमुखपद्माभ्यां ताभ्यां पुष्पाणि याचितः
भुवं विष्टभ्य हस्ताभ्यां पस्पर्श शिरसा महीम् ॥
192.m:
Asked for flowers by the two with blossoming lotus-like faces,
he planted his hands on the ground and touched the earth with his head.

192.s:
prasādasumukhau nāthau mama geham upāgatau
dhanyo 'ham arcayiṣyāmīty āha tau mālyajīvikaḥ //
192.d:
प्रसादसुमुखौ नाथौ मम गेहम् उपागतौ
धन्यो ऽहम् अर्चयिष्यामीत्य् आह तौ माल्यजीविकः ॥
192.m:
“My two lords, gracious and sweet-faced, have arrived at my home!
Blessed am I; I shall worship you,” said that seller of garlands to them.

192.s:
tataḥ prahṛṣṭavadanas tayoḥ puṣpāṇi kāmataḥ
cārūṇy etāni caitāni pradadau sa vilobhayan //
192.d:
ततः प्रहृष्टवदनस् तयोः पुष्पाणि कामतः
चारूण्य् एतानि चैतानि प्रददौ स विलोभयन् ॥
192.m:
Then, with a joyful face, he gave them flowers as they desired,
alluring them: “These are beautiful, and these [too].”

192.s:
punaḥ punaḥ praṇamyāsau mālākārottamo dadau
puṣpāṇi tābhyāṃ cārūṇi gandhavanty amalāni ca //
192.d:
पुनः पुनः प्रणम्यासौ मालाकारोत्तमो ददौ
पुष्पाणि ताभ्यां चारूणि गन्धवन्त्य् अमलानि च ॥
192.m:
Bowing again and again, that best of garland-makers gave
flowers to both of them, lovely, fragrant, and pure.

192.s:
mālākārāya kṛṣṇo 'pi prasannaḥ pradadau varam
śrīs tvāṃ matsaṃśrayā bhadra na kadācit tyajiṣyati //
192.d:
मालाकाराय कृष्णो ऽपि प्रसन्नः प्रददौ वरम्
श्रीस् त्वां मत्संश्रया भद्र न कदाचित् त्यजिष्यति ॥
192.m:
Pleased, Kṛṣṇa too granted a boon to the garland-maker:
“Prosperity, relying on me, dear man, shall never leave you.

192.s:
balahānir na te saumya dhanahānir athāpi vā
yāvad dharaṇisūryau ca saṃtatiḥ putrapautrikī //
192.d:
बलहानिर् न ते सौम्य धनहानिर् अथापि वा
यावद् धरणिसूर्यौ च संततिः पुत्रपौत्रिकी ॥
192.m:
There will be no loss of strength for you, gentle one, nor any loss of wealth,
and your lineage of sons and grandsons will endure as long as the earth and the sun.

192.s:
bhuktvā ca vipulān bhogāṃs tvam ante matprasādataḥ
mamānusmaraṇaṃ prāpya divyalokam avāpsyasi //
192.d:
भुक्त्वा च विपुलान् भोगांस् त्वम् अन्ते मत्प्रसादतः
ममानुस्मरणं प्राप्य दिव्यलोकम् अवाप्स्यसि ॥
192.m:
And having enjoyed vast pleasures, in the end, by my grace,
attaining remembrance of me, you will reach the celestial world.

192.s:
dharme manaś ca te bhadra sarvakālaṃ bhaviṣyati
yuṣmatsaṃtatijātānāṃ dīrgham āyur bhaviṣyati //
192.d:
धर्मे मनश् च ते भद्र सर्वकालं भविष्यति
युष्मत्संततिजातानां दीर्घम् आयुर् भविष्यति ॥
192.m:
Your mind will always be devoted to dharma, dear man;
those born in your lineage will have long life.

192.s:
nopasargādikaṃ doṣaṃ yuṣmatsaṃtatisaṃbhavaḥ
avāpsyati mahābhāga yāvat sūryo bhaviṣyati //
192.d:
नोपसर्गादिकं दोषं युष्मत्संततिसंभवः
अवाप्स्यति महाभाग यावत् सूर्यो भविष्यति ॥
192.m:
No calamity or misfortune will fall upon one born of your lineage,
O highly fortunate one, as long as the sun shall endure.”

192.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktvā tadgṛhāt kṛṣṇo baladevasahāyavān
nirjagāma muniśreṣṭhā mālākāreṇa pūjitaḥ //
192.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वा तद्गृहात् कृष्णो बलदेवसहायवान्
निर्जगाम मुनिश्रेष्ठा मालाकारेण पूजितः ॥
192.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having spoken thus, Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Baladeva,
departed from his house, O best of sages, after being honored by the garland-maker.

193.s:
vyāsa uvāca
rājamārge tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ sānulepanabhājanām
dadarśa kubjām āyāntīṃ navayauvanagocarām //
193.d:
व्यास उवाच
राजमार्गे ततः कृष्णः सानुलेपनभाजनाम्
ददर्श कुब्जाम् आयान्तीं नवयौवनगोचराम् ॥
193.m:
Vyāsa said:
Then on the royal highway, Kṛṣṇa saw a hunchbacked woman
approaching with a vessel of ointments, within the realm of fresh youth.

193.s:
tām āha lalitaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kasyedam anulepanam
bhavatyā nīyate satyaṃ vadendīvaralocane //
193.d:
ताम् आह ललितं कृष्णः कस्येदम् अनुलेपनम्
भवत्या नीयते सत्यं वदेन्दीवरलोचने ॥
193.m:
Kṛṣṇa playfully said to her: “For whom is this ointment
being carried by you? Speak the truth, O blue-lotus-eyed one!”

193.s:
sakāmenaiva sā proktā sānurāgā hariṃ prati
prāha sā lalitaṃ kubjā dadarśa ca balāt tataḥ //
193.d:
सकामेनैव सा प्रोक्ता सानुरागा हरिं प्रति
प्राह सा ललितं कुब्जा ददर्श च बलात् ततः ॥
193.m:
Addressed by him with evident affection, she, filled with passion toward Hari,
spoke playfully, and then the hunchbacked woman looked at him intently.

193.s:
kubjovāca
kānta kasmān na jānāsi kaṃsenāpi niyojitā
naikavakreti vikhyātām anulepanakarmaṇi //
193.d:
कुब्जोवाच
कान्त कस्मान् न जानासि कंसेनापि नियोजिता
नैकवक्रेति विख्याताम् अनुलेपनकर्मणि ॥
193.m:
Kubjā said:
“O handsome one, why do you not know me, appointed even by Kaṃsa,
known as Naikavakrā, engaged in the work of preparing ointments?

193.s:
nānyapiṣṭaṃ hi kaṃsasya prītaye hy anulepanam
bhavaty aham atīvāsya prasādadhanabhājanam //
193.d:
नान्यपिष्टं हि कंसस्य प्रीतये ह्य् अनुलेपनम्
भवत्य् अहम् अतीवास्य प्रसादधनभाजनम् ॥
193.m:
Indeed, ointment ground by no one else brings pleasure to Kaṃsa;
I am exceedingly the recipient of his favor and wealth.”

193.s:
śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca
sugandham etad rājārhaṃ ruciraṃ rucirānane
āvayor gātrasadṛśaṃ dīyatām anulepanam //
193.d:
श्रीकृष्ण उवाच
सुगन्धम् एतद् राजार्हं रुचिरं रुचिरानने
आवयोर् गात्रसदृशं दीयताम् अनुलेपनम् ॥
193.m:
The blessed Kṛṣṇa said:
“This is fragrant, worthy of a king, and delightful, O charming-faced one!
Give us ointment that is suitable for our bodies.”

193.s:
vyāsa uvāca
śrutvā tam āha sā kṛṣṇaṃ gṛhyatām iti sādaram
anulepaṃ ca pradadau gātrayogyam athobhayoḥ //
193.d:
व्यास उवाच
श्रुत्वा तम् आह सा कृष्णं गृह्यताम् इति सादरम्
अनुलेपं च प्रददौ गात्रयोग्यम् अथोभयोः ॥
193.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having heard him, she said to Kṛṣṇa: “Take it!” with respect,
and she gave ointment suitable for the bodies of both.

193.s:
bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau tatas tau puruṣarṣabhau
sendracāpau virājantau sitakṛṣṇāv ivāmbudau //
193.d:
भक्तिच्छेदानुलिप्ताङ्गौ ततस् तौ पुरुषर्षभौ
सेन्द्रचापौ विराजन्तौ सितकृष्णाव् इवाम्बुदौ ॥
193.m:
Their limbs anointed with decorative streaks, those two bulls among men
shone like white and black clouds adorned with a rainbow.

193.s:
tatas tāṃ cibuke śaurir ullāpanavidhānavit
ullāpya tolayām āsa dvyaṅgulenāgrapāṇinā //
193.d:
ततस् तां चिबुके शौरिर् उल्लापनविधानवित्
उल्लाप्य तोलयाम् आस द्व्यङ्गुलेनाग्रपाणिना ॥
193.m:
Then Śauri, who knew the method of uplifting, having lifted her up by the chin
with two fingers of his outstretched hand, raised her up.

193.s:
cakarṣa padbhyāṃ ca tadā ṛjutvaṃ keśavo 'nayat
tataḥ sā ṛjutāṃ prāptā yoṣitām abhavad varā //
193.d:
चकर्ष पद्भ्यां च तदा ऋजुत्वं केशवो ऽनयत्
ततः सा ऋजुतां प्राप्ता योषिताम् अभवद् वरा ॥
193.m:
And Keśava pressed down her feet, and brought her to straightness;
then, having attained straightness, she became the best among women.

193.s:
vilāsalalitaṃ prāha premagarbhabharālasam
vastre pragṛhya govindaṃ vraja gehaṃ mameti vai //
193.d:
विलासललितं प्राह प्रेमगर्भभरालसम्
वस्त्रे प्रगृह्य गोविन्दं व्रज गेहं ममेति वै ॥
193.m:
Playfully and gracefully she spoke, languid with the burden of swelling love,
grasping Govinda by his garment: “Do come to my house!”

193.s:
āyāsye bhavatīgeham iti tāṃ prāha keśavaḥ
visasarja jahāsoccai rāmasyālokya cānanam //
193.d:
आयास्ये भवतीगेहम् इति तां प्राह केशवः
विससर्ज जहासोच्चै रामस्यालोक्य चाननम् ॥
193.m:
“I shall come to your house,” Keśava said to her.
He dismissed her and laughed loudly, looking at the face of Rāma.

193.s:
bhakticchedānuliptāṅgau nīlapītāmbarāv ubhau
dhanuḥśālāṃ tato yātau citramālyopaśobhitau //
193.d:
भक्तिच्छेदानुलिप्ताङ्गौ नीलपीताम्बराव् उभौ
धनुःशालां ततो यातौ चित्रमाल्योपशोभितौ ॥
193.m:
Their limbs smeared with decorative streaks, both wearing blue and yellow garments,
adorned with variegated garlands, they then went to the armory.

193.s:
adhyāsya ca dhanūratnaṃ tābhyāṃ pṛṣṭais tu rakṣibhiḥ
ākhyātaṃ sahasā kṛṣṇo gṛhītvāpūrayad dhanuḥ //
193.d:
अध्यास्य च धनूरत्नं ताभ्यां पृष्टैस् तु रक्षिभिः
आख्यातं सहसा कृष्णो गृहीत्वापूरयद् धनुः ॥
193.m:
Finding the splendid bow, when informed by the guards whom they questioned,
Kṛṣṇa quickly took it up and drew the bow.

193.s:
tataḥ pūrayatā tena bhajyamānaṃ balād dhanuḥ
cakārātimahāśabdaṃ mathurā tena pūritā //
193.d:
ततः पूरयता तेन भज्यमानं बलाद् धनुः
चकारातिमहाशब्दं मथुरा तेन पूरिता ॥
193.m:
Then, broken by force by him as he drew it,
the bow made an immense sound, and Mathurā was filled with it.

193.s:
anuyuktau tatas tau ca bhagne dhanuṣi rakṣibhiḥ
rakṣisainyaṃ nikṛtyobhau niṣkrāntau kārmukālayāt //
193.d:
अनुयुक्तौ ततस् तौ च भग्ने धनुषि रक्षिभिः
रक्षिसैन्यं निकृत्योभौ निष्क्रान्तौ कार्मुकालयात् ॥
193.m:
Assailed then by the guards when the bow was broken,
both cut down the army of guards and emerged from the armory.

193.s:
akrūrāgamavṛttāntam upalabhya tathā dhanuḥ
bhagnaṃ śrutvātha kaṃso 'pi prāha cāṇūramuṣṭikau //
193.d:
अक्रूरागमवृत्तान्तम् उपलभ्य तथा धनुः
भग्नं श्रुत्वाथ कंसो ऽपि प्राह चाणूरमुष्टिकौ ॥
193.m:
Learning the news of Akrūra’s arrival, and also hearing
that the bow was broken, Kaṃsa then spoke to Cāṇūra and Muṣṭika:

193.s:
kaṃsa uvāca
gopāladārakau prāptau bhavadbhyāṃ tau mamāgrataḥ
mallayuddhena hantavyau mama prāṇaharau hi tau //
193.d:
कंस उवाच
गोपालदारकौ प्राप्तौ भवद्भ्यां तौ ममाग्रतः
मल्लयुद्धेन हन्तव्यौ मम प्राणहरौ हि तौ ॥
193.m:
Kaṃsa said:
“The two cowherd boys have arrived; in my presence
they must be killed by you in a wrestling match, for they seek my life.

193.s:
niyuddhe tadvināśena bhavadbhyāṃ toṣito hy aham
dāsyāmy abhimatān kāmān nānyathaitan mahābalau //
193.d:
नियुद्धे तद्विनाशेन भवद्भ्यां तोषितो ह्य् अहम्
दास्याम्य् अभिमतान् कामान् नान्यथैतन् महाबलौ ॥
193.m:
I will be pleased by you through their destruction in close combat,
and I will grant your desired wishes; it will not be otherwise, O mighty ones!

193.s:
nyāyato 'nyāyato vāpi bhavadbhyāṃ tau mamāhitau
hantavyau tadvadhād rājyaṃ sāmānyaṃ vo bhaviṣyati //
193.d:
न्यायतो ऽन्यायतो वापि भवद्भ्यां तौ ममाहितौ
हन्तव्यौ तद्वधाद् राज्यं सामान्यं वो भविष्यति ॥
193.m:
Whether justly or unjustly, those two enemies of mine
must be killed by you; with their slaughter, the kingdom will be shared with you.”

193.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity ādiśya sa tau mallau tataś cāhūya hastipam
provācoccais tvayā mattaḥ samājadvāri kuñjaraḥ //
193.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् आदिश्य स तौ मल्लौ ततश् चाहूय हस्तिपम्
प्रोवाचोच्चैस् त्वया मत्तः समाजद्वारि कुञ्जरः ॥
193.m:
Vyāsa said:
Having thus instructed the two wrestlers, and having summoned the elephant-keeper,
he said loudly: “By you an elephant in rut

193.s:
sthāpyaḥ kuvalayāpīḍas tena tau gopadārakau
ghātanīyau niyuddhāya raṅgadvāram upāgatau //
193.d:
स्थाप्यः कुवलयापीडस् तेन तौ गोपदारकौ
घातनीयौ नियुद्धाय रङ्गद्वारम् उपागतौ ॥
193.m:
named Kuvalayāpīḍa must be stationed at the arena gate;
by him those two cowherd boys, having arrived at the arena gate for combat, must be killed.”

193.s:
tam ājñāpyātha dṛṣṭvā ca mañcān sarvān upāhṛtān
āsannamaraṇaḥ kaṃsaḥ sūryodayam udaikṣata //
193.d:
तम् आज्ञाप्याथ दृष्ट्वा च मञ्चान् सर्वान् उपाहृतान्
आसन्नमरणः कंसः सूर्योदयम् उदैक्षत ॥
193.m:
Having given this command, and seeing that all the platforms had been prepared,
Kaṃsa, whose death was near, watched for the sunrise.

193.s:
tataḥ samastamañceṣu nāgaraḥ sa tadā janaḥ
rājamañceṣu cārūḍhāḥ saha bhṛtyair mahībhṛtaḥ //
193.d:
ततः समस्तमञ्चेषु नागरः स तदा जनः
राजमञ्चेषु चारूढाः सह भृत्यैर् महीभृतः ॥
193.m:
Then all the townspeople mounted upon the ordinary platforms,
and kings ascended the royal platforms along with their attendants.

193.s:
mallaprāśnikavargaś ca raṅgamadhye samīpagaḥ
kṛtaḥ kaṃsena kaṃso 'pi tuṅgamañce vyavasthitaḥ //
193.d:
मल्लप्राश्निकवर्गश् च रङ्गमध्ये समीपगः
कृतः कंसेन कंसो ऽपि तुङ्गमञ्चे व्यवस्थितः ॥
193.m: And the group of wrestling umpires was stationed nearby in the middle of the arena / by Kaṃsa; Kaṃsa too took his place on a high platform.

193.s:
antaḥpurāṇāṃ mañcāś ca yathānye parikalpitāḥ
anye ca vāramukhyānām anye nagarayoṣitām //
193.d:
अन्तःपुराणां मञ्चाश् च यथान्ये परिकल्पिताः
अन्ये च वारमुख्यानाम् अन्ये नगरयोषिताम् ॥
193.m: And other platforms were arranged for the women of the royal household, / others for the courtesans, and others for the city women.

193.s:
nandagopādayo gopā mañceṣv anyeṣv avasthitāḥ
akrūravasudevau ca mañcaprānte vyavasthitau //
193.d:
नन्दगोपादयो गोपा मञ्चेष्व् अन्येष्व् अवस्थिताः
अक्रूरवसुदेवौ च मञ्चप्रान्ते व्यवस्थितौ ॥
193.m: The cowherds, headed by Nandagopa, were seated on other platforms, / and Akrūra and Vasudeva took their places at the edge of a platform.

193.s:
nagarīyoṣitāṃ madhye devakī putragardhinī
antakāle 'pi putrasya drakṣyāmīti mukhaṃ sthitā //
193.d:
नगरीयोषितां मध्ये देवकी पुत्रगर्धिनी
अन्तकाले ऽपि पुत्रस्य द्रक्ष्यामीति मुखं स्थिता ॥
193.m: Among the city women stood Devakī, longing for her son, / thinking: “Even at the hour of death, I shall behold my son's face.”

193.s:
vādyamāneṣu tūryeṣu cāṇūre cātivalgati
hāhākārapare loka āsphoṭayati muṣṭike //
193.d:
वाद्यमानेषु तूर्येषु चाणूरे चातिवल्गति
हाहाकारपरे लोक आस्फोटयति मुष्टिके ॥
193.m: While the musical instruments were being sounded, and Cāṇūra was bounding vigorously about, / while the people were shouting in distress, and Muṣṭika was slapping his arms in challenge,

193.s:
hatvā kuvalayāpīḍaṃ hastyārohapracoditam
madāsṛganuliptāṅgau gajadantavarāyudhau //
193.d:
हत्वा कुवलयापीडं हस्त्यारोहप्रचोदितम्
मदासृगनुलिप्ताङ्गौ गजदन्तवरायुधौ ॥
193.m: having slain Kuvalayāpīḍa, who had been urged on by the elephant-driver, / their limbs smeared with rut-fluid and blood, with the elephant’s tusks as excellent weapons,

193.s:
mṛgamadhye yathā siṃhau garvalīlāvalokinau
praviṣṭau sumahāraṅgaṃ baladevajanārdanau //
193.d:
मृगमध्ये यथा सिंहौ गर्वलीलावलोकिनौ
प्रविष्टौ सुमहारङ्गं बलदेवजनार्दनौ ॥
193.m: Like two lions among deer, gazing about with proud grace, / Baladeva and Janārdana entered the vast arena.

193.s:
hāhākāro mahāñ jajñe sarvaraṅgeṣv anantaram
kṛṣṇo 'yaṃ balabhadro 'yam iti lokasya vismayāt //
193.d:
हाहाकारो महाञ् जज्ञे सर्वरङ्गेष्व् अनन्तरम्
कृष्णो ऽयं बलभद्रो ऽयम् इति लोकस्य विस्मयात् ॥
193.m: Thereupon a great cry of dismay arose in all parts of the arena, / out of the people's wonder: "This is Kṛṣṇa, this is Balabhadra!"

193.s:
so 'yaṃ yena hatā ghorā pūtanā sā niśācarī
prakṣiptaṃ śakaṭaṃ yena bhagnau ca yamalārjunau //
193.d:
सो ऽयं येन हता घोरा पूतना सा निशाचरी
प्रक्षिप्तं शकटं येन भग्नौ च यमलार्जुनौ ॥
193.m: "This is the one by whom that terrible night-wandering demoness Pūtanā was slain, / by whom the cart was overturned, and the twin arjuna trees broken.

193.s:
so 'yaṃ yaḥ kāliyaṃ nāgaṃ nanartāruhya bālakaḥ
dhṛto govardhano yena saptarātraṃ mahāgiriḥ //
193.d:
सो ऽयं यः कालियं नागं ननर्तारुह्य बालकः
धृतो गोवर्धनो येन सप्तरात्रं महागिरिः ॥
193.m: This is the child who climbed upon the serpent Kāliya and danced, / by whom the great mountain Govardhana was held up for seven nights.

193.s:
ariṣṭo dhenukaḥ keśī līlayaiva mahātmanā
hato yena ca durvṛtto dṛśyate so 'yam acyutaḥ //
193.d:
अरिष्टो धेनुकः केशी लीलयैव महात्मना
हतो येन च दुर्वृत्तो दृश्यते सो ऽयम् अच्युतः ॥
193.m: By that great-souled one Ariṣṭa, Dhenuka, and the wicked Keśī / were slain in mere play; this is that imperishable Acyuta now seen.

193.s:
ayaṃ cāsya mahābāhur baladevo 'grajo 'grataḥ
prayāti līlayā yoṣinmanonayananandanaḥ //
193.d:
अयं चास्य महाबाहुर् बलदेवो ऽग्रजो ऽग्रतः
प्रयाति लीलया योषिन्मनोनयननन्दनः ॥
193.m: And here ahead goes his mighty-armed elder brother Baladeva, / playfully moving forward, delighting the minds and eyes of women.

193.s:
ayaṃ sa kathyate prājñaiḥ purāṇārthāvalokibhiḥ
gopālo yādavaṃ vaṃśaṃ magnam abhyuddhariṣyati //
193.d:
अयं स कथ्यते प्राज्ञैः पुराणार्थावलोकिभिः
गोपालो यादवं वंशं मग्नम् अभ्युद्धरिष्यति ॥
193.m: This is he spoken of by the wise who perceive the meaning of the Purāṇas, / the cowherd who will deliver the sunken Yādava lineage.

193.s:
ayaṃ sa sarvabhūtasya viṣṇor akhilajanmanaḥ
avatīrṇo mahīm aṃśo nūnaṃ bhāraharo bhuvaḥ //
193.d:
अयं स सर्वभूतस्य विष्णोर् अखिलजन्मनः
अवतीर्णो महीम् अंशो नूनं भारहरो भुवः ॥
193.m: This is a portion of Viṣṇu, who constitutes all beings and is the source of all birth, / descended to earth, surely to take away the burden of the world."

193.s:
ity evaṃ varṇite paurai rāme kṛṣṇe ca tatkṣaṇāt
uras tatāpa devakyāḥ snehasnutapayodharam //
193.d:
इत्य् एवं वर्णिते पौरै रामे कृष्णे च तत्क्षणात्
उरस् तताप देवक्याः स्नेहस्नुतपयोधरम् ॥
193.m: As Rāma and Kṛṣṇa were thus described by the citizens, / Devakī's breast burned at that moment, her bosom trickling with milk from love.

193.s:
mahotsavam ivālokya putrāv eva vilokayan
yuveva vasudevo 'bhūd vihāyābhyāgatāṃ jarām //
193.d:
महोत्सवम् इवालोक्य पुत्राव् एव विलोकयन्
युवेव वसुदेवो ऽभूद् विहायाभ्यागतां जराम् ॥
193.m: Gazing upon his two sons as if beholding a great festival, / Vasudeva, casting off the old age that had come upon him, became as if young again.

193.s:
vistāritākṣiyugalā rājāntaḥpurayoṣitaḥ
nāgarastrīsamūhaś ca draṣṭuṃ na virarāma tau //
193.d:
विस्तारिताक्षियुगला राजान्तःपुरयोषितः
नागरस्त्रीसमूहश् च द्रष्टुं न विरराम तौ ॥
193.m: With wide-opened pairs of eyes, the women of the king's inner apartments / and the crowd of city women did not cease gazing upon the two.

193.s:
striya ūcuḥ
sakhyaḥ paśyata kṛṣṇasya mukham apy ambujekṣaṇam
gajayuddhakṛtāyāsasvedāmbukaṇikāñcitam //
193.d:
स्त्रिय ऊचुः
सख्यः पश्यत कृष्णस्य मुखम् अप्य् अम्बुजेक्षणम्
गजयुद्धकृतायासस्वेदाम्बुकणिकाञ्चितम् ॥
193.m: The women said: / "Look, friends, at Kṛṣṇa's lotus-eyed face, / graced with droplets of sweat from the exertion of fighting the elephant,

193.s:
vikāsīva sarombhojam avaśyāyajalokṣitam
paribhūtākṣaraṃ janma saphalaṃ kriyatāṃ dṛśaḥ //
193.d:
विकासीव सरोम्भोजम् अवश्यायजलोक्षितम्
परिभूताक्षरं जन्म सफलं क्रियतां दृशः ॥
193.m: like a blooming lotus in a lake sprinkled with frost-water! / Let this birth, having transcended impermanence, make our eyes fruitful!

193.s:
śrīvatsāṅkaṃ jagaddhāma bālasyaitad vilokyatām
vipakṣakṣapaṇaṃ vakṣo bhujayugmaṃ ca bhāmini //
193.d:
श्रीवत्साङ्कं जगद्धाम बालस्यैतद् विलोक्यताम्
विपक्षक्षपणं वक्षो भुजयुग्मं च भामिनि ॥
193.m: O radiant one, behold this child's chest marked with the Śrīvatsa, the abode of the universe, / and his pair of arms that destroy adversaries!

193.s:
valgatā muṣṭikenaiva cāṇūreṇa tathā paraiḥ
kriyate balabhadrasya hāsyam īṣad vilokyatām //
193.d:
वल्गता मुष्टिकेनैव चाणूरेण तथा परैः
क्रियते बलभद्रस्य हास्यम् ईषद् विलोक्यताम् ॥
193.m: Look at the gentle smile made by Balabhadra / as Muṣṭika struts about, and likewise Cāṇūra and the others!

193.s:
sakhyaḥ paśyata cāṇūraṃ niyuddhārtham ayaṃ hariḥ
samupaiti na santy atra kiṃ vṛddhā yuktakāriṇaḥ //
193.d:
सख्यः पश्यत चाणूरं नियुद्धार्थम् अयं हरिः
समुपैति न सन्त्य् अत्र किं वृद्धा युक्तकारिणः ॥
193.m: Friends, look! This Hari is advancing to wrestle with Cāṇūra; / are there no elders here who act with propriety?

193.s:
kva yauvanonmukhībhūtaḥ sukumāratanur hariḥ
kva vajrakaṭhinābhogaśarīro 'yaṃ mahāsuraḥ //
193.d:
क्व यौवनोन्मुखीभूतः सुकुमारतनुर् हरिः
क्व वज्रकठिनाभोगशरीरो ऽयं महासुरः ॥
193.m: Where is Hari, delicate-bodied and just on the verge of youth, / and where is this great asura, his massive body as hard as a thunderbolt?

193.s:
imau sulalitau raṅge vartete navayauvanau
daiteyamallāś cāṇūrapramukhās tv atidāruṇāḥ //
193.d:
इमौ सुललितौ रङ्गे वर्तेते नवयौवनौ
दैतेयमल्लाश् चाणूरप्रमुखास् त्व् अतिदारुणाः ॥
193.m: These two, exceedingly graceful, are in the arena in their fresh youth, / whereas the Daiteya wrestlers headed by Cāṇūra are exceedingly fierce.

193.s:
niyuddhaprāśnikānāṃ tu mahān eṣa vyatikramaḥ
yad bālabalinor yuddhaṃ madhyasthaiḥ samupekṣyate //
193.d:
नियुद्धप्राश्निकानां तु महान् एष व्यतिक्रमः
यद् बालबलिनोर् युद्धं मध्यस्थैः समुपेक्ष्यते ॥
193.m: This is a great transgression on the part of the wrestling umpires, / that an unequal match between a child and a strongman is ignored by the arbiters."

193.s:
vyāsa uvāca
itthaṃ purastrīlokasya vadataś cālayan bhuvam
vavarṣa harṣotkarṣaṃ ca janasya bhagavān hariḥ //
193.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्थं पुरस्त्रीलोकस्य वदतश् चालयन् भुवम्
ववर्ष हर्षोत्कर्षं च जनस्य भगवान् हरिः ॥
193.m: Vyāsa said: / As the townswomen were speaking thus, the blessed lord Hari, / shaking the earth, showered supreme delight upon the people.

193.s:
balabhadro 'pi cāsphoṭya vavalga lalitaṃ yadā
pade pade tadā bhūmir na śīrṇā yat tad adbhutam //
193.d:
बलभद्रो ऽपि चास्फोट्य ववल्ग ललितं यदा
पदे पदे तदा भूमिर् न शीर्णा यत् तद् अद्भुतम् ॥
193.m: When Balabhadra too clapped his arms and leaped gracefully, / it was a wonder that the ground was not shattered at every step.

193.s:
cāṇūreṇa tataḥ kṛṣṇo yuyudhe 'mitavikramaḥ
niyuddhakuśalo daityo baladevena muṣṭikaḥ //
193.d:
चाणूरेण ततः कृष्णो युयुधे ऽमितविक्रमः
नियुद्धकुशलो दैत्यो बलदेवेन मुष्टिकः ॥
193.m: Then Kṛṣṇa of unmeasured prowess fought with Cāṇūra, / and the Daitya Muṣṭika, skilled in wrestling, fought with Baladeva.

193.s:
saṃnipātāvadhūtaiś ca cāṇūreṇa samaṃ hariḥ
kṣepaṇair muṣṭibhiś caiva kīlāvajranipātanaiḥ //
193.d:
संनिपातावधूतैश् च चाणूरेण समं हरिः
क्षेपणैर् मुष्टिभिश् चैव कीलावज्रनिपातनैः ॥
193.m: Hari [fought] with Cāṇūra through clashes and shakings, / throws, fists, and blows like thunderbolts and pegs,

193.s:
pādodbhūtaiḥ pramṛṣṭābhis tayor yuddham abhūn mahat
aśastram atighoraṃ tat tayor yuddhaṃ sudāruṇam //
193.d:
पादोद्भूतैः प्रमृष्टाभिस् तयोर् युद्धम् अभून् महत्
अशस्त्रम् अतिघोरं तत् तयोर् युद्धं सुदारुणम् ॥
193.m: and kicks and sweeps; a great combat ensued between the two. / Weaponless, exceedingly terrible, it was a most dreadful fight between them.

193.s:
svabalaprāṇaniṣpādyaṃ samājotsavasaṃnidhau
yāvad yāvac ca cāṇūro yuyudhe hariṇā saha //
193.d:
स्वबलप्राणनिष्पाद्यं समाजोत्सवसंनिधौ
यावद् यावच् च चाणूरो युयुधे हरिणा सह ॥
193.m: Executed by their own strength and vitality in the presence of the festive assembly, / the longer Cāṇūra fought with Hari,

193.s:
prāṇahānim avāpāgryāṃ tāvat tāvan na bāndhavam
kṛṣṇo 'pi yuyudhe tena līlayaiva jaganmayaḥ //
193.d:
प्राणहानिम् अवापाग्र्यां तावत् तावन् न बान्धवम्
कृष्णो ऽपि युयुधे तेन लीलयैव जगन्मयः ॥
193.m: the more he suffered severe loss of vitality, finding no ally. / Kṛṣṇa too, who embodies the world, fought with him in mere sport.

193.s:
khedāc cālayatā kopān nijaśeṣakare karam
balakṣayaṃ vivṛddhiṃ ca dṛṣṭvā cāṇūrakṛṣṇayoḥ //
193.d:
खेदाच् चालयता कोपान् निजशेषकरे करम्
बलक्षयं विवृद्धिं च दृष्ट्वा चाणूरकृष्णयोः ॥
193.m: From distress, [Kaṃsa] angrily wrung his hand with his other remaining hand, / having seen the loss of strength in Cāṇūra and its increase in Kṛṣṇa.

193.s:
vārayām āsa tūryāṇi kaṃsaḥ kopaparāyaṇaḥ
mṛdaṅgādiṣu vādyeṣu pratiṣiddheṣu tatkṣaṇāt //
193.d:
वारयाम् आस तूर्याणि कंसः कोपपरायणः
मृदङ्गादिषु वाद्येषु प्रतिषिद्धेषु तत्क्षणात् ॥
193.m: Filled with rage, Kaṃsa stopped the horns; / and when the drums and other instruments were stopped at that moment,

193.s:
khasaṃgatāny avādyanta daivatūryāṇy anekaśaḥ
jaya govinda cāṇūraṃ jahi keśava dānavam //
193.d:
खसंगतान्य् अवाद्यन्त दैवतूर्याण्य् अनेकशः
जय गोविन्द चाणूरं जहि केशव दानवम् ॥
193.m: divine horns in the sky sounded in various ways: / "Triumph, Govinda! Slay the Dānava Cāṇūra, Keśava!"

193.s:
ity antardhigatā devās tuṣṭuvus te praharṣitāḥ
cāṇūreṇa ciraṃ kālaṃ krīḍitvā madhusūdanaḥ //
193.d:
इत्य् अन्तर्धिगता देवास् तुष्टुवुस् ते प्रहर्षिताः
चाणूरेण चिरं कालं क्रीडित्वा मधुसूदनः ॥
193.m: Thus the gods, remaining invisible, praised him in great joy. / Having played with Cāṇūra for a long time, the slayer of Madhu,

193.s:
utpāṭya bhrāmayām āsa tadvadhāya kṛtodyamaḥ
bhrāmayitvā śataguṇaṃ daityamallam amitrajit //
193.d:
उत्पाट्य भ्रामयाम् आस तद्वधाय कृतोद्यमः
भ्रामयित्वा शतगुणं दैत्यमल्लम् अमित्रजित् ॥
193.m: making an effort to kill him, lifted him up and whirled him around. / Having whirled the Daitya wrestler a hundred times, the conqueror of foes

193.s:
bhūmāv āsphoṭayām āsa gagane gatajīvitam
bhūmāv āsphoṭitas tena cāṇūraḥ śatadhā bhavan //
193.d:
भूमाव् आस्फोटयाम् आस गगने गतजीवितम्
भूमाव् आस्फोटितस् तेन चाणूरः शतधा भवन् ॥
193.m: dashed him against the ground, his life having already departed in the sky. / Smashed against the earth by him, Cāṇūra shattered into a hundred pieces,

193.s:
raktasrāvamahāpaṅkāṃ cakāra sa tadā bhuvam
baladevas tu tatkālaṃ muṣṭikena mahābalaḥ //
193.d:
रक्तस्रावमहापङ्कां चकार स तदा भुवम्
बलदेवस् तु तत्कालं मुष्टिकेन महाबलः ॥
193.m: and then turned the ground into a great mire of streaming blood. / Meanwhile, the mighty Baladeva

193.s:
yuyudhe daityamallena cāṇūreṇa yathā hariḥ
so 'py enaṃ muṣṭinā mūrdhni vakṣasy āhatya jānunā //
193.d:
युयुधे दैत्यमल्लेन चाणूरेण यथा हरिः
सो ऽप्य् एनं मुष्टिना मूर्ध्नि वक्षस्य् आहत्य जानुना ॥
193.m: fought with the Daitya wrestler Muṣṭika, just as Hari did with Cāṇūra. / He too struck him on the head with his fist and on the chest with his knee,

193.s:
pātayitvā dharāpṛṣṭhe niṣpipeṣa gatāyuṣam
kṛṣṇas tośalakaṃ bhūyo mallarājaṃ mahābalam //
193.d:
पातयित्वा धरापृष्ठे निष्पिपेष गतायुषम्
कृष्णस् तोशलकं भूयो मल्लराजं महाबलम् ॥
193.m: threw him down onto the surface of the earth, and crushed the lifespring out of him. / Next, Kṛṣṇa knocked down the wrestler-king, the mighty Tośalaka,

193.s:
vāmamuṣṭiprahāreṇa pātayām āsa bhūtale
cāṇūre nihate malle muṣṭike ca nipātite //
193.d:
वाममुष्टिप्रहारेण पातयाम् आस भूतले
चाणूरे निहते मल्ले मुष्टिके च निपातिते ॥
193.m: to the earth's surface with a blow of his left fist. / When the wrestler Cāṇūra had been slain, Muṣṭika struck down,

193.s:
nīte kṣayaṃ tośalake sarve mallāḥ pradudruvuḥ
vavalgatus tadā raṅge kṛṣṇasaṃkarṣaṇāv ubhau //
193.d:
नीते क्षयं तोशलके सर्वे मल्लाः प्रदुद्रुवुः
ववल्गतुस् तदा रङ्गे कृष्णसंकर्षणाव् उभौ ॥
193.m: and Tośalaka brought to destruction, all the wrestlers fled. / Then both Kṛṣṇa and Saṃkarṣaṇa leaped about in the arena,

193.s:
samānavayaso gopān balād ākṛṣya harṣitau
kaṃso 'pi koparaktākṣaḥ prāhoccair vyāyatān narān //
193.d:
समानवयसो गोपान् बलाद् आकृष्य हर्षितौ
कंसो ऽपि कोपरक्ताक्षः प्राहोच्चैर् व्यायतान् नरान् ॥
193.m: joyfully pulling in cowherds of their own age by force. / Kaṃsa too, his eyes red with anger, shouted loudly to his tall men:

193.s:
gopāv etau samājaughān niṣkramyetāṃ balād itaḥ
nando 'pi gṛhyatāṃ pāpo nigaḍair āśu badhyatām //
193.d:
गोपाव् एतौ समाजौघान् निष्क्रम्येतां बलाद् इतः
नन्दो ऽपि गृह्यतां पापो निगडैर् आशु बध्यताम् ॥
193.m: "Let these two cowherds be forcibly cast out from the gathering! / Let the wicked Nanda also be seized and quickly bound in irons!

193.s:
avṛddhārheṇa daṇḍena vasudevo 'pi vadhyatām
valganti gopāḥ kṛṣṇena ye ceme sahitāḥ punaḥ //
193.d:
अवृद्धार्हेण दण्डेन वसुदेवो ऽपि वध्यताम्
वल्गन्ति गोपाः कृष्णेन ये चेमे सहिताः पुनः ॥
193.m: Let Vasudeva too be executed with a punishment unfitting for an elder! / Moreover, the cowherds who strut about along with Kṛṣṇa—

193.s:
gāvo hriyantām eṣāṃ ca yac cāsti vasu kiṃcana
evam ājñāpayantaṃ taṃ prahasya madhusūdanaḥ //
193.d:
गावो ह्रियन्ताम् एषां च यच् चास्ति वसु किंचन
एवम् आज्ञापयन्तं तं प्रहस्य मधुसूदनः ॥
193.m: let their cows be seized, and whatever wealth they possess!" / As he was giving such orders, the slayer of Madhu laughed,

193.s:
utpatyāruhya tanmañcaṃ kaṃsaṃ jagrāha vegitaḥ
keśeṣv ākṛṣya vigalatkirīṭam avanītale //
193.d:
उत्पत्यारुह्य तन्मञ्चं कंसं जग्राह वेगितः
केशेष्व् आकृष्य विगलत्किरीटम् अवनीतले ॥
193.m: leaped up, mounted that platform, and swiftly seized Kaṃsa. / Dragging him by the hair, his crown slipping off, onto the ground,

193.s:
sa kaṃsaṃ pātayām āsa tasyopari papāta ca
niḥśeṣajagadādhāraguruṇā patatopari //
193.d:
स कंसं पातयाम् आस तस्योपरि पपात च
निःशेषजगदाधारगुरुणा पततोपरि ॥
193.m: he hurled Kaṃsa down and fell upon him; / falling upon him with the weight of the support of the entire universe,

193.s:
kṛṣṇena tyājitaḥ prāṇānn ugrasenātmajo nṛpaḥ
mṛtasya keśeṣu tadā gṛhītvā madhusūdanaḥ //
193.d:
कृष्णेन त्याजितः प्राणान्न् उग्रसेनात्मजो नृपः
मृतस्य केशेषु तदा गृहीत्वा मधुसूदनः ॥
193.m: By Kṛṣṇa the king, Ugrasena’s son, was made to yield up his life-breaths. / Then, seizing the dead man by the hair, Madhusūdana,

193.s:
cakarṣa dehaṃ kaṃsasya raṅgamadhye mahābalaḥ
gauraveṇātimahatā paripātena kṛṣyatā //
193.d:
चकर्ष देहं कंसस्य रङ्गमध्ये महाबलः
गौरवेणातिमहता परिपातेन कृष्यता ॥
193.m: mighty in strength, dragged Kaṃsa’s body into the middle of the arena; / and as it was dragged along with tremendous weight and impact,

193.s:
kṛtā kaṃsasya dehena vegitena mahātmanā
kaṃse gṛhīte kṛṣṇena tadbhrātābhyāgato ruṣā //
193.d:
कृता कंसस्य देहेन वेगितेन महात्मना
कंसे गृहीते कृष्णेन तद्भ्राताभ्यागतो रुषा ॥
193.m: a [broad furrow] was made by the rushing body of the great-souled Kaṃsa. / When Kaṃsa had been seized by Kṛṣṇa, his brother rushed up in fury;

193.s:
sunāmā balabhadreṇa līlayaiva nipātitaḥ
tato hāhākṛtaṃ sarvam āsīt tad raṅgamaṇḍalam //
193.d:
सुनामा बलभद्रेण लीलयैव निपातितः
ततो हाहाकृतं सर्वम् आसीत् तद् रङ्गमण्डलम् ॥
193.m: Sunāman was brought down by Balabhadra as if in mere sport. / Then a cry of grief arose from that whole circle of the arena,

193.s:
avajñayā hataṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇena mathureśvaram
kṛṣṇo 'pi vasudevasya pādau jagrāha satvaram //
193.d:
अवज्ञया हतं दृष्ट्वा कृष्णेन मथुरेश्वरम्
कृष्णो ऽपि वसुदेवस्य पादौ जग्राह सत्वरम् ॥
193.m: seeing the lord of Mathurā slain contemptuously by Kṛṣṇa. / Then Kṛṣṇa quickly took hold of Vasudeva’s feet,

193.s:
devakyāś ca mahābāhur baladevasahāyavān
utthāpya vasudevas tu devakī ca janārdanam
smṛtajanmoktavacanau tāv eva praṇatau sthitau //
193.d:
देवक्याश् च महाबाहुर् बलदेवसहायवान्
उत्थाप्य वसुदेवस् तु देवकी च जनार्दनम्
स्मृतजन्मोक्तवचनौ ताव् एव प्रणतौ स्थितौ ॥
193.m: and those of Devakī, the long-armed one, accompanied by Baladeva. / Having raised up Janārdana, Vasudeva and Devakī, / remembering the words spoken at his birth, remained bowed down.

193.s:
vasudeva uvāca
prasīda devadeveśa devānāṃ pravara prabho
tathāvayoḥ prasādena kṛtābhyuddhāra keśava //
193.d:
वसुदेव उवाच
प्रसीद देवदेवेश देवानां प्रवर प्रभो
तथावयोः प्रसादेन कृताभ्युद्धार केशव ॥
193.m: Vasudeva said: / Be gracious, O lord of the gods of gods, O foremost of the gods, O lord! / Keśava, by your grace the deliverance of us two has been accomplished.

193.s:
ārādhito yad bhagavān avatīrṇo gṛhe mama
durvṛttanidhanārthāya tena naḥ pāvitaṃ kulam //
193.d:
आराधितो यद् भगवान् अवतीर्णो गृहे मम
दुर्वृत्तनिधनार्थाय तेन नः पावितं कुलम् ॥
193.m: Since the Lord, worshipped, descended into my house / to destroy the wicked, by that our lineage has been purified.

193.s:
tvam antaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ sarvabhūteṣv avasthitaḥ
vartate ca samastātmaṃs tvatto bhūtabhaviṣyatī //
193.d:
त्वम् अन्तः सर्वभूतानां सर्वभूतेष्व् अवस्थितः
वर्तते च समस्तात्मंस् त्वत्तो भूतभविष्यती ॥
193.m: You reside within all beings; you are established in all beings. / O self of all, past and future exist from you.

193.s:
yajñe tvam ijyase 'cintya sarvadevamayācyuta
tvam eva yajño yajvā ca yajñānāṃ parameśvara //
193.d:
यज्ञे त्वम् इज्यसे ऽचिन्त्य सर्वदेवमयाच्युत
त्वम् एव यज्ञो यज्वा च यज्ञानां परमेश्वर ॥
193.m: In sacrifice you are worshipped, O unthinkable one, O Acyuta whose form is all the gods! / You alone are the sacrifice and the sacrificer, O supreme lord of sacrifices!

193.s:
sāpahnavaṃ mama mano yad etat tvayi jāyate
devakyāś cātmaja prītyā tad atyantaviḍambanā //
193.d:
सापह्नवं मम मनो यद् एतत् त्वयि जायते
देवक्याश् चात्मज प्रीत्या तद् अत्यन्तविडम्बना ॥
193.m: That this mind of mine and of Devakī should arise toward you / in deceitful affection, [thinking you our] son, is an utter mockery.

193.s:
tvaṃ kartā sarvabhūtānām anādinidhano bhavān
kva ca me mānuṣasyaiṣā jihvā putreti vakṣyati //
193.d:
त्वं कर्ता सर्वभूतानाम् अनादिनिधनो भवान्
क्व च मे मानुषस्यैषा जिह्वा पुत्रेति वक्ष्यति ॥
193.m: You are the creator of all beings, without beginning or end; / and where is this human tongue of mine, that it should say, “Son”?

193.s:
jagad etaj jagannātha saṃbhūtam akhilaṃ yataḥ
kayā yuktyā vinā māyāṃ so 'smattaḥ saṃbhaviṣyati //
193.d:
जगद् एतज् जगन्नाथ संभूतम् अखिलं यतः
कया युक्त्या विना मायां सो ऽस्मत्तः संभविष्यति ॥
193.m: From whom this entire universe has arisen, O lord of the world— / by what reason could he, without illusory power, be born from us?

193.s:
yasmin pratiṣṭhitaṃ sarvaṃ jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam
sa koṣṭhotsaṅgaśayano manuṣyāj jāyate katham //
193.d:
यस्मिन् प्रतिष्ठितं सर्वं जगत् स्थावरजङ्गमम्
स कोष्ठोत्सङ्गशयनो मनुष्याज् जायते कथम् ॥
193.m: In whom this entire world, mobile and immobile, is established, / how could he, lying in the lap of the womb, be born from a human?

193.s:
sa tvaṃ prasīda parameśvara pāhi viśvam
aṃśāvatārakaraṇair na mamāsi putraḥ
ābrahmapādapamayaṃ jagad īśa sarvaṃ
citte vimohayasi kiṃ parameśvarātman
193.d:
स त्वं प्रसीद परमेश्वर पाहि विश्वम्
अंशावतारकरणैर् न ममासि पुत्रः
आब्रह्मपादपमयं जगद् ईश सर्वं
चित्ते विमोहयसि किं परमेश्वरात्मन्
193.m: So be gracious, O supreme lord; protect the universe! / By these creations of partial descents, you are not my son. / Why, O supreme self and lord, do you delude in mind / this entire universe composed of beings from Brahmā to plants?

193.s:
māyāvimohitadṛśā tanayo mameti
kaṃsād bhayaṃ kṛtavatā tu mayātitīvram
nīto 'si gokulam arātibhayākulasya
vṛddhiṃ gato 'si mama caiva gavām adhīśa
193.d:
मायाविमोहितदृशा तनयो ममेति
कंसाद् भयं कृतवता तु मयातितीव्रम्
नीतो ऽसि गोकुलम् अरातिभयाकुलस्य
वृद्धिं गतो ऽसि मम चैव गवाम् अधीश
193.m: With eyes deluded by illusory power, thinking, “He is my son,” / and terrified of Kaṃsa, / I, distraught with fear of the enemy, brought you to Gokula; / and you, O lord of cattle, have grown there as mine.

193.s:
karmāṇi rudramarudaśviśatakratūnāṃ
sādhyāni yāni na bhavanti nirīkṣitāni
tvaṃ viṣṇur īśajagatām upakārahetoḥ
prāpto 'si naḥ parigataḥ paramo vimohaḥ
193.d:
कर्माणि रुद्रमरुदश्विशतक्रतूनां
साध्यानि यानि न भवन्ति निरीक्षितानि
त्वं विष्णुर् ईशजगताम् उपकारहेतोः
प्राप्तो ऽसि नः परिगतः परमो विमोहः
193.m: Deeds which, when contemplated, cannot be accomplished / by the Rudras, the Maruts, the Aśvins, or Indra, [are done by you]. / You are Viṣṇu, who have come for the welfare of the worlds of the Lord; / our supreme delusion has vanished.

194.s:
vyāsa uvāca
tau samutpannavijñānau bhagavatkarmadarśanāt
devakīvasudevau tu dṛṣṭvā māyāṃ punar hariḥ //
194.d:
व्यास उवाच
तौ समुत्पन्नविज्ञानौ भगवत्कर्मदर्शनात्
देवकीवसुदेवौ तु दृष्ट्वा मायां पुनर् हरिः ॥
194.m: Vyāsa said: / Seeing them both attain knowledge from witnessing the Lord’s deed, / Devakī and Vasudeva, Hari once again [cast] his illusory power;

194.s:
mohāya yaducakrasya vitatāna sa vaiṣṇavīm
uvāca cāmba bhos tāta cirād utkaṇṭhitena tu //
194.d:
मोहाय यदुचक्रस्य विततान स वैष्णवीम्
उवाच चाम्ब भोस् तात चिराद् उत्कण्ठितेन तु ॥
194.m: he spread his Vaiṣṇava illusory power to delude the host of Yadus, / and said: “O mother! O father! Having longed for you for a long time,

194.s:
bhavantau kaṃsabhītena dṛṣṭau saṃkarṣaṇena ca
kurvatāṃ yāti yaḥ kālo mātāpitror apūjanam //
194.d:
भवन्तौ कंसभीतेन दृष्टौ संकर्षणेन च
कुर्वतां याति यः कालो मातापित्रोर् अपूजनम् ॥
194.m: we two, terrified of Kaṃsa, have now seen you, along with Saṃkarṣaṇa. / The time that passes for those who do not worship their mother and father,

194.s:
sa vṛthā kleśakārī vai sādhūnām upajāyate
gurudevadvijātīnāṃ mātāpitroś ca pūjanam //
194.d:
स वृथा क्लेशकारी वै साधूनाम् उपजायते
गुरुदेवद्विजातीनां मातापित्रोश् च पूजनम् ॥
194.m: arises only to cause useless pain to virtuous people. / One who performs the worship of elders, gods, twice-born,

194.s:
kurvataḥ saphalaṃ janma dehinas tāta jāyate
tat kṣantavyam idaṃ sarvam atikramakṛtaṃ pitaḥ
kaṃsavīryapratāpābhyām āvayoḥ paravaśyayoḥ //
194.d:
कुर्वतः सफलं जन्म देहिनस् तात जायते
तत् क्षन्तव्यम् इदं सर्वम् अतिक्रमकृतं पितः
कंसवीर्यप्रतापाभ्याम् आवयोः परवश्ययोः ॥
194.m: and mother and father, O father, has an embodied life that bears fruit. / Therefore, all this transgression committed by us two, / who were under the control of another through Kaṃsa’s power and prowess, must be forgiven, O father!”

194.s:
vyāsa uvāca
ity uktvātha praṇamyobhau yaduvṛddhān anukramāt
pādānatibhiḥ sasnehaṃ cakratuḥ pauramānasam //
194.d:
व्यास उवाच
इत्य् उक्त्वाथ प्रणम्योभौ यदुवृद्धान् अनुक्रमात्
